That reported symptom is identical to the one an un-normalized cast produces — 'the projection does not simplify' — which is what makes this expensive. You re-run cast normalization, it changes nothing, and the obstacle starts to look mathematical. Rule: when a projection stalls, look at the HEAD of the term you are projecting before you look at its arguments.

The move has two halves. (1) Convert each generic head to its concrete counterpart the moment it appears, before reaching for any projection lemma. (2) Do not build the entire complex identity and extract the real part at the end. Enter the complex world at the start: rewrite the real integrand backwards through the generic-to-concrete lemma so the goal becomes the real part of a complex integral, apply the commutation lemma once, evaluate in ℂ, and come back out through the same lemma. The library proves its own real exponential integrals this way, and that direction also keeps every rewrite target unique instead of leaving several candidate subterms under an integral binder.

LEAF — the names, and what each requires.

- `RCLike.re_to_complex`, `RCLike.im_to_complex`, `RCLike.I_to_complex`, `RCLike.normSq_to_complex` in `Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean`, namespace `RCLike`. All four are `rfl` and all four are `@[simp]`. Being `rfl` is why `show Complex.re _ = _` also works where a rewrite is awkward. `normSq_to_complex` being `@[simp]` is why a bare `simp` on an `RCLike.re` goal over ℂ can land on `normSq` — prefer `simp only [RCLike.re_to_complex, …]` with your concrete lemmas listed explicitly.

- `integral_re (hf : Integrable f μ) : ∫ x, RCLike.re (f x) ∂μ = RCLike.re (∫ x, f x ∂μ)`, in `Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/ContinuousLinearMap.lean`. It requires integrability of the COMPLEX integrand, not of its real part. Siblings in the same file: `integral_im`, `integral_ofReal` and `integral_complex_ofReal` (both `@[norm_cast]`), `integral_re_add_im`, `setIntegral_re_add_im`.

- Worked template, two lines, in `Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/ImproperIntegrals.lean` (the real exponential integral over `Ioi`): `simp_rw [Real.exp, ← RCLike.re_to_complex, Complex.ofReal_mul]` to enter, then `rw [integral_re, <the complex evaluation>, RCLike.re_to_complex, RCLike.re_to_complex, Complex.div_ofReal_re, Complex.neg_re]` to leave. Read it before writing your own extraction step.

- Once the head is `Complex.re`, the pointwise real part of an oscillatory kernel closes in ONE step with `Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_re (x : ℝ) : (Complex.exp (x * Complex.I)).re = Real.cos x` (`@[simp]`; imaginary sibling `exp_ofReal_mul_I_im`, and `Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I` for the full `cos + sin * I` form). Expanding through `Complex.mul_re` and `Complex.exp_re` by hand is the slow road.

- The transform pair is defined through `innerₗ`, so unfolding the inverse transform (`Real.fourierInv_eq'`) leaves the phase carrying an inner-product pairing rather than a product even on the line. Discharge `inner ℝ x v = x * v` as its own step before expecting the phase to match anything.

6cd850620dbb47a2124c483754fa35d91a4408cc.hook: A Function.update fills a removable singularity, every hypothesis you hold is about the original function, and rw [Function.update_of_ne] will not fire inside the goal to strip the update off.
6cd850620dbb47a2124c483754fa35d91a4408cc.name: carry-a-filled-singularity-by-eventual-equality-not-by-rewriting-the-update
6cd850620dbb47a2124c483754fa35d91a4408cc.body:
PATTERN — the obstacle. You fill a removable singularity by defining the
extension `Function.update h c v`, and immediately every pointwise fact you hold
is about `h` while every goal is about the extension. Stripping the update off
inside the goal looks like the way through, and `rw [Function.update_of_ne]`
does not fire: when the function was introduced with `set`, the update term is
not syntactically present in the goal at all, and the lemma's argument shape
(`a' ≠ a`, with the filled value folded into the rewrite target) mismatches on
that value. Fighting that rewrite pointwise is a cost you pay again at each of
differentiability, continuity and analyticity.

PATTERN — the move. Never rewrite the update inside a goal. Prove ONCE that the
extension agrees with the original on a whole neighbourhood of any point other
than the filled one, then transport each property along that eventual equality.
The extension now behaves exactly like the original everywhere except at `c`,
which is the only place it was ever meant to differ, and `c` is handled
separately and once. This is the same discipline as passing to a normalized
version of a function and carrying an agreement relation forward: here the
repair is a single point value and the agreement relation is an `=ᶠ` on the
punctured neighbourhood.

LEAF (@how) — pinned Mathlib, elaborated with no `sorry`:
 * The agreement, given `hzc : z ≠ c`:
   `filter_upwards [(isOpen_compl_singleton (x := c)).mem_nhds hzc] with w hw`,
   then `show Function.update h c v w = h w`, then
   `rw [Function.update_apply, if_neg (by simpa using hw)]`
   yields `hev : Function.update h c v =ᶠ[𝓝 z] h`.
 * The transporters DISAGREE on orientation, and this is where the round-trips
   go. `DifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq : DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f x →`
   `  f₁ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] f → DifferentiableAt 𝕜 f₁ x` wants NEW =ᶠ OLD, so
   `hd.congr_of_eventuallyEq hev` applies directly. Capital `Eq`:
   `congr_of_eventually_eq` does not exist. But
   `AnalyticAt.congr : AnalyticAt 𝕜 f x → f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g → AnalyticAt 𝕜 g x`
   wants OLD =ᶠ NEW, so there you write `ha.congr hev.symm`.
   `ContinuousAt.congr` follows `AnalyticAt.congr`, not the differentiability
   one.
 * At the filled point the update is computed, not transported:
   `continuousAt_update_same : ContinuousAt (Function.update f x y) x ↔`
   `  Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] x) (𝓝 y)`.
 * The punctured-neighbourhood hypothesis a removability theorem wants is
   assembled by rewriting FIRST: `rw [eventually_nhdsWithin_iff]`, then
   `filter_upwards [hU.mem_nhds hc] with z hz hzc`, where the extra binder is
   the `z ≠ c`. Pushing an open-set membership into `𝓝[≠] c` with
   `.mono nhdsWithin_le_nhds` fails twice over: field notation does not apply
   to a membership-typed term, and the filter inequality runs the other way.
   Feed the result to
   `Complex.analyticAt_of_differentiable_on_punctured_nhds_of_continuousAt`.

a212f5e5bd291ff1b651dbd202ecc8090bc239e7.hook: bridging the non-monic divisor sum ∑ᶠ w, divisor (fun u => p.eval u) (closedBall 0 1) w from circleIntegral_logDeriv_eq_divisor_sum to (p.roots.filter (fun w => ‖w‖ < 1)).card WITHOUT q.Monic and without zeroCountInClosedBall_aeval_eq_card_filter: divisor = rootMultiplicity pointwise via exists_eq_pow_rootMultiplicity_mul_and_not_dvd + MeromorphicOn.divisor_apply + meromorphicOrderAt_eq_int_iff, then finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset over (p.roots.filter _).toFinset with Polynomial.count_roots, Multiset.count_filter_of_pos, Multiset.toFinset_sum_count_eq; cast ℤ → ℂ by (Int.castAddHom ℂ).map_finsum with finiteSupport (isCompact_closedBall 0 1); boundary nonvanishing on sphere 0 1 from the curve hypothesis via image_circleMap_Ioc
a212f5e5bd291ff1b651dbd202ecc8090bc239e7.body:
Certified close (Mathlib as pinned by apm-lean f7de6887, 2026-08-25, lean exit 0, no sorry) of the argument-principle half of a winding-number-of-a-Laurent-curve problem: from the LIB theorem ConstructionTargets.Rouche.circleIntegral_logDeriv_eq_divisor_sum to the filtered root count of a cleared polynomial p := Σ_{k<2N+1} C (a (k-N)) * X^k - C z * X^N, whose leading coefficient is arbitrary. The Monic-requiring sibling bridges (zeroCountInClosedBall_aeval_eq_card_filter) are NOT needed; monicity never enters.

(1) Apply the library theorem to f := fun u => p.eval u on C(0,1):
  apply ConstructionTargets.Rouche.circleIntegral_logDeriv_eq_divisor_sum
  · norm_num                                            -- 0 < 1
  · exact (analyticOnNhd_id.aeval_polynomial _).mono (Set.subset_univ _)
  · exact hne                                           -- ∀ w ∈ Metric.sphere 0 1, p.eval w ≠ 0
Result: ∮ w in C(0,1), logDeriv (fun u => p.eval u) w = (∑ᶠ w, (MeromorphicOn.divisor (fun u => p.eval u) (Metric.closedBall 0 1) w : ℂ)) * (2 * π * I).

(2) hne from the curve hypothesis hz : ∀ t ∈ Icc 0 (2π), γ t ≠ z: for w ∈ sphere 0 1, `have hw' : w ∈ circleMap 0 1 '' Set.Ioc 0 (2π) := by rw [image_circleMap_Ioc]; simpa using hw`, obtain ⟨t, ht, rfl⟩; circleMap 0 1 t = exp (I * t) by `simp only [circleMap, ofReal_one, one_mul, zero_add]; congr 1; ring`; so circleMap 0 1 t ≠ 0 (exp_ne_zero), rewrite p.eval with the evaluation identity p.eval w = w^N * (Laurent sum - z), and close with mul_ne_zero (pow_ne_zero _ hw0) (sub_ne_zero.mpr (hz t ⟨ht.1.le, ht.2⟩)) after rewriting the Laurent sum back to γ t. p ≠ 0 follows from hne at 1 ∈ sphere 0 1 (`by simp`).

(3) Pointwise divisor = root multiplicity, for any p ≠ 0, any U, w ∈ U:
  obtain ⟨q, hpq, hq⟩ := p.exists_eq_pow_rootMultiplicity_mul_and_not_dvd hp w   -- p = (X - C w)^m * q, ¬ (X - C w) ∣ q
  hqeval : q.eval w ≠ 0 := fun h => hq (Polynomial.dvd_iff_isRoot.mpr h)
  hpmer : MeromorphicOn (fun u => p.eval u) U := ((AnalyticOnNhd.eval_polynomial p).mono (Set.subset_univ U)).meromorphicOn
  rw [MeromorphicOn.divisor_apply hpmer hw]
  hord : meromorphicOrderAt (fun u => p.eval u) w = (m : ℤ) — (meromorphicOrderAt_eq_int_iff (AnalyticOnNhd.eval_polynomial p w (Set.mem_univ w)).meromorphicAt).mpr ⟨fun u => q.eval u, AnalyticOnNhd.eval_polynomial q w (Set.mem_univ w), hqeval, _⟩, the last component by `filter_upwards with u`, `rw [hpq, eval_mul, eval_pow, eval_sub, eval_X, eval_C]`, `simp only [smul_eq_mul, zpow_natCast]`.
  rw [hord]; simp.

(4) Finsum to card, given hne on the sphere: let s := (p.roots.filter fun w => ‖w‖ < 1).toFinset; `rw [finsum_eq_sum_of_support_subset (s := s)]`.
  Main goal: Finset.sum_congr rfl; for w ∈ s (so ‖w‖ < 1, hence w ∈ closedBall 0 1 by `simpa [Metric.mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right] using hwnorm.le`) rewrite with (3), then `rw [← Polynomial.count_roots p, Multiset.count_filter_of_pos (p := fun u => ‖u‖ < 1) (a := w) (s := p.roots) hwnorm]`; finally `rw [← Nat.cast_sum]; exact_mod_cast Multiset.toFinset_sum_count_eq (p.roots.filter fun w => ‖w‖ < 1)`.
  Support goal: from divisor ≠ 0 get w ∈ closedBall (by_contra + Function.locallyFinsuppWithin.apply_eq_zero_of_notMem _ hn), then rootMultiplicity ≠ 0 via (3), then w ∈ p.roots via Polynomial.mem_roots hp and (Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_pos hp).mp; ‖w‖ ≤ 1 upgrades to ‖w‖ < 1 by lt_of_le_of_ne, the equality case contradicting hne (w ∈ sphere by `simpa [Metric.mem_sphere, dist_zero_right] using heq`).

(5) Cast the ℤ-valued finsum to ℂ: the ℂ-finsum equals (Int.castAddHom ℂ) applied to the ℤ-finsum by `((Int.castAddHom ℂ).map_finsum ((MeromorphicOn.divisor (fun u => p.eval u) (Metric.closedBall 0 1)).finiteSupport (isCompact_closedBall 0 1))).symm`, then `rw [hsum]; norm_cast`. Net: ∮ w in C(0,1), logDeriv (fun u => p.eval u) w = ((p.roots.filter fun w => ‖w‖ < 1).card : ℂ) * (2 * π * I), ready for the parametrization bridge (see the interval-to-circle memory).

40b4dfc7e8113bedd6a08baa0619cac6ea6ee4bb.hook: Splitting a measure-theoretic integral over the line into two half-lines when the integrand is only PIECEWISE equal to the forms your evaluation lemmas want — an `|x|`, a sign, a two-sided decay. Both split lemmas (`intervalIntegral.integral_Iic_add_Ioi`, `MeasureTheory.integral_add_compl`) take ONE global function, so it is tempting to redefine the integrand as `if x ∈ Ioi 0 then … else …` so that both branches are literally present. Do not. Every downstream obligation is then stated over the `if`-form — including BOTH `IntegrableOn` hypotheses of the split — so each branch-free half-line lemma costs a `setIntegral_congr_fun` and each integrability fact an `IntegrableOn.congr_fun`, and what is left over is a bare `congr 1` that reports as a shape mismatch rather than as a mathematical gap. Split the ORIGINAL integrand and remove the branch on each piece AFTERWARDS, where the membership hypothesis is in scope and `abs_of_pos` / `abs_of_nonpos` discharge it in one rewrite; state every half-line helper lemma over that same original integrand rather than over its simplified branch. If you genuinely need a branchy global function, build it with `Set.piecewise`, not a raw `if`: `MeasureTheory.integral_piecewise` splits it in one step and takes its integrability hypotheses on the two branch-free pieces.
40b4dfc7e8113bedd6a08baa0619cac6ea6ee4bb.name: split-the-original-integrand-never-manufacture-an-if-to-fit-the-split
40b4dfc7e8113bedd6a08baa0619cac6ea6ee4bb.body:
PATTERN — the case split belongs after the split of the domain, not inside the integrand.

A kernel that is defined by a case distinction at a point — an absolute value, a sign, a one-sided decay glued at 0 — has to be integrated over the whole line, and every closed-form evaluation the library offers is for a half-line and for a branch-free integrand. The two facts collide at the split lemma, which takes a single global function. The tempting repair is to make one function that literally contains both branches, with an `if` on the splitting set. It typechecks, and it is a trap.

The cost is not one congruence, it is four. After the split, each piece integral is still stated over the branchy function, so neither half-line evaluation lemma matches; that is two congruences. But the split lemma also demands integrability of the SAME branchy function on each piece, and those hypotheses are equally unmatched; that is two more. Every one of them is a restatement of the same trivial pointwise fact, and the leftover obligation surfaces as a bare congruence step that reports a shape difference, so it reads as though something mathematical is still missing when nothing is.

The move: split the integrand you already have, and eliminate the branch on each PIECE, where the membership hypothesis is in scope and one rewrite kills it. Equivalently, and better, decide the shape before proving anything: state each half-line helper lemma over the ORIGINAL global integrand restricted to that piece, not over its branch-free simplification. Then the split composes with a plain rewrite and there is no congruence at all. The asymmetric case is the diagnostic — if one of your two half-line lemmas mentions the case split and the other does not, you have already made this mistake and the mismatch will surface at assembly.

A branchy global function is sometimes genuinely what you want. Then use the library's own branchy constructor rather than a raw conditional, because only the former carries restriction API.

LEAF — the names, and what each requires.

- `intervalIntegral.integral_Iic_add_Ioi (h_left : IntegrableOn f (Iic b) μ) (h_right : IntegrableOn f (Ioi b) μ)`. Note both hypotheses are about the SAME `f` — this is where a branchy `f` charges you twice.
- `MeasureTheory.integral_add_compl (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hfi : Integrable f μ) : ∫ x in s, f + ∫ x in sᶜ, f = ∫ x, f`. Usually the better split for a decaying kernel: one GLOBAL integrability fact instead of two restricted ones, and you generally have to prove global integrability anyway for the inversion or domination step downstream. It hands you `sᶜ`, so pair it with `Set.compl_Iic : (Iic a)ᶜ = Ioi a` (and `Set.Iic_union_Ioi : Iic a ∪ Ioi a = univ` with `integrableOn_univ` if you assembled integrability from the two pieces instead).
- Removing the branch on a piece: `MeasureTheory.setIntegral_congr_fun (hs : MeasurableSet s) (h : EqOn f g s)` for the integral, and `MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn.congr_fun (h : IntegrableOn f s μ) (hst : EqOn f g s) (hs : MeasurableSet s)` for the integrability — note the argument ORDER differs between the two (`EqOn` last vs `EqOn` first), which is a real source of lost cycles. The iff form is `integrableOn_congr_fun`.
- If you do need a branchy global function: `Set.piecewise`, whose branch lemmas `Set.piecewise_eq_of_mem` and `Set.piecewise_eq_of_notMem` are both `@[simp]` (note the recent capital-M spelling of the second), and `MeasureTheory.integral_piecewise (hs : MeasurableSet s) (hf : IntegrableOn f s μ) (hg : IntegrableOn g sᶜ μ) : ∫ x, s.piecewise f g x ∂μ = ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ + ∫ x in sᶜ, g x ∂μ`. Its integrability hypotheses are on the two BRANCH-FREE functions, which is exactly the saving; `MeasureTheory.Integrable.piecewise` gives the global fact. A raw `if` has none of this.

f51c5ee41c7222e8c002bed6164097e972f24695.hook: The remaining step is that the Maclaurin coefficients tend to zero for a function analytic on a disc of radius strictly larger than the radius in question, and the plan routes through a Cauchy estimate on a larger sphere with a compact thickening and a geometric squeeze.
f51c5ee41c7222e8c002bed6164097e972f24695.name: coefficient-decay-by-summing-at-the-target-modulus
f51c5ee41c7222e8c002bed6164097e972f24695.body:
PATTERN — the obstacle. The remaining goal is decay of Maclaurin coefficients:
`c n → 0`, or `‖c n‖ * r ^ n` bounded/summable. The function is analytic on a
disc of radius strictly larger than the radius `r` you care about, and the plan
that suggests itself is Cauchy's estimate — thicken the compact disc to a
strictly larger one, bound the function on the larger sphere by compactness,
divide by `R ^ n`, squeeze with a geometric sequence. That chain is correct, and
it is five steps each with its own hypothesis shape, and it is where time-boxed
attempts die with the boundary still open.

PATTERN — the move. Do not estimate the coefficients; SUM them. A power series
converges at every point strictly inside its disc of convergence, and the terms
of a convergent series tend to zero. So if the point of modulus `r` lies inside
the region where the function is analytic, evaluate the expansion at ONE such
point: the resulting `HasSum` already says the coefficients times `r ^ n` are
summable, hence null. With `r = 1` and the point `1`, "the coefficients tend to
zero" becomes "the series converges at 1", and the whole thickening/sphere/
squeeze chain disappears. Worth holding in general: before estimating decay of
`c n * r ^ n`, ask whether some point of modulus `r` is interior to the domain
of analyticity. If it is, one evaluation beats every estimate — and a pole
exactly on `|z| = r` is not an obstruction if the function you expanded is the
pole-subtracted one, since that is precisely why its disc got bigger.

LEAF (@how) — pinned Mathlib, elaborated with no `sorry`:
 * `HasFPowerSeriesOnBall.hasSum : HasFPowerSeriesOnBall f p x R →`
   `  y ∈ Metric.eball 0 (R : ℝ≥0∞) → HasSum (fun n => p n fun _ => y) (f (x + y))`
   The membership is in the EXTENDED-metric ball at an `ℝ≥0∞` radius, not in
   `Metric.ball`. Spelling trap: `EMetric.ball` is a deprecated alias and
   `rw [Metric.eball_coe]` will NOT fire on a goal stated with it ("did not find
   an occurrence of the pattern eball ?x ↑?r"). State the membership with
   `Metric.eball`, then `rw [Metric.eball_coe]` (`eball x ↑r = ball x r`; the
   pre-rename name was `Metric.emetric_ball_nnreal`), then
   `simp only [mem_ball, dist_zero_right, norm_one]` and `norm_num`.
 * `simpa [FormalMultilinearSeries.ofScalars] using h` collapses
   `ofScalars 𝕜 c n (fun _ => y)` to the scalar term; at `y = 1` that is `c n`.
   Take `.summable` FIRST and simp the `Summable` statement rather than the
   `HasSum` one: `HasSum` also mentions the sum's VALUE, which here is the
   opaque updated-function term, and stating it forces a placeholder Lean
   cannot synthesise ("don't know how to synthesize placeholder for argument").
 * `Summable.tendsto_atTop_zero : Summable f → Tendsto f atTop (𝓝 0)` finishes.

Assembled, from a ball expansion `hb` already stated in your own coefficients:
   have hs : Summable c := by
     simpa [FormalMultilinearSeries.ofScalars] using (hb.hasSum hmem).summable
   exact hs.tendsto_atTop_zero

2ad8e97a50d62672364fca891c5f8d70a60f3a13.hook: you put the integrand into a continuous normal form and then noticed the summands are each ~1/x and NOT in L¹, so `Integrable rep volume` looks unreachable and you retreat to the raw quotient for the integrability half — that retreat is the trap. You never need integrability of a summand: the slowly decaying terms cancel in the sum by construction. Bound the ASSEMBLED function, `‖rep x‖ ≤ C * ‖(1 + x ^ 2)⁻¹‖` on two half-lines, and hand the compact middle to `LocallyIntegrable`; `Continuous.locallyIntegrable.integrable_of_isBigO_atBot_atTop` with `Asymptotics.isBigO_iff` witnesses and `integrable_inv_one_add_sq.integrableAtFilter` asks for exactly that and for nothing about the pieces
2ad8e97a50d62672364fca891c5f8d70a60f3a13.name: integrability-of-a-sum-whose-summands-are-not-integrable
2ad8e97a50d62672364fca891c5f8d70a60f3a13.body:
PATTERN — a non-sequitur that can cost the whole attempt.

Having rewritten an integrand into a continuous normal form as a *sum* — a difference of sinc terms, of logarithms, of partial fractions — it is tempting to check the pieces for integrability, find that each decays only like 1/x, and conclude the normal form is useless for the integrability obligation. That inference is invalid. The decomposition was chosen precisely because the slowly decaying leading terms cancel in the sum, so the sum decays one order better than any summand. Nothing in the integrability API asks about summands; there is no obligation to discharge for them.

The retreat this triggers is worse than the delay. Going back to the raw quotient to prove `Integrable` puts the removable points back into the estimate: the denominator's sign is no longer decided, `abs` has to be pushed through a product of linear factors, and the case analysis reappears that the normal form existed to remove. You end up with two estimates instead of one, on the harder of the two functions.

THE MOVE. Prove integrability of the assembled representative, and only of the representative. Bound it against a fixed integrable profile on the two tails and let local integrability cover the compact middle for free. The a.e. equality you already have transports `Integrable` back to the original function at the end.

LEAF — the spellings.
* `Continuous.locallyIntegrable.integrable_of_isBigO_atBot_atTop (g := fun x : ℝ => (1 + x ^ 2)⁻¹) (g' := fun x : ℝ => (1 + x ^ 2)⁻¹)` leaves four goals in this order: an `atBot` big-O witness, integrability of the profile at `atBot`, an `atTop` big-O witness, integrability of the profile at `atTop`.
* Each big-O witness is `Asymptotics.isBigO_iff.mpr ⟨C, _⟩` followed by `filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_le_atBot (-T : ℝ)]` (respectively `Filter.eventually_ge_atTop (T : ℝ)`) `with x hx`; the goal is then the plain pointwise norm bound `‖rep x‖ ≤ C * ‖(1 + x ^ 2)⁻¹‖`.
* The reference profile is `integrable_inv_one_add_sq.integrableAtFilter _`, usable unchanged on both sides.
* `Real.continuous_sinc` plus `fun_prop` (after `unfold`) supplies the `Continuous` hypothesis for a finite combination of sinc terms at affine arguments.
* Transport back at the end with `Integrable.congr` on the a.e. equality; the value half uses `MeasureTheory.integral_congr_ae`.
* A saving that is easy to miss: on the tail it is legitimate to rewrite the representative *back* into quotient form and estimate there, because both linear factors are nonzero on that region. The removable points are not in the tail, so that rewrite carries no side condition beyond the tail hypothesis itself.

MINED FROM. A Student reached the sinc normal form, observed correctly that neither sinc term is in L¹ of the line, concluded from that the normal form could not serve the integrability half, and spent the rest of its attempt on a global bound for the raw quotient that turned out to be false on part of its range.

db3d4bf1fe749c7e6802b243a6a79784f6991c3d.hook: Refuting an index-two subgroup via normality, commutator containment, and a Lagrange divisibility contradiction.
db3d4bf1fe749c7e6802b243a6a79784f6991c3d.name: index-two-subgroup-refuted-via-commutator-containment
db3d4bf1fe749c7e6802b243a6a79784f6991c3d.body: PATTERN — the obstacle. Refuting 'G has a subgroup of index two' by enumeration or by a squares-of-generators argument: enumeration is infeasible and the square route is false as usually phrased (an odd-order element g satisfies g = (g^((n+1)/2))^2 only with an order-dependent exponent; g = (g^2)^2 holds only for order three). The compiled route uses the commutator subgroup instead. PATTERN — the move. An index-2 subgroup is normal; the quotient has order 2, hence is commutative, so the commutator subgroup of G lies in H; identify the commutator with an explicit small subgroup (or show the needed small subgroup ≤ commutator), then contradict Lagrange: the small subgroup's card does not divide card H. LEAF — spellings (pinned Mathlib, compiled in the source artifact). Subgroup.card_mul_index and Subgroup.index_eq_card turn card H = half card G into H.index = 2; Subgroup.normal_of_index_eq_two (hH : H.index = 2) : H.Normal; quotient card 2 gives commutativity via isCyclic_of_prime_card + .commutative; Subgroup.Normal.quotient_commutative_iff_commutator_le upgrades it to commutator G ≤ H; for alternating groups on four letters alternatingGroup.kleinFour_eq_commutator (requires card = 4 by norm_num) and alternatingGroup.kleinFour_card_of_card_eq_four give a cardinality that cannot divide 6, closed by omega. MINED FROM a residual where a no-subgroup-of-order-six conjunct stayed sorry and the standard index-2 argument was not attempted within budget; an earlier square-generator deposit on the same obstacle was rejected as mathematically inaccurate. No problem identifiers are needed to apply this.

9914e00532f59a06e7198c79726d4960df82c786.hook: An informal plan routes through a period-shift rectangular contour with an interior pole, but the formalization target is a real principal-value limit: budget the contour route against what the library actually packages before committing to it.
9914e00532f59a06e7198c79726d4960df82c786.name: contour-absence-departure-real-axis-series
9914e00532f59a06e7198c79726d4960df82c786.body: Departure from the file's proposed route. At the working revision the library exposes Cauchy-Goursat for functions differentiable on a closed rectangle (integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_differentiableOn) but no packaged residue theorem for a rectangle with an interior pole, and a circle-integral residue lemma does not discharge the period-shift argument. The certified proof abandons the contour: on the real axis the pole-free paired integrand expands as the difference of two exponentially decaying geometric families; integrate each family termwise on the half-line, reindex the finite partial sums, and identify the reciprocal-difference series with the library's cotangent partial-sum limit (tendsto_logDeriv_euler_cot_sub, cot_series_rep'), splitting off the unmatched reflected endpoint which tends to zero. Reusable fact: the contour route is a dependency gap, not a mathematical necessity, and the real-axis series route closes the same goal with standard API.

769ca4f627eff23772fddae36069983005d47e1d.hook: Proving Tendsto (fun n => integral of test function f against oscillatory family g_n) to 0 where g_n has no a.e. pointwise limit, so dominated or Vitali convergence and tendsto_Lp_of_tendsto_ae are unavailable.
769ca4f627eff23772fddae36069983005d47e1d.name: oscillatory-weak-null-by-dense-class-plus-uniform-bound
769ca4f627eff23772fddae36069983005d47e1d.body: Trigger: goal Tendsto (fun n => ∫ f * gₙ) atTop (nhds 0) for arbitrary L¹/L∞ f against oscillatory gₙ (alternating dyadic signs, characters, oscillating indicators). Move: (1) prove exact cancellation ∫ s * gₙ = 0 on a dense class of step functions s — for alternating dyadic signs each coarse level-m cell refines into paired equal-measure odd/even level-n subcells whose contributions cancel exactly once n exceeds both m and the family's lowest exceptional level; (2) prove the uniform bound ‖∫ h * gₙ‖ ≤ ∫ |h| from |gₙ| ≤ 1 via norm_integral_le_integral_norm plus integral_congr_ae; (3) approximate f in L¹ by a step function s and split ∫ f·gₙ = ∫ (f−s)·gₙ by integral_sub with the cancellation ∫ s·gₙ = 0, then bound with the uniform bound and the ε/2+ε/2 budget, taking the tail index as max (level of s + 1) (lowest exceptional level of the family). Reason it works: convergence needs checking only on the dense class, and the uniform bound is exactly what legalizes extension to arbitrary f. Do the cellwise cancellation directly rather than bundling into an orthogonality/inner-product argument: proving orthogonality separately would require the same cellwise cancellation, so skip the bundling. Rewrite as Metric.tendsto_atTop: for each ε pick the level from density, then every larger n is handled uniformly.

fb9a9bb3de77abe3e07d8927373ff2305f06f7d0.hook: When a reciprocal logarithmic majorant must be integrated near an endpoint and a direct change-of-variables theorem assumes the transformed integrability that is still missing.
fb9a9bb3de77abe3e07d8927373ff2305f06f7d0.name: prove logarithmic-tail integrability through an antiderivative before substitution
fb9a9bb3de77abe3e07d8927373ff2305f06f7d0.body: First prove integrability of 1 / (x * (log x)^2) on a tail by recognizing it as the nonnegative derivative of -(log x)^(-1), using integrableOn_Ioi_deriv_of_nonneg' and the limit (log x)^(-1) -> 0. Then transport that established tail integrability through integrableOn_image_iff_integrableOn_abs_deriv_smul for the reciprocal parametrization. This ordering avoids the circular obligation created by substitution lemmas that require integrability on both sides.

5774393888c9b7eb312b89e48aabe131f604265d.hook: A finite Galois extension contains an element, and the normal closure of its generated intermediate field must be identified with the field generated by all roots of its minimal polynomial, but no packaged equality is available.
5774393888c9b7eb312b89e48aabe131f604265d.name: identify-simple-normal-closure-by-root-set-membership
5774393888c9b7eb312b89e48aabe131f604265d.body: Let R be the intermediate field adjoined by the root set. The ambient splitting theorem gives the minimal polynomial split over R, so `Normal.of_isSplittingField` makes R normal; the universal property `IntermediateField.normalClosure_le_iff_of_normal` then proves the normal closure is at most R after checking the original element is a root. For the reverse inclusion, regard the element as a member of its normal closure, use normality there to obtain splitting of its minimal polynomial, transport that minimal polynomial along the inclusion with `minpoly.algHom_eq`, and apply `IntermediateField.splits_iff_mem` to show every ambient root belongs to the normal closure. This avoids extending embeddings or enumerating conjugates.

57b76f67986495c6f597fb3eb5404892ec4c53a2.hook: A weak Fourier identity quantifies only over real-valued or conjugate-symmetric test vectors, but the target is a pointwise complex multiplier equation at each nonzero frequency.
57b76f67986495c6f597fb3eb5404892ec4c53a2.name: Recover complex Fourier coefficients with conjugate-symmetric paired probes
57b76f67986495c6f597fb3eb5404892ec4c53a2.body: Use a two-frequency test vector supported at k and -k, with coefficients q and star q, so it remains conjugate-symmetric. Apply the weak identity twice, first with q = 1 and then with q = Complex.I. Symmetry of the unknown and forcing makes the paired contributions duplicate the real and imaginary components respectively; simplify each scalar equality, then reconstruct the complex multiplier equation with Complex.ext. This avoids the invalid move of testing with a single complex Fourier basis vector, which need not lie in the real test subspace. In Mathlib, lp.single builds the probes, tsum_eq_sum reduces each infinite sum to the two-point Finset, and Complex.ext closes from the recovered components.

4c16635ff73eabf9cb59b48cb57b38a6f59a677e.hook: when native_decide or fin_cases decide fails on Equiv.Perm.IsThreeCycle / IsCycle / pointwise cycle-step goals for a concrete finite permutation
4c16635ff73eabf9cb59b48cb57b38a6f59a677e.name: cycle-predicate-decide-via-quantified-statement
4c16635ff73eabf9cb59b48cb57b38a6f59a677e.body: IsThreeCycle and IsCycle synthesize no Decidable instance, so native_decide fails with 'failed to synthesize Decidable'; fin_cases x <;> native_decide on a pointwise statement fails with 'Expected type must not contain free variables' because the Fin subtype property stays a metavariable. Move: (a) prove 3-cycles via card_support_eq_three_iff.mp (by native_decide) — the iff is root-namespace; (b) state orbit/cycle-step facts as a standalone top-level quantified proposition and close with plain decide — the quantified form decides cleanly while the binder-context form does not; (c) build IsCycle from an explicit witness whose SameCycle side is that quantified decidable statement. Note Subgroup.closure has no computable Decidable instance even on a finite group — do not brute-force closure equalities.

b5dee01e5ccff96f20398182208a8d6dccde68be.hook: Two continuous functionals agree on all derivatives of compactly supported smooth functions, and one must identify their difference explicitly.
b5dee01e5ccff96f20398182208a8d6dccde68be.name: kernel functional from projection onto derivatives
b5dee01e5ccff96f20398182208a8d6dccde68be.body: With a unit-integral test function rho, decompose phi as Q phi + (integral phi) • rho, where Q phi has integral zero. Construct a compactly supported smooth primitive of Q phi, so any functional annihilating test-function derivatives vanishes on Q phi. Linearity then gives w(phi) = w(rho) * integral(phi). This avoids quotient-space machinery: the normalized rank-one projection supplies both the kernel description and the scalar coefficient. Mined from the residual asking for uniqueness of distributional primitives up to a constant distribution.

bbe60d28c42ddf0cf35dac05bb00d9117d2ec667.hook: A pointwise family HasSum (fun n => a n * z ^ n) (f z) holds on a ball and the plan treats converting it into HasFPowerSeriesAt (ofScalars a) 0 — including any radius bound — as an unsolved bridge needing a HasFPowerSeriesOnBall construction or a cross-frame import.
bbe60d28c42ddf0cf35dac05bb00d9117d2ec667.name: hassum-to-hasfpowerseriesat-conversion-is-one-rewrite
bbe60d28c42ddf0cf35dac05bb00d9117d2ec667.body: Rewrite rule. scope: packaging coefficient sequences into FormalMultilinearSeries machinery in Lean/Mathlib. before: plan a bespoke construction of HasFPowerSeriesOnBall (with explicit radius bookkeeping) or import a frame-local compiled bridge before coefficient identification can start. after: rw [hasFPowerSeriesAt_iff] — the definition is already the filter statement (fun x => HasSum (fun n => (s n).smulRightApply 1 x) (f x)) eventually in nhds of the point — then filter_upwards [Metric.ball_mem_nhds of_centre zero_lt_one] and simpa [FormalMultilinearSeries.coeff_ofScalars, mul_comm] on the given pointwise family. The radius data is already carried by the ball in the hypothesis; no separate radius lemma is needed. level: domain (complex analysis / power series formalization). confidence: high — machine-checked in the certified head of the mined solve (git commit 143e17dd25b60d09f1546f669d097f462490d073). evidence-ids: [base-file boundary comment claiming the conversion remains the open bridge, certified head commit 143e17dd25b60d09f1546f669d097f462490d073].

4b9f6da6d4722f23d465cbc879b926b3ff3f7510.hook: A lintegral or measure argument needs the set where f vanishes, and MeasurableSet on that level set cannot be obtained from an integrability hypothesis.
4b9f6da6d4722f23d465cbc879b926b3ff3f7510.name: level-sets-of-an-almost-everywhere-measurable-function-are-not-measurable-so-never-quantify-the-bad-set
4b9f6da6d4722f23d465cbc879b926b3ff3f7510.body:
PATTERN - the obstacle. From Integrable f mu, or from any merely almost-everywhere measurable hypothesis, the LEVEL SETS of f are not measurable. The set where f vanishes, the set where it passes a threshold, the set where a case-split integrand takes its exceptional value: none of them carry MeasurableSet. That blocks a whole family of routes at once, and they are the routes a seat reaches for first - bound a lintegral below by the indicator of the bad set, compute the restricted measure of it, show it is null and push through by monotonicity. The failure surfaces as an instance-synthesis failure on MeasurableSet, deep inside a route already invested in, and it does not suggest its own fix. Two independent attempts on the same statement both spent their opening moves here.

PATTERN - the move. Do not quantify the bad set. Obtain the statement you want as an almost-everywhere fact directly, so that no set is ever named. Finiteness of an extended-nonnegative lintegral yields almost-everywhere finiteness of the integrand in ONE step; if the integrand was built to take its exceptional value exactly on the bad set, that finiteness IS the almost-everywhere statement excluding it, and the set never enters the proof. Where you genuinely need a measurable version of the set, take it for the canonical measurable REPRESENTATIVE rather than for f: the representative's level sets are measurable, it agrees with f almost everywhere, and almost-everywhere agreement is all any measure-theoretic conclusion downstream actually consumed.

LEAF - which lemmas demand the set and which do not (elaborated against the pinned Mathlib).
- Demand MeasurableSet, hence blocked: Measurable.ite wants MeasurableSet of the branch predicate's set; lintegral_indicator wants MeasurableSet of the set; Measure.restrict_apply wants MeasurableSet of the set being measured.
- Demands it indirectly, and is the long way round: measure_eq_top_of_setLIntegral_ne_top : AEMeasurable f (mu.restrict s) -> (lintegral of f over s) <> top -> mu {x | x in s and f x = top} = 0. It still needs the same almost-everywhere-measurability packaging as the short route, and then leaves measure_mono_null bookkeeping to get from that set to the one you care about.
- Demands no set at all, and is the short route: ae_lt_top' : AEMeasurable f mu -> (lintegral of f) <> top -> for almost every x, f x < top. One step, landing already in the almost-everywhere layer.
- The representative escape hatch: for the measurable representative g, the preimage of a singleton under g is a MeasurableSet - built as the singleton's measurability composed with g's - and that is exactly the argument Measurable.ite is asking for. You never obtain the corresponding fact for f, and you never need it.

abcc439d7d8cd918667da5a51216eb3bf3279d09.hook: compose Mathlib's packaged 𝓓 operators (fderivCLM/postcompCLM/monoCLM/limitCLM) before hand-rolling LF seminorm estimates; Distribution is a UniformConvergenceCLM type synonym
abcc439d7d8cd918667da5a51216eb3bf3279d09.name: testfunction-clm-toolbox-compose-before-seminorm-estimates
abcc439d7d8cd918667da5a51216eb3bf3279d09.body: PATTERN — Before hand-rolling seminorm estimates to build a continuous linear operator on the test-function space 𝓓, compose the already-packaged CLMs in Mathlib/Analysis/Distribution: `TestFunction.fderivCLM` (derivative), `TestFunction.postcompCLM` (postcompose values by a CLM T, `postcompCLM_apply : postcompCLM T f = T ∘ f`), `TestFunction.monoCLM` (continuous inclusion when order decreases / domain opens), `TestFunction.limitCLM` (the general stage-wise LF constructor: supply Φ : 𝓓 → V and continuity of ofSupportedInCLM ∘L Φ on each 𝓓_K). A derivative-on-test-functions operator is literally `(ContinuousLinearMap.apply ℝ ℝ (1:ℝ)) ∘L TestFunction.fderivCLM ℝ ⊤ ⊤`. Only when no composition of these yields the operator (e.g. an integration/antidifferentiation operator, whose target support varies with the input) does the multi-hour stagewise seminorm construction become necessary — schedule it as its own session, not a cold 30-minute attempt. LEAF facts (verified against this Mathlib checkout): (1) Distribution abbreviates 𝓓(Ω,ℝ) →L_c[ℝ] F = CompactConvergenceCLM = UniformConvergenceCLM, a type SYNONYM: generic CLM simp lemmas like `ContinuousLinearMap.sub_apply` do NOT match — use the namespaced `UniformConvergenceCLM.sub_apply` and siblings. (2) Bundled TestFunction arithmetic is not defeq pointwise: `(φ - k•ρ + k•ρ) a` needs `TestFunction.coe_add`, `coe_sub`, `coe_smul` (namespaced). (3) `TestFunction.coe_injective` does not exist; the ext lemma is `TestFunction.ext (∀ a, f a = g a)`. (4) A canonical unit-integral test function is `ContDiffBump.normed volume` with `contDiff_normed`, `integral_normed (∫ = 1)`, `support_normed_eq (ball)`, `tsupport_normed_eq (closedBall)`; ContDiffBump has no `one` constructor — build `⟨1, 2, one_pos, by norm_num⟩ : ContDiffBump (0:ℝ)`. (5) `ContDiff.differentiable` in this snapshot wants `n ≠ 0` on WithTop ℕ∞ — pass `one_ne_zero`. (6) `ContinuousLinearMap.apply` takes the field and module explicitly: `apply ℝ ℝ (1:ℝ)`. Provenance (mined-from): f207 student-attempt-2 residual — part (b) open on assembling a normalized primitive operator P; part (c) closed via the transpose route plus these lemmas; also corrects the stale 'no derivative operator' leaf of the intervention-1 deposit (TestFunction.fderivCLM exists, with `fderivCLM_apply : fderivCLM 𝕜 n k f = if k + 1 ≤ n then fderiv ℝ f else 0`).

634c906c1cd0acadbee3bc6cb057227453435e92.hook: HasDerivAt congr wrappers fail on simp-normalized integrand shapes — state the derivative identity in simp's own normal form
634c906c1cd0acadbee3bc6cb057227453435e92.name: restate-hasderivat-in-simp-normal-form-instead-of-congr-wrappers
634c906c1cd0acadbee3bc6cb057227453435e92.body: When evaluating an integral by FTC via intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt / integral_Ioi_of_hasDerivAt_of_tendsto', the HasDerivAt hypothesis must match the goal function up to syntactic equality; simp's normal form inserts id-lambdas and *1/*-1 factors (fun x => Real.exp ((-fun y => id y + x) x)), and ring, congr 1, or simp only [id_eq] do not erase them post-hoc. Do not fight the wrapper lemmas (HasDerivAt.congr, .congr_deriv, .congr_of_eventuallyEq) on the raw expression. Instead: (1) let simp show you its own normal form of the integrand, (2) state a standalone have : HasDerivAt <normalized shape> <derivative> x and prove THAT with HasDerivAt combinators matching the normal form (Real.deriv_exp, .comp, .add, .const_mul), then (3) discharge the congr step by Filter.EventuallyEq via funext-style rewriting or by integral_congr_ae / setIntegral_congr_fun at the integral level, bypassing the pointwise congr wrapper entirely. Symptoms of the trap: coercion/cast-mismatch errors after push_cast, or ring leaving goals containing id; this same normal-form blockage also stalls the final field_simp/ring on the summed pieces.

36780c82d51ded034b76dedf868e1526584a0bea.hook: A finite commutative group needs a subgroup of prime index (or a maximal/quotient-of-order-p subgroup) and searches for `Subgroup.IsMaximal`, character theory, or a packaged prime-index extraction return nothing.
36780c82d51ded034b76dedf868e1526584a0bea.name: prime-index-subgroup-of-finite-abelian-via-cyclic-coordinates
36780c82d51ded034b76dedf868e1526584a0bea.body: PATTERN — why subgroup-existence conclusions stall in finite abelian groups. Mathlib has NO Subgroup.IsMaximal for subgroups (IsMaximal exists only for ideals) and no theorem converting p ∣ Nat.card A for a finite commutative group into ∃ M : Subgroup A, M.index = p. Searching maximal subgroups, characters, or quotient correspondence for a packaged route wastes the budget. The move that works: expose cyclic coordinates through a decomposition equivalence, select one coordinate whose modulus p divides, and take the kernel of the coordinate projection. LEAF — spellings. The endomorphism x ↦ x ^ p is `powMonoidHom (A := A) p`: the group argument is IMPLICIT (bare `powMonoidHom A p` fails with an ℕ type mismatch) and an anonymous constructor ⟨fun x => x^p, …⟩ for `A →* A` is rejected because the expected type is a structure — use `powMonoidHom`. Cauchy-type existence: `exists_prime_orderOf_eq` does NOT exist; only backward forms `orderOf_eq_prime` / `orderOf_eq_prime_iff` (element in hand → order p), so element existence must come from `IsPGroup` API or the decomposition. Full index-p route: `CommGroup.equiv_prod_multiplicative_zmod_of_finite` rewrites the cardinality as a finite product; `Prime.dvd_finset_prod_iff` picks the coordinate; compose with `Pi.evalMonoidHom` and `ZMod.castHom`, prove surjectivity from `Function.surjective_eval` + `ZMod.castHom_surjective`; conclude with `Subgroup.index_ker` and `MonoidHom.range_eq_top`; pull back along any surjective quotient map with `Subgroup.index_comap_of_surjective`. MINED FROM a Student attempt on a normal-subgroup/Sylow problem that spent its 30-minute budget confirming the API absence and debugging powMonoidHom spellings with the index-p conjunct open. No problem-specific identifiers are needed to apply this pattern.

d5af56197b3ba775f22e0a57fa065a945dd31ded.hook: A theorem requests a linear map on all functions, but the integral formula is only known to be integrable for functions satisfying linearity-stable regularity and support predicates.
d5af56197b3ba775f22e0a57fa065a945dd31ded.name: build-an-integral-functional-on-a-test-function-submodule-before-extending
d5af56197b3ba775f22e0a57fa065a945dd31ded.body: Package the admissible functions as a Submodule by proving zero, addition, and scalar closure. Define the integral formula as a LinearMap on that submodule, proving map_add and map_smul with integral_add and integral_smul under the available integrability hypotheses. Then use LinearMap.exists_extend to obtain a linear map on the ambient function space and recover the formula on admissible functions with DFunLike.congr_fun. The extension is algebraic; continuity estimates can be proved separately only on the constrained inputs where they are needed.

4527915f248d89325bc57bc4300d4c8550f321d1.hook: A compiled sibling artifact already proves the exact auxiliary estimate needed, but it lives behind a frame-local import and its hypotheses name frame-local definitions that would have to be rebuilt anyway.
4527915f248d89325bc57bc4300d4c8550f321d1.name: self-contained-cauchy-estimate-beats-cross-frame-lemma-import
4527915f248d89325bc57bc4300d4c8550f321d1.body: Process/cost memory. The base plan routed the coefficient-decay step through a previously compiled frame-local lemma (Cauchy-decay estimate from an earlier problem) via import. The solver instead re-derived the estimate in about 15 lines directly from Mathlib primitives: compact thickening to a strictly larger ball, DiffContOnCl upgrade, Complex.norm_iteratedDeriv_le_of_forall_mem_sphere_norm_le on the larger sphere, geometric decay, squeeze. Cost lesson: when the sibling lemma's statement must be re-hypothesized on new definitions, the import route costs more than re-derivation from Mathlib, and the re-derived version has no cross-frame dependency that can rot. Prefer Mathlib-grounded re-derivation whenever the reusable content is a standard estimate rather than a genuinely new theorem.

4adf5e169080d8389d76342961d99f3f2f89208e.hook: when simultaneously diagonalizing commuting diagonalizable matrices over an algebraically closed field, or building a common eigenbasis from an eigenspace decomposition
4adf5e169080d8389d76342961d99f3f2f89208e.name: commuting-semisimple-family-common-eigenbasis-recipe
4adf5e169080d8389d76342961d99f3f2f89208e.body: PATTERN (linear algebra over an algebraically closed field). To simultaneously diagonalize a commuting family of individually diagonalizable matrices, do NOT build a dimension induction by hand. Transport each matrix to Module.End via Matrix.toLin', prove each is semisimple (Module.End.isSemisimple_of_squarefree_aeval_eq_zero after conjugating to a diagonal, transported along LinearEquiv.isSemisimple_iff with the conjugation intertwining equation), then use Mathlib's commuting-family decomposition machinery and reassemble a conjugating matrix via Basis.toMatrix. LEAF (exact spelling, Mathlib around v4.29). Module.End.iSup_iInf_maxGenEigenspace_eq_top_of_iSup_maxGenEigenspace_eq_top_of_commute gives the supremum over characters of the infimum of maxGenEigenspaces equal to top, from Pairwise Commute plus Module.End.iSup_maxGenEigenspace_eq_top. Module.End.independent_iInf_maxGenEigenspace_of_forall_mapsTo gives iSupIndep via Module.End.mapsTo_maxGenEigenspace_of_comm. Collapse generalized to ordinary eigenspaces with ((Module.End.isFinitelySemisimple_iff_isSemisimple).mpr hsemi).maxGenEigenspace_eq_eigenspace under simpa only. Assemble the common eigenbasis. Module.Free.chooseBasis of each infimum-eigenspace, DFinsupp.basis over the sigma index, then .map (hind.linearEquiv htop); reindex via Cardinal.eq on mk_eq_rank''. T is b.toMatrix std with invertibility from Module.Basis.invertibleToMatrix b std and the inverse given by std.toMatrix b; the identity T mul M mul T inverse equals LinearMap.toMatrix b b M.toLin' (via LinearMap.toMatrix_comp rewrites) converts the eigenbasis law f i (b j) = chi j i smul b j directly into Matrix.IsDiag of both conjugates.

34cc68ee55d882e5192fe387450c8c97f02a486e.hook: The integrand is a cell indicator times a signed function that is constant (±1, or any c) on that half-open cell Ico a b, the measure is a restriction such as volume.restrict (Icc 0 1), and the integral must come out as the constant times the cell length; the indicator, the restricted measure, and the ENNReal-to-real conversion of the cell's measure block the evaluation.
34cc68ee55d882e5192fe387450c8c97f02a486e.name: integrate-a-cellwise-constant-signed-function-under-a-restricted-lebesgue-measure
34cc68ee55d882e5192fe387450c8c97f02a486e.body:
PATTERN — the obstacle. After a refinement, each fine cell contributes ∫ (indicator of the cell) · g with g constant on that cell, and the value is c · (b − a). Three layers sit between the goal and that number: the indicator (the goal is a Bochner integral of indicator s 1 * g, not a set integral), the restriction ((volume.restrict I) (Ico a b) is volume (Ico a b ∩ I), not volume (Ico a b)), and the ENNReal-valued measure (Measure.real, or .toReal of an ENNReal.ofReal). Each layer is one rewrite; a search for a single lemma that does all three finds nothing, and trying to simp through all of them at once leaves cast and nonnegativity side goals.

PATTERN — the move. Peel the layers in order, and do it once as a lemma quantified over the cell index with the constant left symbolic (if Odd k then 1 else -1, or a general c), so the sign enters only the finite sum afterwards. (1) Replace the integrand by the indicator of the constant: funext, by_cases on membership, the cell-constancy fact inside the cell, simp outside (or fold indicator s 1 * g into indicator s g with Set.indicator_mul_left). (2) Turn the indicator into a set integral and evaluate the constant. (3) Evaluate the restricted measure of the cell: intersect with the restriction set, use that the cell sits inside it, then the Lebesgue measure of a half-open interval and the ENNReal-to-real conversion.

LEAF — names and what they require (pinned Mathlib, located by grep).
- MeasureTheory.integral_indicator (hs : MeasurableSet s) : ∫ x, indicator s f x ∂μ = ∫ x in s, f x ∂μ, with measurableSet_Ico; then MeasureTheory.setIntegral_const (c : E) : ∫ _ in s, c ∂μ = μ.real s • c (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Set.lean), or integral_const (c : E) : ∫ _, c ∂μ = μ.real univ • c after simp has pushed the restriction; smul on ℝ is smul_eq_mul.
- MeasureTheory.Measure.restrict_apply (ht : MeasurableSet t) : μ.restrict s t = μ (t ∩ s). When the cell lies inside the restriction set, Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub removes the intersection (hsub : Ico a b ⊆ Icc 0 1 from 0 ≤ a and b ≤ 1, the latter by (div_le_one (by positivity)).2 after exact_mod_cast on k ≤ 2^n). If the cell is not inside, MeasureTheory.Measure.restrict_restrict (hs : MeasurableSet s) : (μ.restrict t).restrict s = μ.restrict (s ∩ t) collapses a double restriction first.
- Real.volume_Ico : volume (Ico a b) = ENNReal.ofReal (b - a); ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (h : 0 ≤ r) : (ENNReal.ofReal r).toReal = r; Measure.real unfolds to (μ s).toReal, so a goal stated with .toReal and one stated with μ.real are the same after unfolding.
- The nonnegativity side goal 0 ≤ b − a for casted endpoints ((k-1 : ℕ) : ℝ) / 2^n and (k : ℝ) / 2^n: Nat.cast_sub (needs 1 ≤ k) to turn the ℕ-subtraction into a real one, then sub_nonneg.mpr with div_le_div_of_nonneg_right; the closing arithmetic for the length 1 / 2^n is field_simp then ring after the same Nat.cast_sub.
- setIntegral_congr_fun (hs : MeasurableSet s) (h : EqOn f g s) is the alternative to the funext route when the constancy fact is stated as EqOn.

Provenance (mined-from): weak nullness of an alternating dyadic sign family, where a prior frame's Student, already holding the refinement and pair-cancellation memories, reported that rewriting each fine cell's indicator·sign integral to ±cell-measure was what it could not finish.

9e80103d9b22a9b282d05c3762db8a7c6ecedaf2.hook: interior Gronwall estimate on [δ,t]; recover endpoint by Tendsto along 𝓝[>] 0 and le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto
9e80103d9b22a9b282d05c3762db8a7c6ecedaf2.name: interior-gronwall-to-endpoint-by-one-sided-limit
9e80103d9b22a9b282d05c3762db8a7c6ecedaf2.body: To compare two ODE solutions on a closed half-line when the available Gronwall-type distance bound (e.g. dist_le_of_trajectories_ODE with constant K from a proven Lipschitz lemma) is stated on a closed interval [δ,t] strictly inside the half-line: apply the bound on [δ,t] for arbitrary 0<δ<t, then send δ→0⁺ along the one-sided filter 𝓝[>] 0 using le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto; continuity of both solutions at the endpoint makes the distance bound continuous, so the limit inherits the inequality at δ=0. This turns an interior-only estimate into an endpoint-inclusive one without any extension theorem. Leaf (membership of 𝓝[>] 0): do NOT rewrite with nhdsWithin_eq (it unfolds 𝓝 itself into an infimum and the goal dies); instead prove Ioo 0 t ∈ 𝓝[>] 0 via inter_mem (mem_nhdsWithin_of_mem_nhds (Iio_mem_nhds h)) (self_mem_nhdsWithin (s := Ioi 0)) plus an explicit set equality Iio t ∩ Ioi 0 = Ioo 0 t.

cc379274a3a453cbaa75dbb92136e5639b5f3795.hook: No orbit/normalizer API in Mathlib's Gal — count via automorphism-cardinality theorems and adjoin degree instead.
cc379274a3a453cbaa75dbb92136e5639b5f3795.name: count-adjoin-local-objects-by-automorphism-cardinality
cc379274a3a453cbaa75dbb92136e5639b5f3795.body: PATTERN — the obstacle. The natural route to counting objects localized to an intermediate field of a splitting field is group-theoretic: transitivity of the Galois action on the root set, an orbit–stabilizer index lemma, and a normalizer/stabilizer correspondence identifying the intermediate field with cosets. None of this is packaged in Mathlib: `FieldTheory/PolynomialGaloisGroup` provides `galActionHom` and `galActionHom_injective` (faithfulness) and `card_of_separable` (a cardinality), but no transitivity theorem, no orbit/stabilizer lemma, and no normalizer correspondence; grepping `Galois/Basic` for `normaliz|orbit|stabiliz|transitiv|index` returns only cardinality bookkeeping (`card_aut_eq_finrank`, `finrank_fixedField_eq_card`, `card_fixingSubgroup_eq_finrank`). Reconstructing the correspondence by hand is the most expensive detour in this domain. PATTERN — the move. Reformulate the counting goal in terms of the cardinality theorems Mathlib does state, and pair them with the degree of the simple adjoin (read off its PowerBasis — see the sibling leaf `read-simple-adjoin-degree-from-its-power-basis`). Two shapes cover most goals: (a) counting embeddings/automorphisms of a subextension — `IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank : Nat.card Gal(E/F) = Module.finrank F E` turns an automorphism count into a degree and back; (b) bounding the number of conjugates landing in a subfield — the faithful action `galActionHom` plus `card_of_separable` bounds the orbit of the whole root set by the group order. When the ambient Galois group is abelian, prefer descending structure along an algebra homomorphism from a simple adjoin into the splitting field (split the minimal polynomial in the ambient field, map it into the adjoin) over building any normalizer orbit. LEAF — verified spellings (elaborated against the pinned Mathlib, import-all): `IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank (F E) [Field F] [Field E] [Algebra F E] [FiniteDimensional F E] [IsGalois F E] : Nat.card Gal(E/F) = Module.finrank F E` — instance arguments, no separability hypothesis. `Polynomial.Gal.card_of_separable : p.Separable → Nat.card p.Gal = Module.finrank F p.SplittingField` — applies to the canonical splitting field attached to the polynomial. `Polynomial.Gal.galActionHom_injective` — faithfulness of the action on the root set; use it to inject a stabilizer/orbit claim into a group-cardinality computation instead of a nonexistent orbit lemma.

ed653c520c1a9952f5edd0b82bac56ddf3091344.hook: A function space is defined by arbitrarily accurate energy approximation from a test class, and an earlier support audit shows every admissible test is zero.
ed653c520c1a9952f5edd0b82bac56ddf3091344.name: collapse approximation spaces after the test class vanishes
ed653c520c1a9952f5edd0b82bac56ddf3091344.body: Rewrite each approximant to zero. The approximation inequality then says the nonnegative energy is below every positive epsilon, hence the energy is zero. For an integrable density consisting of a square plus a finite sum of squares, `integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg` yields almost-everywhere zero, so the represented value vanishes almost everywhere. Scope: variational spaces defined by approximation. Before: construct a Hilbert completion and representatives. After: prove the test class trivial, force the approximated energy to zero, and use the zero representative. Level: domain-specific formalization rewrite. Confidence: high. Evidence: a certified Lean proof closes a purported positive-dimensional weak-solution branch for arbitrary forcing by this reduction.

b245321d922bedad19324036d0e70114e3c0845d.hook: when Sylow or p-group Mathlib lemmas fail instance search despite matching hypotheses
b245321d922bedad19324036d0e70114e3c0845d.name: local-fact-prime-via-leti
b245321d922bedad19324036d0e70114e3c0845d.body: Sylow / p-group Mathlib API is stated over [Fact p.Prime], and a prime hypothesis that arrives as a theorem premise is not automatically an instance inside the proof — instance search then silently fails on lemmas that otherwise match. The fix is to install the instance locally at the point of use with letI : Fact p.Prime := ⟨hp⟩ before calling Sylow lemmas or IsPGroup search. General rule: when Mathlib API requires [Fact p.Prime] and your primality fact comes from a hypothesis, introduce it with letI rather than trying to pass it as an explicit argument.

e4319be9d6d684701089d419cad76c7ab7b777c8.hook: A maximum modulus route on a disk needs frontier limits, but the problem file opens only what its statement needs and the boundary comment's API hint is unchecked prose: the limit names and the frontier bound constant do not resolve, and the axiom report then names sorryAx although no sorry is written in the file.
e4319be9d6d684701089d419cad76c7ab7b777c8.name: check-the-names-before-trusting-the-axiom-report
e4319be9d6d684701089d419cad76c7ab7b777c8.body:
PATTERN — the axiom report is downstream of elaboration, so it cannot tell "you left a hole" from "the elaborator made one for you".

You are mid-proof, closing a boundary argument on a disk: a bound on the frontier is in hand and the value at the centre follows by maximum modulus. Two things then go wrong together, and they look like one thing.

First, names. A boundary comment's API hint is prose, not a checked reference: it can put a constant in the wrong namespace, and the surrounding file opens the minimal namespace set its STATEMENT needs, not the set your proof needs. Scoped notation that is not opened is silently absent rather than mis-parsed, and limit vocabulary is the usual casualty — the neighbourhood filter, the within-neighbourhood filter, the eventually quantifier and the tendsto predicate all live in scopes a complex-analysis header does not open.

Second, the report. When an identifier does not resolve, Lean reports an error and then keeps going, elaborating the offending term to a synthetic hole. A synthetic hole is sorryAx, exactly like a hand-written sorry. So a file that elaborates WITH ERRORS still prints an axiom line, and that line says your theorem depends on sorryAx while a search of the source for the word sorry returns nothing. Hunting harder for the missing sorry is the wrong search; the cause is upstream, in the error list you filtered out of the build output.

Rule: the axiom report is meaningful only on an error-free elaboration, and a zero exit status from the build command is not that. Read the full compiler output first, resolve every unknown identifier and unknown constant, and only then read the axiom line. Extending the file's open line is not a statement change — the theorem text is untouched — so extend it the moment the first limit-flavoured name fails to resolve, and say in your report that you did.

LEAF — the concrete checks.

- The maximum modulus bound for a ball is the ROOT constant `norm_le_of_forall_mem_frontier_norm_le`, declared in Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/AbsMax.lean OUTSIDE `namespace Complex`. A Complex-qualified spelling of it is an unknown constant, and a boundary comment may well hand you exactly that. It pairs with `DiffContOnCl.mk_ball`, built from differentiability on the open ball plus continuity on the closed ball. Check every name a comment gives you before building a route on it: one check round trip, no proof cost.

- A header of the form `open Complex Metric Set` does NOT bring in the limit notation used by `le_of_tendsto`, `tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff` or `filter_upwards`. Add `Topology Filter` to the same line.

- Diagnose in this order: (1) the full build output for the file, unfiltered, looking for "error:"; (2) then a textual search for sorry; (3) only then the axiom report. A clean run is: no errors, no sorry, and an axiom list of exactly propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

- Related spelling traps in the same family: there is no `Complex.norm` (use the norm bars) and no `Complex.imaginaryI` (the imaginary unit is `Complex.I`).

e3d8ff3201be3a949456f27fcc7c1df53a20dced.hook: Assembling an integral estimate where the mathematics is settled but the compiler keeps reporting unknown identifiers: the integral congruence lemma, the measurability of an absolute-value integrand such as |f x - g x|, the triangle inequality bound for the integrand, the epsilon-N form of a limit of integrals, or an order case split — each guessed name is absent.
e3d8ff3201be3a949456f27fcc7c1df53a20dced.name: everywhere-facts-enter-the-integral-layer-through-ae-and-norm-spellings
e3d8ff3201be3a949456f27fcc7c1df53a20dced.body:
PATTERN — the obstacle. Once the analytic argument is settled, a measure-integration proof usually dies on names rather than mathematics: the congruence lemma for an integral, the measurability of a derived integrand like `|f x - g x|`, the triangle inequality for absolute values, the epsilon-N unpacking of a limit, and an order case split all get guessed in an everywhere / absolute-value vocabulary, and each guess is an unknown identifier. Each miss costs a full compile of a Mathlib-importing file.

PATTERN — the move. The integral layer is stated in almost-everywhere and norm vocabulary. Convert an everywhere fact into an a.e. fact at the point of use instead of looking for an everywhere variant; state derived-integrand measurability through the norm, which for real functions is definitionally the absolute value; use the `_le` spellings for inequality bounds; unpack limits through the metric characterisation.

LEAF — names and shapes (elaborated against the pinned Mathlib; the absent names were checked absent).
- `integral_congr_ae (h : f =ᵐ[μ] g) : ∫ a, f a ∂μ = ∫ a, g a ∂μ`. For a pointwise-everywhere equality `h : ∀ x, f x = g x`, write `integral_congr_ae (Filter.Eventually.of_forall h)` or `integral_congr_ae (ae_of_all μ h)`. There is no `integral_congr` for the Bochner integral; that name exists only as `intervalIntegral.integral_congr` and for simple functions.
- `AEStronglyMeasurable.norm : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => ‖f x‖) μ`. For real-valued `f g`, `(hf.sub hg).norm` closes the goal `AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => |f x - g x|) μ` by definitional unfolding of the real norm. `AEStronglyMeasurable.abs` does not exist (`.abs` is an invalid field); the other working route is `continuous_abs.comp_aestronglyMeasurable (hf.sub hg)`. (`AEMeasurable.abs` exists, but for the other measurability predicate.)
- Triangle inequality: `abs_add_le (a b) : |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b|`; `abs_add` is absent. Also `abs_sub (a b) : |a - b| ≤ |a| + |b|` and `abs_sub_le (a b c) : |a - c| ≤ |a - b| + |b - c|`.
- Limits: `Metric.tendsto_atTop : Tendsto u atTop (𝓝 a) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, dist (u n) a < ε` is the epsilon-N form (`Metric.tendsto_iff` is absent). Pair it with `tendsto_zero_iff_norm_tendsto_zero` to pass between `𝓝 0` and norms; after `rw [tendsto_zero_iff_norm_tendsto_zero, Metric.tendsto_atTop]` the per-n goal reads `dist ‖u n‖ 0 < ε`, and `simp only [Real.dist_eq, sub_zero, Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_abs]` turns it into `|u n| < ε`.
- Order case splits: `lt_or_ge (a b) : a < b ∨ b ≤ a` and `le_or_gt (a b) : a ≤ b ∨ b < a`; `le_or_lt` and `lt_or_le` are absent in this Mathlib. For a level truncation `max (-k) (min k (f x))` the bound `|…| ≤ k` needs no case split: `rw [abs_le]` then `⟨le_max_left _ _, max_le (by simp) (min_le_left _ _)⟩`.

Provenance (mined-from): an attempt at an L1-to-L2 truncation bridge on the unit interval that closed, but reported seven such unknown-identifier misses on the way; every leaf above was re-elaborated in a scratch probe against the pinned Mathlib.

1a2bcdfd13115f1a876ec75c8100cca1ed88327a.hook: An arbitrarily indexed family of commuting nilpotent endomorphisms acts on a finite-dimensional space, while the common-kernel argument is available only for a finite family.
1a2bcdfd13115f1a876ec75c8100cca1ed88327a.name: extend-a-finite-common-kernel-through-the-operator-span
1a2bcdfd13115f1a876ec75c8100cca1ed88327a.body: Choose finitely many operators from the family whose range spans the range of the whole family, obtain a nonzero vector killed by those generators, and package the operators killing that vector as a submodule of the endomorphism space. Since that submodule contains the finite spanning family, it contains the range of every original operator. In Mathlib, `Submodule.exists_fun_fin_finrank_span_eq` supplies actual range elements as finite generators; `Submodule.span_le` and `Submodule.subset_span` then transport the common-kernel equation through their span.

40ac3baad7ab4643d2172ab7ba8c24a71df7b444.hook: A half-line ODE predicate gives continuity at the initial endpoint and differentiability only in the open interior, but a closed-interval uniqueness API requires HasDerivWithinAt at that endpoint.
40ac3baad7ab4643d2172ab7ba8c24a71df7b444.name: recover a closed-endpoint ODE derivative from the interior law
40ac3baad7ab4643d2172ab7ba8c24a71df7b444.body: Use hasDerivWithinAt_Ici_of_tendsto_deriv. Supply endpoint continuity, interior differentiability restricted from Ici to Ioi, self_mem_nhdsWithin, and a Tendsto proof for the interior derivative. Rewrite the derivative by the ODE law inside an eventual-congruence argument; continuity of the trajectory and vector field then gives the required limit. Arc rewrite rule: scope = weak half-line ODE encodings; before = avoid the closed-interval uniqueness theorem and prove a delta-to-zero Gronwall limit because the endpoint derivative seems absent; after = reconstruct the one-sided endpoint derivative from the limiting interior derivative and invoke ODE_solution_unique directly; level = Mathlib API/proof architecture; confidence = high; evidence-ids = certified endpoint recovery and uniqueness declarations in the solver head.

97d1dbcc0ce18baa8c595a45024ff07c1287ba4f.hook: A truncated principal-value or improper integral on a half-line is to be evaluated by expanding the integrand as a geometric or exponential series, the truncation endpoints move with the limit parameter, and the search for one lemma that carries the interval-integral limit through the infinite sum returns nothing.
97d1dbcc0ce18baa8c595a45024ff07c1287ba4f.name: decouple-truncation-limit-from-series-interchange-on-a-fixed-half-line
97d1dbcc0ce18baa8c595a45024ff07c1287ba4f.body:
PATTERN — the obstacle. The truncation limit and the series limit are independent, and no library statement couples them; the search for a lemma that transports a moving-endpoint interval integral through a tsum comes back empty because nothing needs to do that.

PATTERN — the move. Decouple the two limits on a fixed domain. (1) Prove first that the integrand is integrable on the whole half-line: continuity on a compact piece next to the endpoint (after pairing or extending away any singularity there) plus an explicitly exponentially dominated tail. (2) The truncated interval integrals then converge to the set integral over the half-line by exhaustion alone, one endpoint at a time; no series appears in this step. (3) Evaluate the set integral on the fixed half-line by integrating FINITE partial sums and passing to the limit by dominated convergence with a majorant independent of the partial-sum index. (4) Identify the two limits by uniqueness of limits.

LEAF — names and what they require (checked at the pinned Mathlib).
- Upper endpoint to infinity: `intervalIntegral_tendsto_integral_Ioi (a : ℝ) (hfi : IntegrableOn f (Ioi a) μ) (hb : Tendsto b l atTop) : Tendsto (fun i => ∫ x in a..b i, f x ∂μ) l (𝓝 (∫ x in Ioi a, f x ∂μ))`. For a truncation `δ ↦ δ⁻¹` along `𝓝[>] 0` the endpoint hypothesis is `tendsto_inv_nhdsGT_zero`.
- Lower endpoint down to the boundary point: `IntegrableOn.continuousWithinAt_Ici_primitive_Ioi (hf : IntegrableOn f (Ioi a₀) μ) : ContinuousWithinAt (fun b ↦ ∫ x in Ioi b, f x ∂μ) (Ici a₀) a₀`, together with `intervalIntegral.integral_Ioi_sub_Ioi (hf : IntegrableOn f (Ioi a) μ) (hab : a ≤ b) : ∫ x in Ioi a, f x ∂μ - ∫ x in Ioi b, f x ∂μ = ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ`, gives `∫ x in a₀..δ, f x → 0` as `δ → a₀` from the right. A two-sided truncation `∫ x in δ..δ⁻¹` is the difference of the two one-sided ones by `intervalIntegral.integral_interval_sub_left`; its interval-integrability inputs come from `intervalIntegrable_iff_integrableOn_Ioc_of_le` and `IntegrableOn.mono_set` off the half-line hypothesis.
- Each exponential term: `integral_exp_mul_complex_Ioi {a : ℂ} (ha : a.re < 0) (c : ℝ) : ∫ x : ℝ in Ioi c, Complex.exp (a * x) = -Complex.exp (a * c) / a`. The rate hypothesis `a.re < 0` is exactly where a strip condition on the parameter enters, once per exponential family; from `c = 0` the value is the reciprocal rate.
- The interchange on the fixed half-line: `MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence (bound : α → ℝ) (F_measurable : ∀ n, AEStronglyMeasurable (F n) μ) (bound_integrable : Integrable bound μ) (h_bound : ∀ n, ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, ‖F n a‖ ≤ bound a) (h_lim : ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, Tendsto (fun n => F n a) atTop (𝓝 (f a)))`, with `F m = ∑ n ∈ Finset.range (m + 1), term n` and `μ = volume.restrict (Ioi 0)`; the ae hypotheses open with `filter_upwards [ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Ioi]`, and each partial sum is measurable via `(integrable_finset_sum _ ...).aestronglyMeasurable`. Pointwise convergence of the partial sums is `(hasSum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one h).tendsto_sum_nat` after `HasSum.mul_left` and `HasSum.sub` shape the families; `‖Complex.exp (-x)‖ < 1` for `x > 0` is `Complex.norm_exp` with `Real.exp_lt_one_iff`.
- The majorant needs no uniform convergence: a finite geometric partial sum equals the full sum times `(1 - r ^ (m + 1))` (`geom_sum_mul_neg`, `tsum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one`), and with `‖r‖ ≤ 1` that factor has norm at most 2, so `‖F m x‖ ≤ 2 * ‖f x‖` with `f` the limit integrand, which step (1) already made integrable.
- `tendsto_nhds_unique` identifies the dominated-convergence limit with the closed-form limit of the integrated partial sums.

Provenance (mined-from): a principal-value integral over the real line with a simple pole at the origin and a parameter in an open strip; the Student named the moving-endpoint termwise step as its wall.

8d92a4d35bd71f085c010cae6fac4bf0636534b4.hook: when a parameter integral must be shown infinitely differentiable via iterated kernel differentiation
8d92a4d35bd71f085c010cae6fac4bf0636534b4.name: kernel-family-indexed-induction-for-parameter-integral-smoothness
8d92a4d35bd71f085c010cae6fac4bf0636534b4.body: Define K n x = integral of f(y)/(x+y)^(n+1); the derivative identity is K n' = -(n+1) * K (n+1), applied on a neighbourhood (x/2, 3x/2) that stays away from the singularity, using the one-derivative dominated-derivative lemma at each level. Get ContDiffOn at level m by induction over m (contDiffOn_succ_iff_deriv_of_isOpen, with the inductive statement quantified over BOTH m and the kernel index n), collecting finite levels with contDiffOn_infty. Leaf facts (current Mathlib): hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le resolves only unqualified — the MeasureTheory-prefixed name is unknown; HasDerivAt.pow leaves a beta-redex ((fun z => z+y)^(n+1)) x that simp only [Pi.pow_apply] resolves; AEStronglyMeasurable.div demands a Group instance the reals lack — use AEStronglyMeasurable.mul with Measurable.inv plus an a.e. congruence; contDiffOn_zero does not rewrite into ContDiffOn (0:enat) goals — use contDiffOn_zero.mpr with defeq unification.

ca51546142a4381d882f516b047d4f2366e35db3.hook: transferring identities proved in an L2 Hilbert completion to a goal stated as a literal pointwise integral, or extracting an approximating sequence from closure-of-tests membership
ca51546142a4381d882f516b047d4f2366e35db3.name: l2-inner-to-literal-integral-glue-via-inner-def
ca51546142a4381d882f516b047d4f2366e35db3.body: Bridging Mathlib's L2 inner product to a statement's literal integral over U of f x * g x. MeasureTheory.inner_def (Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/L2Space.lean): for f g : α →₂[μ] E, ⟪f, g⟫ = ∫ a : α, ⟪f a, g a⟫ ∂μ; the coercions are strongly measurable and the integrand integrable (integrable_inner, mem_L1_inner). For ℝ-valued L2 classes the inner product is therefore exactly the literal pointwise-product integral, so identities proved in a Hilbert completion transfer to raw-integral statements after choosing coercions. Pair with Metric.mem_closure_iff_seq_limit to extract an approximating sequence (with norm control) from membership in the closure of test functions, enabling Cauchy-Schwarz transfers from test functions to arbitrary members.

2f7663aed8619146056d93ed1e899ac026f6385c.hook: A coupled constant-coefficient second-order ODE has been diagonalized into scalar hyperbolic and trigonometric modes, but no ready-made uniqueness theorem matches the interval-local hypotheses.
2f7663aed8619146056d93ed1e899ac026f6385c.name: classify scalar ODE modes by a Wronskian quotient
2f7663aed8619146056d93ed1e899ac026f6385c.body: For a scalar mode u'' = u with u(0)=0, differentiate W(t)=u'(t)sinh(t)-u(t)cosh(t); for u''=-u use W(t)=u'(t)sin(t)-u(t)cos(t). The ODE makes W'=0 on the open interval. Extend constancy to the closed interval with Set.EqOn.closure and continuity, evaluate at the zero endpoint to get W=0, and then show the derivative of u/sinh or u/sin is zero. Set.isOpen_Ioo.exists_is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero yields u=C*sinh or u=C*sin; closure supplies the endpoints. This avoids searching for a packaged boundary-value uniqueness theorem and works directly with deriv, ContDiff, Ioo, and Icc.

52ef15432270ca03461471ac66bf17f256f47eda.hook: when a large alternating group must be shown non-solvable in a Mathlib revision with no A_n simplicity theorem for n at least 6 (only isSimpleGroup_five), and the fin_5 witness computation is the available anchor
52ef15432270ca03461471ac66bf17f256f47eda.name: alternating-nonsolvability-witness-transplant-and-perfectness-route
52ef15432270ca03461471ac66bf17f256f47eda.body: Two routes to not-IsSolvable of a large alternating group beyond embedding A5. (1) Perfectness: commutator_alternatingGroup_eq_top (5 <= card) gives Group.IsPerfect, then Group.IsPerfect.not_isSolvable. (2) Witness transplant: transplant the witness computation of Equiv.Perm.fin_5_not_solvable into the larger alternating group by multiplying each odd witness permutation by an extra transposition on the surplus points so every witness becomes even while agreeing with the original on the 5 base points; the key conjugation identity then holds by native_decide on the underlying permutations, and the derivedSeries induction from not_solvable_of_mem_derivedSeries goes through verbatim (fully-qualified root names: derivedSeries_normal, Subgroup.commutator_mem_commutator, Subgroup.mem_top).

060dcb478834de4f167dcb84f9a746867f6f840f.hook: When an integral transform must be proved smooth on an open positive-parameter domain but the available theorem gives only a pointwise first derivative under the integral.
060dcb478834de4f167dcb84f9a746867f6f840f.name: iterate dominated parameter differentiation through a kernel family
060dcb478834de4f167dcb84f9a746867f6f840f.body: Introduce a natural-number-indexed kernel family whose nth member has denominator power n+1. On a neighbourhood such as (x/2,3x/2), dominate the derivative of every indexed kernel by a constant multiple of the original integrable input; `hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le` then identifies each derivative with the next family member. Prove `ContDiffOn` by induction using `contDiffOn_succ_iff_deriv_of_isOpen`: before, repeated differentiation is an unstructured iteration obligation; after, the derivative recurrence shifts the index and the induction hypothesis discharges smoothness. Scope: parameter integrals on an open set with an integrable local derivative majorant. Level: domain proof pattern. Confidence: certified single instance.

84879e616f0330fba6f3e3b60aeeb83c90137a6d.hook: When a continuous lift through Complex.exp must be upgraded to complex differentiability on an open set, retrieve the strict-derivative local-inverse API and transfer regularity by eventual equality.
84879e616f0330fba6f3e3b60aeeb83c90137a6d.name: continuous-exp-lift-via-strict-derivative-local-inverse
84879e616f0330fba6f3e3b60aeeb83c90137a6d.body: For each source point, set a to the lifted value and use Complex.hasStrictDerivAt_exp a with Complex.exp_ne_zero a. Construct L with HasStrictDerivAt.localInverse, obtain differentiability of L from HasStrictDerivAt.to_localInverse, and compose L with the holomorphic projected map. The key neighborhood step is HasStrictDerivAt.eventually_left_inverse: pull that eventual statement back along continuity of the lift, rewrite the projection identity, and use DifferentiableWithinAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq_of_mem. For a lift whose domain is a subtype, eventually_nhds_subtype_iff converts the neighborhood statement to nhdsWithin on the ambient set. Mined from the residual of upgrading a continuous exponential lift to a holomorphic ambient representative.
