85165c91bd84cca34c02a9c32e2aa26b7c456911.hook: A holomorphic boundary argument has pointwise radial convergence, while Cauchy integrals run over circles whose radius tends to the boundary.
85165c91bd84cca34c02a9c32e2aa26b7c456911.name: dominated-convergence-for-moving-circle-integrals
85165c91bd84cca34c02a9c32e2aa26b7c456911.body: Rewrite each circle integral as a fixed angular interval integral. For a fixed interior evaluation point, restrict the radius filter eventually above both a positive lower radius and the midpoint between its norm and the boundary. The reverse triangle inequality then gives a radius-independent lower bound for the Cauchy denominator; combine it with the angular majorant and apply intervalIntegral.tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence. Scope: one-sided radial limits of parametrized circle integrals. Before: seek a boundary-uniqueness theorem consuming pointwise limits. After: prove an eventual fixed-domain DCT statement and identify the eventually constant Cauchy integral. Level: domain proof shape. Confidence: high; witnessed by a certified Lean proof.

503dac2ad456d751a632d2101919c85ba40de248.hook: Applying the Fourier inversion theorem to recover a point value of an L1 kernel, then reducing a half-line cosine integral to the full-line one.
503dac2ad456d751a632d2101919c85ba40de248.name: fourier-inversion-application-hypotheses-and-half-line-fold
503dac2ad456d751a632d2101919c85ba40de248.body: Leaf rewrite rule. Scope: evaluating real oscillatory integrals through transform pairs. Before: attacking the half-line integral directly, or omitting the inversion theorem's side conditions. After: (a) inversion via fourierInv_fourier_eq with the evaluation point set to frequency / (2*pi) requires two explicit hypotheses the tactic will not find - Integrable of the transformed function, discharged by rewriting the transform pointwise to a scalar multiple of (1+w^2)^-1 and using integrable_inv_one_add_sq.const_mul, and ContinuousAt of the kernel at the evaluation point, discharged by fun_prop; (b) restate with Real.fourierInv_eq' and take real parts with integral_re only after the full complex equality is established, verifying the pointwise real-part identity as its own step; (c) fold the full-line integral to the half-line by integral_comp_abs applied to the cosine kernel, rewriting cos(|x|*s) to cos(x*s) by casework with abs_of_nonneg / abs_of_nonpos, Real.cos_neg and neg_mul; (d) reduce a kernel (x^2+a^2)^-1 to the standard 1+u^2 form by the exact change of variables integral_comp_mul_left_Ioi followed by integral_const_mul. Level: domain (real analysis / Fourier methods in Lean). Confidence: high, commit-certified.

df8c1f676def3597a0bd42b897af46dd1dac8dad.hook: when a distributional derivative/primitive operator must be a continuous linear map but its natural codomain is the test-function LF space — transpose into the dual 𝓓′ instead; Mathlib has no continuity criterion for maps INTO 𝓓
df8c1f676def3597a0bd42b897af46dd1dac8dad.name: transpose-distributional-operators-into-dual-not-into-test-functions
df8c1f676def3597a0bd42b897af46dd1dac8dad.body: PATTERN — When a distributional operator (derivative, primitive, normalized primitive, transpose of a differential operator) must be shipped as a continuous linear map and the natural codomain is the test-function space 𝓓, building a map INTO 𝓓 is the wrong route: the LF inductive-limit topology on 𝓓 offers no continuity criterion for incoming linear maps in Mathlib, and the support of the image varies with the input (a primitive's support is strictly larger than the input's), so no fixed-support stage 𝓓_K contains the range. Transpose instead: define the new object as an element of the dual 𝓓′ (a Distribution) by a pairing formula that only uses existing distribution actions, and prove ITS continuity with the universal property for maps FROM 𝓓, which reduces to continuity on each fixed-support stage 𝓓_K where seminorm estimates are meaningful. LEAF (verified against Mathlib Analysis/Distribution, current master): `Distribution.lean` exposes only `mapCLM` (postcomposition of a distribution by a CLM F →L G) and `mapCLM_apply`; there is no distributional-derivative operator, no primitive operator, no transpose API. The test-function topology lives in `TestFunction.lean`: `TestFunction.topologicalSpace` is the LF inductive limit; `originalTop` is the sup of the coinduced topologies from each `𝓓_K`; `topologicalSpace_le_iff` characterizes it; `continuous_ofSupportedIn` and the bundled `ofSupportedInCLM : 𝓓_K →L 𝕜 𝓓` give the continuous inclusions; and the ONLY universal property is `TestFunction.continuous_iff_continuous_comp` — a LINEAR map f : 𝓓 →ₗ V into a locally convex space is continuous iff f ∘ ofSupportedIn K is continuous for every compact K ⊆ Ω. A Distribution is an abbrev for 𝓓(Ω,ℝ) →L[ℝ] F, so any object you can present through that interface is continuous by construction; build deriv/primitive operators as pairings, never as operators on 𝓓 itself. Provenance (mined-from): f207 student-attempt-1 residual — parts (b)/(c) blocked on shipping a normalized distributional primitive as a map into 𝓓.

8ceb3a67a6aed56c0bc0384b963b3ad0c0c683ea.hook: A nonnegative sequence has vanishing integrals but every point admits arbitrarily late values above every threshold, and the goal asks to negate almost-everywhere convergence to some finite limit.
8ceb3a67a6aed56c0bc0384b963b3ad0c0c683ea.name: Refute almost-everywhere convergence with a cofinally unbounded subsequence
8ceb3a67a6aed56c0bc0384b963b3ad0c0c683ea.body: Assume almost-everywhere convergence and intersect that full-measure event with membership in the restricted set. At such a point, convergence to a gives an index N after which every value is within 1 of a. Cofinal unboundedness at threshold a+1 supplies k >= N with a+1 <= f k x, contradicting the distance bound. Promote the pointwise contradiction to an almost-everywhere False statement; ae_iff then forces the restricted measure of univ to be zero, which contradicts the known positive measure of the restriction. This avoids trying to identify a common divergent subsequence or prove that the limit must be zero.

e740c8bd41eb100f515596388b50d958a0d8c74b.hook: second-pass spellings for the entire injective ⇒ affine route (reciprocal difference quotient + Liouville): Tendsto.inv0 and slope_def do not exist — use Tendsto.inv₀ and simp [slope]; fill the puncture with continuousAt_iff_punctured_nhds then Tendsto.congr' (needs the EventuallyEq .symm, Tendsto.congr wants pointwise); IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn gives hmax with membership-only application hmax hz; div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (not _left) for a / c ≤ b / c; linarith cannot divide by δ — rw [div_le_iff₀] / div_eq_iff first then nlinarith or linear_combination
e740c8bd41eb100f515596388b50d958a0d8c74b.body:
Second certified close of the same entire-injective-implies-affine route (reciprocal difference quotient G, Liouville on its difference quotient Q; Mathlib as pinned by apm-lean f7de6887, 2026-08-25, lean exit 0, no sorry). The route was reused from a shelf memory "verbatim in structure" and the Lean was written fresh; these are the spellings that cost compile cycles the second time, with the form that compiled. Complements the first-pass list (filter_upwards single binder, ▸ transport, div_le_div_iff phantom, is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero endpoints, subst, mul_le_mul order).

(1) `Tendsto.inv0` and `slope_def` do not exist. The inverse-limit lemma is `Tendsto.inv₀` (subscript zero): `((hf.differentiableAt).hasDerivAt.tendsto_slope).inv₀ hw : Tendsto (fun z => (slope f w z)⁻¹) (𝓝[≠] w) (𝓝 (deriv f w)⁻¹)`. `slope` unfolds by `simp [slope]` — it is `(y - x)⁻¹ • (f y - f x)`, so after `rw [hGval z hz, div_eq_inv_mul]` the goal closes by `simp [slope]`.

(2) Filling the puncture: instead of a hand-written ContinuousAt helper, `rw [continuousAt_iff_punctured_nhds, hGw]` turns `ContinuousAt G w` into the punctured limit, and `exact hsl.congr' hGeq.symm` closes it. Direction matters: `Tendsto.congr'` takes `f₁ =ᶠ[l] f₂` and maps `Tendsto f₁ l …` to `Tendsto f₂ l …`, so with `hGeq : G =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] w] fun z => (slope f w z)⁻¹` you need `hGeq.symm`. `Tendsto.congr` (no prime) wants a pointwise `∀ x, f₁ x = f₂ x`, not an EventuallyEq.

(3) `IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn` binder order: `obtain ⟨z₀, hmem, hmax⟩ := (isCompact_closedBall (0 : ℂ) R).exists_isMaxOn ⟨0, mem_closedBall_self hR⟩ (hG.continuous.continuousOn.norm)` gives `hmax : IsMaxOn (‖G ·‖) (closedBall 0 R) z₀`, and the bound is `fun z hz => hmax hz` — membership only; do not pass the point.

(4) `div_le_div_of_nonneg_left` scales the LEFT argument; for `a / c ≤ b / c` from `a ≤ b` and `0 ≤ c` use `div_le_div_of_nonneg_right h1 hc` (the `.le` of a positivity fact).

(5) `linarith` cannot see through division by a variable (`… / δ`, `… / ‖z - w‖`). Clear the denominator first: `rw [div_le_iff₀ hpos]` for `a / b ≤ c`, `rw [div_eq_iff hne] at h1` for an equation, then `nlinarith` / `linear_combination h1` on the polynomial goal.

(6) The far-field bound for the difference quotient of G composes as `calc ‖G z - G w‖ / ‖z - w‖ ≤ (K * (1 + ‖z‖) + ‖G w‖) / ‖z - w‖ := div_le_div_of_nonneg_right h1 hdenpos.le` then `_ ≤ 2 * (K * 2 + ‖G w‖) := h2`, where `h2` comes from `‖z‖ / 2 ≤ ‖z - w‖` cleared by `div_le_iff₀`.

Operational: the controller-owned memory searches can exceed a 30 s shell default under substrate load; retry with a longer timeout before concluding the corpus has nothing — the decisive memory surfaced on the third query, phrased in the obstacle's own words ("entire injective function must be linear essential singularity at infinity").

88bd0fbe9e851f10bab94854b52baece45fe2257.hook: Cancelling alternating contributions over a decomposition: do not build an explicit pairing bijection on the index Finset. If the terms cancel in consecutive pairs, sum over `Finset.range (2 * k)` and induct on k, peeling TWO terms per step with `Finset.sum_range_succ` twice; the pair hypothesis `forall i, g (2*i) + g (2*i+1) = 0` then closes each step by `simpa using h k`, with `2 * (k+1) = (2*k+1) + 1` supplied by `ring` before the rewrite. Whole proof is six lines and needs no reindexing lemma, no `Finset.sum_nbij`, no even/odd filter split. Verified: elaborates against the pinned Mathlib, exit 0, no sorry. Use it whenever a signed function is constant on each cell of a refinement and adjacent cells carry opposite signs — the sum-side obligation is then this, not a combinatorial pairing argument.
88bd0fbe9e851f10bab94854b52baece45fe2257.name: pair-cancellation-is-an-induction-not-a-bijection
88bd0fbe9e851f10bab94854b52baece45fe2257.body:
PATTERN — the obstacle. A refinement argument produces a finite sum whose
terms cancel in adjacent pairs (a sign that alternates cell by cell, a
telescoping difference, a function that is +1 on odd cells and -1 on even
ones). The instinct is to express the cancellation as a structural fact about
the index set: split the Finset into evens and odds, build a bijection between
the halves, and sum along it. That is a combinatorial detour. It needs a
reindexing lemma you then have to find, the bijection's side conditions are
fiddly, and none of it is about the mathematics you are actually doing.

PATTERN — the move. Cancellation in consecutive pairs is an INDUCTION on the
number of pairs, not a bijection on the index set. Write the range as an even
length, induct on the pair count, and peel two terms per step. Each step is
exactly one application of the pair hypothesis, so the proof length is
independent of how the signs were produced upstream — which means you can
state and close the summation obligation BEFORE you have proved anything about
the cells, and hand it the sign lemma later. That ordering matters: it keeps a
cheap, closable obligation from being blocked behind an expensive one.

The general shape of the obligation to state is: a function on indices, a
hypothesis that each consecutive pair sums to zero, and a conclusion that the
sum over an even-length range is zero. Everything problem-specific stays in
the hypothesis.

LEAF (@how) — pinned Mathlib; this elaborated, exit 0, no sorry:

  (g : N -> R) (k : N) (h : forall i, g (2*i) + g (2*i+1) = 0) :
    sum over i in Finset.range (2*k) of g i = 0

  induction k with
  | zero => simp
  | succ k ih =>
      have hstep : 2 * (k + 1) = (2 * k + 1) + 1 := by ring
      rw [hstep, Finset.sum_range_succ, Finset.sum_range_succ, ih]
      simpa using h k

 * `Finset.sum_range_succ` is the only summation lemma required. Applying it
   twice is what peels a whole pair; the `hstep` rewrite is needed because
   `2 * (k+1)` is not syntactically `(2*k+1)+1` and `Finset.sum_range_succ`
   matches only the successor form. `ring` proves `hstep`; `omega` also works.
 * `ih` is discharged by the same `rw`, so there is no separate appeal to it.
 * `simpa using h k` absorbs the `add_zero` / re-association left by the two
   peels. If the pair hypothesis is stated with the opposite orientation
   (`g (2*i+1) + g (2*i) = 0`) add `add_comm` to the `simpa` set rather than
   restating the hypothesis.
 * If the range is not literally of the form `2 * k`, convert first: an
   argument over `Finset.Ico p q` becomes a range through
   `Finset.sum_Ico_eq_sum_range`, and a refinement of one coarse cell into
   `2 ^ (n - m)` fine cells is already even whenever `m < n`, so `k` is
   `2 ^ (n - m - 1)`.

d6c49eba0c434795c8169ee5493a4073d434dc28.hook: Trying to conclude a subgroup coerced into a larger subgroup equals bottom, but the lemma you found talks about disjointness; also rewriting after a set of a normalCore fails
d6c49eba0c434795c8169ee5493a4073d434dc28.name: subgrouple-eq-bot-is-stated-as-disjoint
d6c49eba0c434795c8169ee5493a4073d434dc28.body: Subgroup.subgroupOf_eq_bot does not state N = bottom; it states Disjoint H N. To recover N = bottom from N <= H, combine disjoint_iff with inf_eq_left.mpr. Separately, after `set N := normalCore P ...`, a rewrite with the obtained N = bottom fact fails because the goal displays the unfolded normalCore; supply it with `exact` (defeq) instead of `rw`. Both frictions were paid once each and then compiled; generalises to any statement whose displayed form is an unfolding of a let/set-bound definition.

f020aef3a569a51060abacc0ed6de0fdd19acc98.hook: In a finite Galois extension, a proof needs to identify the normal closure of a simple intermediate field with the field generated by all roots of the generator's minimal polynomial, but no packaged equality is available.
f020aef3a569a51060abacc0ed6de0fdd19acc98.name: identify-simple-normal-closure-by-root-membership
f020aef3a569a51060abacc0ed6de0fdd19acc98.body: Use the universal property of `IntermediateField.normalClosure` in both directions. For the root-generated field, obtain `Normal` from `IntermediateField.adjoin_rootSet_isSplittingField` and `Normal.of_isSplittingField`, then show it contains the original generator via `Polynomial.mem_rootSet` and `minpoly.aeval`. Conversely, place the generator in the normal closure, regard it as an element of that subtype, transport its minimal polynomial along the subtype inclusion with `minpoly.algHom_eq`, and use normality to get splitting there. `IntermediateField.splits_iff_mem` then puts every ambient root in the normal closure. This avoids the apparent need to extend embeddings or enumerate conjugates. Rewrite rule: scope = finite Galois simple extensions; before = expand the normal closure as a supremum of conjugate fields and seek embedding-extension machinery; after = prove the two inclusions using normality, minimal-polynomial transport, and root membership; level = proof shape; confidence = high; evidence-ids = certified solver head and base boundary departure. Mined from a residual where the missing bridge was exactly the simple-extension normal-closure identity.

cb525f12f5f37151094a2e6db71a86eea391b096.hook: A real oscillatory integral - a cosine or exponential transform of an even, absolutely integrable kernel like 1/(x^2+a^2) or exp(-c|x|) - must be evaluated in closed form, and the informal or file-suggested route is the residue theorem over a semicircular contour, which the library does not support.
cb525f12f5f37151094a2e6db71a86eea391b096.name: fourier-inversion-replaces-residue-calculus
cb525f12f5f37151094a2e6db71a86eea391b096.body: Pattern (trigger/move/reason). Trigger: the target is a full-line or half-line Fourier cosine transform of an even decaying kernel, and searches for residue, contour-deformation, arc-estimate, or a prepackaged transform of the kernel come back empty. Move: dualise instead of deforming - compute the Fourier transform of the symmetric decaying kernel directly from the library's one-sided complex-exponential integrals (upper half-line where the exponent coefficient has negative real part, lower half-line where positive, stitched along 0), then apply the Fourier inversion theorem at the rescaled frequency and take the real part; the half-line integral folds out of the full-line one by evenness. Reason: the library's Fourier folder carries the whole argument (transform lemmas for exponentials, the inversion theorem with its explicit integrability-of-the-transform and continuity-at-the-point hypotheses), while its complex-analysis folder has no residue theorem at all, so the honest cost comparison is 'adapt Fourier conventions' versus 'build contour integration from scratch'. The seam is convention: the library's transform is 2pi-normalized, so the evaluation frequency must be rescaled by 1/(2pi) and the phase identity verified pointwise before any real-part extraction.

d85b006767fe5fe2f3f8d318d752aaaaca3938bd.hook: A splitting-field or root-counting proof fails wholesale at the statement level: rootSet/card lemmas do not apply, or a remembered IsAlgClosed splits_codomain shape reports deprecated. Any proof about Splits/rootSet written from older Mathlib memory.
d85b006767fe5fe2f3f8d318d752aaaaca3938bd.name: splits-rootset-new-api-mapped-polynomial
d85b006767fe5fe2f3f8d318d752aaaaca3938bd.body: Recent Mathlib's Polynomial.Splits takes no ring-hom argument (field implicit), and card_rootSet_eq_natDegree applies to Splits (p.map (algebraMap F K)), not the unmapped p. Scratch written against the older shape fails with unrelated-looking errors before any mathematics. Rewrite the statement to the mapped polynomial first. Deprecated splits_codomain still compiles — a deprecation warning is a generation tell, not a failure. Witness: rewriting a whole complex-model proof to the new signatures made it compile.

34c5566f9de1e693fce6e491a1cab92eff3cc801.hook: constructing or classifying a hom out of a cyclic group by the image of its generator
34c5566f9de1e693fce6e491a1cab92eff3cc801.name: cyclic-source-hom-from-generator-image
34c5566f9de1e693fce6e491a1cab92eff3cc801.body:
PATTERN. Classifying or constructing homomorphisms out of a cyclic source group into an arbitrary target, including a non-commutative one such as an automorphism group. A hand-rolled definition by cases on the two elements of the source forces a manual multiplicativity case analysis; the classification instead reduces to enumerating target elements whose order divides the generator's order, because such an element determines the hom. Mathlib packages this construction, so no presentation or quotient of the integers is needed.

LEAF. monoidHomOfForallMemZpowers, in Mathlib.GroupTheory.SpecificGroups.Cyclic, with hypotheses (hg that every x is in zpowers g) and (hg' that orderOf g' divides orderOf g), produces a map G to* G'; the target needs only a Group instance, so MulAut of any group qualifies. monoidHomOfForallMemZpowers_apply_gen states the map sends g to g'. For sources where the map can be written directly, MonoidHom.mk' also accepts any Group target with only a map_mul proof; it does NOT require a commutative target.

Coin rationale. No existing pattern id in the mathematics libraries names the cyclic-source hom construction; this id names the obstacle and the move.

mined-from. guide-intervention-2 of a semidirect-product frame; the Student's remaining wall was a classification of maps from a two-element quotient group into MulAut, where a by-cases witness construction ran out of budget on multiplicativity.

e614a242cb26fccbe4792e2ba36aa99dc8424ec3.hook: You need 'a multiset of pairwise non-associated primes contains each associate class at most once' and search finds no countP_le_one lemma.
e614a242cb26fccbe4792e2ba36aa99dc8424ec3.name: countp-associated-le-one-has-no-packaged-lemma-prove-by-multiset-induction
e614a242cb26fccbe4792e2ba36aa99dc8424ec3.body: No packaged Multiset.countP_le_one of any shape exists in current Mathlib. Prove the bound as a small helper by Multiset induction: the empty/cons case names (not zero/cons), discharging the cons step from nodup (the head is not among the tail) plus the fact that Associated is an equivalence so any two elements of the tail satisfying the same head-relative association predicate are themselves associated (or use filter/count lemmas: Multiset.count_eq_card_filter_eq and Multiset.nodup_iff_count_le_one transport the nodup fact). What makes distinct orbit images non-associated is the purity/degree argument, not the counting; separate the two.

2aceaee46008634ad797459820fc82f15701f2a6.hook: Retrieve when a fixed-point construction needs continuous functions on an unbounded closed domain with a sup bound and decay at infinity.
2aceaee46008634ad797459820fc82f15701f2a6.name: decaying-half-line contractions belong in C0 closed balls
2aceaee46008634ad797459820fc82f15701f2a6.body: Use `C₀(X, E)` as the complete sup-norm carrier and restrict the operator to `Metric.closedBall`. If the domain is an ordered subtype such as a closed half-line, provide `CompactIccSpace` so `cocompact_eq_atTop` exposes the desired order-filter decay. Point evaluations are bounded through `BoundedContinuousFunction.norm_coe_le_norm`, and `BoundedContinuousFunction.dist_coe_le_dist` turns evaluation differences into ambient metric bounds. This avoids constructing a bespoke complete function space while retaining exactly the continuity, decay, radius, and contraction data Banach's theorem needs.

55281ca6098e22564abc96650774d6f226f78a33.hook: A commuting semisimple--nilpotent decomposition must prove that the semisimple summand acts by the eigenvalue on a generalized eigenspace, and an explicit restriction proof would require extensive subtype bookkeeping.
55281ca6098e22564abc96650774d6f226f78a33.name: use-the-packaged-generalized-eigenspace-action-theorem
55281ca6098e22564abc96650774d6f226f78a33.body: Rewrite the generalized-eigenspace witness with `Module.End.mem_genEigenspace`, prove the original operator commutes with the semisimple summand by expanding the commuting sum, convert `IsSemisimple` through `Module.End.isFinitelySemisimple_iff_isSemisimple`, and apply `Module.End.apply_eq_of_mem_of_comm_of_isFinitelySemisimple_of_isNil` with `k := top`. The packaged theorem directly yields the scalar-action equality and subsumes the longer route through restricted endomorphisms and decomposition uniqueness.

7bbb264cf396c7ee0a6eee69e795b2230ed4bf36.hook: A smooth regularization converges to a locally integrable kernel away from one pole, and convergence of its integral pairing is required.
7bbb264cf396c7ee0a6eee69e795b2230ed4bf36.name: regularized singular pairing by almost-everywhere dominated convergence
7bbb264cf396c7ee0a6eee69e795b2230ed4bf36.body: Apply `tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence` with four ingredients: eventual strong measurability from smoothness, a parameter-independent integrable dominator, and pointwise convergence after removing the pole almost everywhere. Establish the last step with `measure_singleton` and `filter_upwards`; there is no need to define or prove convergence at the singular point. For a compactly supported continuous multiplier, a dominator consisting of the absolute limiting kernel pairing plus a constant multiple of the multiplier is integrable by local integrability on compact support.

71e1db9d24d40cbf28fffe46a1cde2747932f6d1.hook: Inducting on a divisibility-ordered list via a gcd-profile: the dropLast step needs saturation, rel_getLast, mul_right_cancel, Pairwise.sublist
71e1db9d24d40cbf28fffe46a1cde2747932f6d1.name: gcd-profile-droplast-uniqueness-mechanics
71e1db9d24d40cbf28fffe46a1cde2747932f6d1.body: Parent pattern: math-formalization/recover-invariant-factors-from-power-kernel-cardinalities. PATTERN — the mechanics of proving two divisibility-ordered factor lists equal from equality of a multiplicative profile (product of per-factor gcds with k). The induction that closes is over the list via dropLast, and each step needs exactly four facts, all with direct library spellings; searching for a packaged chain-transitivity/last lemma for List.Pairwise finds nothing — prove saturation by List.pairwise_cons induction by hand. (1) Saturation: if the profile at k equals the product of the list, every entry divides k — compare Nat.gcd_le_left and profile-divides-product, split the product equality with nlinarith into a.gcd k = a and profile-tail = product-tail, then Nat.gcd_eq_left_iff_dvd. (2) Last-factor equality: evaluate each list's profile at the OTHER list's last element and apply saturation both ways, concluding with Nat.dvd_antisymm; membership of the last element is List.getLast_mem, and Pairwise relating-to-last is List.Pairwise.rel_getLast. (3) Cancellation: profile d k = profile d.dropLast k * (d.getLast _).gcd k from List.dropLast_append_getLast (congrArg the profile over the append equation), then Nat.mul_right_cancel with positivity from Nat.gcd_pos_of_pos_left. (4) The ≥2 bound and Pairwise both survive dropLast via List.dropLast_subset and List.Pairwise.sublist (List.dropLast_sublist). Recursive list equality terminates via termination_by d.length with decreasing_by from List.length_pos_of_ne_nil. Also: a Fin-indexed product over d.length should be replaced by List.map/List.prod early — Finset.prod_univ_succ does not exist in current Mathlib; List.prod_ofFn / List.ofFn_getElem_eq_map bridge the two presentations. MINED FROM an attempt that held the profile idea but exhausted its budget formalizing exactly these four steps; spellings verified against a compiling development.

1335f45f61d99e953f6d6f23b068530ae9a11b92.hook: A family of Cauchy integrals tends to zero as radii approach the boundary, and the evaluation point lies strictly inside every sufficiently large smaller circle.
1335f45f61d99e953f6d6f23b068530ae9a11b92.name: eventual-cauchy-formula-turns-a-vanishing-integral-limit-into-a-point-value
1335f45f61d99e953f6d6f23b068530ae9a11b92.body: Use Ioo_mem_nhdsLT to show that eventually the radius is greater than the point norm and less than the domain radius. On that eventual set, the circle Cauchy formula makes the integral family equal to the constant scalar multiple of the interior value. Transfer the limit with Tendsto.congr', use uniqueness of limits against tendsto_const_nhds, and cancel the nonzero Cauchy scalar.

c62dd8ebc6eec7986b239357123699baf37e09ed.hook: when polynomial evaluation on a diagonal-shaped matrix or endomorphism is needed entrywise and no packaged aeval-on-diagonal lemma is found
c62dd8ebc6eec7986b239357123699baf37e09ed.name: entrywise-polyeval-on-diagonal-via-polynomial-induction
c62dd8ebc6eec7986b239357123699baf37e09ed.body: This Mathlib (lean4 v4.29-era) packages no entrywise evaluation lemma for polynomials on diagonal matrices: probes for a Matrix.aeval-diagonal name failed (unknown constant) and exact?/simp stall on the entry goal. Prove the identity aeval (Matrix.diagonal v) q i j = if i = j then eval (v i) q else 0 by Polynomial.induction_on', whose constructor cases are add and monomial — not the add/mul/const split first attempted. The monomial case closes with Matrix.diagonal_pow and Finset.prod_apply (pointwise product application). Prediction error from the attempted round: expecting a packaged entrywise-aeval lemma; none exists, and the by-induction proof is short once the right induction principle is chosen.

69815df70779ddb9ed51de94f9f5e3ba77b65766.hook: When a theorem supplies a finite group's cardinality as p^n and the desired Mathlib conclusions are phrased through IsPGroup instances or predicates.
69815df70779ddb9ed51de94f9f5e3ba77b65766.name: bridge-finite-prime-power-cardinality-to-is-p-group-api
69815df70779ddb9ed51de94f9f5e3ba77b65766.body: Install letI : Fact p.Prime := <hp> before invoking the p-group API, then construct hG : IsPGroup p G with IsPGroup.of_card after rewriting Nat.card to Fintype.card via Nat.card_eq_fintype_card. For a nontrivial-center conclusion, turn 1 < Fintype.card G into a Nontrivial G instance with Fintype.one_lt_card_iff_nontrivial and use hG.bot_lt_center. For nilpotence, hG.isNilpotent feeds nilpotent_iff_lowerCentralSeries directly. This avoids unfolding or rebuilding the standard finite-p-group theory.

5309464c55ad85b88b0c1c2f30842601aa5fb5d4.hook: When assembling the truncation sandwich, the exact Mathlib interfaces that package a bounded measurable function into Lp, keep products integrable, and bound an integral by the integral of its bound.
5309464c55ad85b88b0c1c2f30842601aa5fb5d4.name: memlp-of-bound-bdd-smul-integral-norm-api-shapes
5309464c55ad85b88b0c1c2f30842601aa5fb5d4.body: Leaf API facts for the truncation pattern. MemLp.of_bound : AEStronglyMeasurable f mu -> C -> (forall^ae x, ||f x|| <= C) -> MemLp f p mu, the one-call route from a.e. boundedness to Lp on any measure. Integrable.bdd_smul : an Integrable f smoothed with an a.e.-M-bounded AEStronglyMeasurable g is Integrable (works for (f - trunc) * g and trunc * g alike). norm_integral_le_of_norm_le : Integrable (|.|-dominated integrand) plus a.e. pointwise norm bound gives ||Integral phi|| <= Integral (bound), and integral_const_mul pulls the constant out. Pointwise convergence of truncations: obtain N with |f x| < N from exists_nat_gt, then tendsto_atTop_of_eventually_const makes h k x eventually constant equal to f x. Measurability transfer for restrict measures: from Measurable ((s).indicator g), use Measurable.aestronglyMeasurable.mono_measure Measure.restrict_le_self and congr with indicator_ae_eq_restrict to get AEStronglyMeasurable g (volume.restrict s). Parent pattern: extend-test-function-convergence-from-Lp-approximants-to-L1-by-bounded-truncation; mined from the certified bridge-theorem closure in the solver head.

ff8d6c424fc9b42418033fa99397645351f92882.hook: when a proof component mixes open-ball membership with a strict norm inequality, or when Lean reports 'invalid by tactic, expected type has not been provided' at the statement or at inline by-terms
ff8d6c424fc9b42418033fa99397645351f92882.name: metric-ball-membership-is-not-defeq-strict-inequality
ff8d6c424fc9b42418033fa99397645351f92882.body: Membership in an open ball centered at zero is not definitionally equal to |x| < R, and inline by-terms inside an anonymous constructor can report 'invalid by tactic, expected type has not been provided' when the real defect is that defeq mismatch underneath — a misleading cascade that misattributes the failure to the tactic syntax. Fix: prove the membership goal, rewrite with Metric.mem_ball and dist_zero_right to surface |x| < R, then extract the two strict halves as named haves before building the constructor. Bisect the proof body against standalone copies of the component to locate the true defect.

6fe11de5ccbdacd059e07caceb878f23898e1b66.hook: A group-theoretic property is encoded by eventual equality of a recursively defined descending subgroup series with bottom, while direct computation of every stage is impractical.
6fe11de5ccbdacd059e07caceb878f23898e1b66.name: refute termination of a descending group series with a persistent commutator witness
6fe11de5ccbdacd059e07caceb878f23898e1b66.body: Choose a concrete nonidentity element x and prove by induction that x belongs to every stage. For a lower central series, the successor step can be discharged by exhibiting a fixed y and a verified identity expressing x as a commutator of x or its inverse with y; after rewriting lowerCentralSeries_succ, Subgroup.commutator_mem_commutator propagates membership. In a small finite permutation group, define x and y explicitly and let decide certify both nontriviality and the multiplication identity. Any claimed terminal stage would then put x in bottom, contradicting x != 1. This turns non-nilpotence into one stable witness plus one finite computation instead of expanding arbitrary series stages.

0aa48202729971b3e2bbf0f8e17f36c667d5630b.hook: Establishing n_p interval Sylow-count constraints in Lean stalls on card-notation, missing Fact (Nat.Prime p), and stuck factorization decidability - not on mathematics.
0aa48202729971b3e2bbf0f8e17f36c667d5630b.name: sylow-count-arithmetic-shell
0aa48202729971b3e2bbf0f8e17f36c667d5630b.body: PATTERN - the obstacle. Establishing Sylow-count constraints (n_p divides the index, n_p = 1 mod p) for a concrete group order in Mathlib stalls on three independent elaboration traps, none of them mathematical: (1) Sylow p G is a Type, so (Sylow p G).card is invalid field notation - use Fintype.card (Sylow p G) or Nat.card; (2) Sylow.card_dvd_index and P.card_eq_multiplicity require an explicit Fact (Nat.Prime p) instance that is not inferred from a numeric literal - supply haveI : Fact (Nat.Prime 5) := by norm_num style; (3) the card lemmas mix Nat.card, Fintype.card, and Subgroup.index forms that omega cannot reconcile - rewrite through Nat.card_eq_fintype_card and Subgroup.card_mul_index explicitly before finishing with omega/norm_num. LEAF - the arithmetic identity (30).factorization 5 = 1 (and its relatives) is NOT closed by decide (the Decidable instance gets stuck on the well-founded Nat.factorization/padicValNat match), and norm_num/simp make no progress; the working incantation is rw [Nat.factorization_def (p := 5) (pp := by norm_num)] reducing to padicValNat 5 30 = 1, then native_decide. Combining: Nat.le_of_dvd caps n_p by the divisor, Nat.ModEq unfolded via simp only [Nat.ModEq] then norm_num, then omega closes the interval membership. With this shell a lemma n_5 in {1,6} / n_3 in {1,10} for order-30 groups compiles in minutes; without it the same arithmetic burns a 30-minute budget. MINED FROM a Student attempt on Sylow structure of order-30 groups that spent its budget discovering each trap by compiler error. No problem-specific identifiers are needed to apply this.

eab1f7e85ded352568db74c76daec1a1599639f4.hook: You hold h : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ and need AEStronglyMeasurable of a pointwise min, max, or constant-mixed variant of f (a truncation, a damping factor); hf.min, hf.max, hf.const all fail as 'invalid field'.
eab1f7e85ded352568db74c76daec1a1599639f4.name: aesm-is-an-exists-no-dot-fields-route-through-a-measurable-representative
eab1f7e85ded352568db74c76daec1a1599639f4.body: AEStronglyMeasurable is an Exists in Mathlib, so dot-notation min/max/const combinators do not exist for it. Obtain a strongly measurable representative first: obtain ⟨f', hf'm, hff⟩ := h gives Measurable f' and f =ᶠ[μ] f'. Build the variant from Measurable.min / Measurable.max / measurable_const on f', then return to the a.e. predicate with Measurable.aestronglyMeasurable.congr along hff. Note the congr takes the a.e.-equality with the representative version on the LEFT of the goal — supply hff, not symm hff, and rewrite backwards when the goal shape flips. Worked route witnessed by clean elaboration of a hard-truncation integrand.

e30e02ab5d8196ce8282a9a26c952b1939ddcf33.hook: A finite Galois correspondence has produced an abstract fixed field, but the goal asks to identify it with the intermediate field generated by one explicit element.
e30e02ab5d8196ce8282a9a26c952b1939ddcf33.name: identify a simple generated field from its fixing subgroup
e30e02ab5d8196ce8282a9a26c952b1939ddcf33.body: Characterize membership in the fixing subgroup of `IntermediateField.adjoin F {x}` by the single equation `σ x = x`: expand `IntermediateField.mem_fixingSubgroup_iff`, prove the reverse direction with `IntermediateField.adjoin_induction`, and use `σ.commutes` on base-field elements. Match that equation with the concrete permutation stabilizer under the automorphism-group equivalence, obtain equality of fixing subgroups by extensionality, and then rewrite the abstract fixed field using `IsGalois.fixedField_fixingSubgroup`. This avoids proving two inclusions between fields or doing invariant calculations. The certified residual witnessed the method for both several cubic generators and a quadratic generator in a finite Galois extension.

1b28ded99b1cd59edd1177b02042029e15d10690.hook: Any finite-group or finite-set Lean proof that mixes Nat.card and Fintype.card and finishes with decide or omega; symptoms are decide getting stuck on a trivial cardinality goal or omega reporting no constraints after a card rewrite.
1b28ded99b1cd59edd1177b02042029e15d10690.name: card-currency-natcard-decide-and-omega
1b28ded99b1cd59edd1177b02042029e15d10690.body: Card statements come in currencies (Nat.card, Fintype.card, Subgroup.index) and mixing them silently breaks finishers. Two witnessed instances: (1) `by decide` stalls on a goal like Nat.card (Fin n) = n because decide does not reduce Nat.card — use `by simp` for the pure-cardinality identity instead. (2) A leftover `rw [Nat.card_eq_fintype_card]` when the ambient lemmas are already stated in Nat.card leaves mismatched heads, and omega then sees no constraints; removing the redundant rewrite (choosing ONE currency for the whole branch) lets omega close both sides. Rule: pick the currency the area's lemmas use (group-theory card lemmas in Mathlib are Nat.card-based), and never insert a currency-bridging rewrite unless the goal actually displays the other currency.

c69ac38248307fa51e02fd2223a9ba1f6ac8d357.hook: Numeric Sylow arithmetic in Lean: omega ignores ModEq/dvd, decide refuses factorization, Sylow Nonempty needs inferInstance.
c69ac38248307fa51e02fd2223a9ba1f6ac8d357.name: numeric-sylow-arithmetic-omega-and-decide-traps
c69ac38248307fa51e02fd2223a9ba1f6ac8d357.body: PATTERN — deriving the numeric Sylow candidate set in Lean is pure Nat arithmetic, and the naive spellings all fail: omega cannot see through ModEq/divisibility hypotheses, decide will not reduce factorization instances, and Sylow types do not take field notation for Nonempty. The move: convert divisibility facts to bare membership in Nat.divisors, state congruences as plain % equations, and compute p-adic valuations by unfolding the definition rather than deciding it. LEAF — the exact repairs that compiled (exit 0, pinned Mathlib): (a) nonemptiness of a Sylow type: `(Sylow 5 G).nonempty` is invalid field notation — use `(inferInstance : Nonempty (Sylow 5 G))`. (b) `decide` does NOT fire on `(Nat.factorization 120) 5 = 1` or `padicValNat 5 120 = 1` (the Decidable instance will not reduce) — compute via `Nat.factorization_def`, `show 120 = 5 * 24`, `padicValNat.mul`, `simp`, then discharge the prime fact. (c) omega IGNORES hypotheses in Nat.ModEq form and in `a | n` form — obtain the quotient with `obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hdvd` and state the congruence as `a % 5 = 1`. (d) even `hq : a * q = 24` leaves omega stuck on a product of two variables — route through `Nat.mem_divisors` plus `Nat.divisors 24 = {1,2,3,4,6,8,12,24}` by `decide` (the explicit divisor Finset DOES decide), then `simp at hmem`. (e) `Nat.card (Sylow 5 G)` and `Fintype.card (Sylow 5 G)` are DIFFERENT omega atoms — bridge with `rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card] at h` before omega. MINED FROM a Student attempt that hit all five traps in sequence while compiling the Sylow-count enumeration for a group-order-120 non-simplicity bridge; each repair is problem-independent.

4212255aca16aa535bd14b4ef3dc5ea4e365cc0a.hook: Pinned-Mathlib names drift: primed variants vanish, implications become iffs, constants move to the root namespace.
4212255aca16aa535bd14b4ef3dc5ea4e365cc0a.name: pinned-mathlib-notation-and-arity-drift-check-with-compiler
4212255aca16aa535bd14b4ef3dc5ea4e365cc0a.body:
PATTERN - the obstacle. On a pinned Mathlib revision the names, namespaces, and lemma *kinds* drift from both current source and from memory of up-to-date Mathlib: constants move to the root namespace, primed variants vanish, and statements that used to be implications become iff lemmas. Applying them like the remembered shape produces unknown-constant errors or elaboration failures with metavariables.

PATTERN - the move. Treat the compiler error stream as the API reference for the pinned build; check each intended lemma once with `#check`/`example` before committing it to the long proof, and record the corrected kind (function vs instance vs iff) — an iff lemma needs `.mp`/`.mpr`, not application.

LEAF - the drifted facts (all repaired against the pinned build, exit 0): `Sylow.card_sylow_modEq_one` is unknown — the constant is unqualified at file top level: `card_sylow_modEq_one q G`. `Nat.Prime.dvd_mul hq hqdvd` and `Nat.dvd_prime hp h` are IFF lemmas here — use `.mp`. `Nat.mul_right_cancel'` does not exist — use `Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_right`, which wants `0 < p` (i.e. `hp.pos`), not `hp.ne_zero`. `Nat.dvd_sub'` does not exist — use plain `Nat.dvd_sub` with argument order `(a ∣ b) (a ∣ c) : a ∣ b - c`. `isNilpotent_of_finite_tfae` has no `Group.` prefix here, and `List.TFAE.out n1 n2` takes NO side-condition proofs (they are default `by rfl`; supplying `(by norm_num)` produces "expected type must not contain metavariables"); `.out 3 0` yields `l[0] ↔ l[3]`, so the direction you want may be `.mp`, not `.mpr`.

035b32ed44828b44aaf4db3c16a101f33de2d08f.hook: Retrieve when continuity, second derivatives, or decay of a parameterized half-line Green integral are blocked by an absolute value in the kernel and a moving improper domain.
035b32ed44828b44aaf4db3c16a101f33de2d08f.name: split absolute-value Green kernels before differentiating parameters
035b32ed44828b44aaf4db3c16a101f33de2d08f.body: Split the integral at the parameter so each absolute-value branch becomes an exponential weight. Express the operator using finite `intervalIntegral` primitives and one fixed `Ioi` integral; use `intervalIntegral.integral_hasDerivAt_right` for the moving endpoints, prove upper-tail identities by subtracting finite primitives from the fixed improper integral, and recombine with ring normalization. This presentation supports continuity, two differentiations, the Green ODE identity, the boundary value, and separate atTop tail estimates through APIs that are substantially easier to apply than direct parameter-integral differentiation.

5e8392553f2055cc96d75f0f3f43445b00dc69da.hook: when proving integrability of inner products or smul pairings of MemLp/Lp-typed functions in Mathlib
5e8392553f2055cc96d75f0f3f43445b00dc69da.name: memlp-integrability-via-lp-structure-roundtrip
5e8392553f2055cc96d75f0f3f43445b00dc69da.body: PATTERN: proving pointwise integrability of pairings of Lp-typed (MemLp) functions fails if you look for top-level lemmas like `integrable_inner` or `MeasureTheory.Integrable.congr_ae`; this Mathlib generation exposes inner-product integrability only on Lp-structured elements, so the route is to round-trip raw functions into the Lp structure, apply the structured lemma, and pull the statement back pointwise. LEAF: the working chain is `MemLp.toLp` → `L2.integrable_inner` → `integrable_congr`/`MemLp.coeFn_toLp` with `filter_upwards` to transfer a.e.; for multiplying an L2 function by an L∞ test function use `MemLp.smul` with the `HolderTriple 2 ⊤ 2` instance, argument order f first then the multiplier (swapped arguments surface as `MemLp (?m • f)`), and `eLpNorm_smul_le_mul_eLpNorm` for the norm side. Each wrong candidate name costs a probe compile — prefer this chain first. Mined from a weak-gradient term ∫ inner (grad_n − grad) (w • ψ) integrability obligation.

6752bd12b8dfe150b5f2626cdf38a0a62a4f75ac.hook: Evaluating an integral through exponential integrals on a half-line and the cotangent partial-fraction expansion, in a file that imports only the Cauchy integral module: the exponential-integral, cotangent, and integer-complement names come back as unknown identifiers although the library has them.
6752bd12b8dfe150b5f2626cdf38a0a62a4f75ac.name: half-line-series-route-needs-two-imports-beyond-the-cauchy-integral-module
6752bd12b8dfe150b5f2626cdf38a0a62a4f75ac.body:
PATTERN — the obstacle. A file set up for a contour argument imports `Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.CauchyIntegral` and nothing else. That closure carries the interval and set integral core, dominated convergence, geometric `HasSum`, and `Function.update` continuity — but not the improper-integral evaluation lemmas, not the cotangent expansion, and not the integer complement. An unknown-identifier error on one of those names is an import gap; it is not evidence that the lemma is absent. Grepping `.lake/packages/mathlib` for the declaration finds its module in seconds, while re-deriving the lemma costs the attempt.

PATTERN — the move. Add the two modules the real-axis series route depends on before writing any proof, and write the integer-complement set by its exported name.

LEAF — checked by elaboration at the pinned Mathlib, starting from the file's single import.
- Already available under `Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.CauchyIntegral`: `tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence`, `IntegrableOn.continuousWithinAt_Ici_primitive_Ioi`, `intervalIntegral.integral_Ioi_sub_Ioi`, `hasSum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one`, `tsum_geometric_of_norm_lt_one`, `continuousAt_update_same`, `HasDerivAt.tendsto_slope_zero`.
- `import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.ImproperIntegrals` brings `integral_exp_mul_complex_Ioi`, `integrableOn_exp_mul_Ioi`, `integrableOn_exp_mul_complex_Ioi`, and, transitively through `Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.IntegralEqImproper`, `intervalIntegral_tendsto_integral_Ioi`. All four are unknown without it.
- `import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Trigonometric.Cotangent` brings `cotTerm` (top level; there is no `Complex.cotTerm`), `tendsto_logDeriv_euler_cot_sub`, `summable_cotTerm`, `cot_series_rep'`, `cot_series_rep`, and, transitively through `Mathlib.Analysis.Complex.IntegerCompl`, `Complex.integerComplement` with `Complex.mem_integerComplement_iff`. All are unknown without it.
- `ℂ_ℤ` is `local notation` inside those Mathlib files and is not exported: in your own file write `integerComplement` under `open Complex` (or `Complex.integerComplement`) and state the hypothesis as `ω ∈ integerComplement`.
- With `open Complex MeasureTheory`, `integral_neg` is ambiguous between `intervalIntegral.integral_neg` and `MeasureTheory.integral_neg`; qualify it. The reflection change of variables is `intervalIntegral.integral_comp_neg`, and the namespace, if opened, is lowercase `intervalIntegral`.
- `Complex.cot` unfolds by `Complex.cot_eq_cos_div_sin`; a target written `π * cos (π * ω) / sin (π * ω)` is `π * cot (π * ω)` up to `mul_div_assoc`.

Provenance (mined-from): a principal-value integral whose file was written for a rectangular contour; the Student adopted the series route from the shelf and lost its first minutes to five unknown identifiers that were imports, not absences.

8f99cc308483e603b8f0c718daf6420bdc402e0b.hook: derivative of c over x^n via hasDerivAt_zpow: Int.cast value spelling and zpow_natCast rewrite trap
8f99cc308483e603b8f0c718daf6420bdc402e0b.name: zpow-cast-normalization-for-nat-exponent-derivatives
8f99cc308483e603b8f0c718daf6420bdc402e0b.body: Pattern: when differentiating a term written naturally as c / x^n (natural-number exponent) and the proof must go through Mathlib's integer-power derivative API, the obstruction is a cast/zpow normalization layer, not the analysis; budget explicit congr/convert steps for it instead of expecting a rewrite to fire. Leaf facts: hasDerivAt_zpow (m : Int) (x : field) (h : x != 0 or 0 <= m) : HasDerivAt (fun x => x^m) ((m : field) * x^(m-1)) x, in Mathlib Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/ZPow.lean. Three traps: (1) the disjunction hypothesis is the THIRD positional argument, after m and x - supplying a tactic proof in that slot makes Lean try to synthesize the Int exponent; (2) the derivative VALUE is spelled with an Int.cast, so a hand-written natural-cast or negated-natural value will not unify - restate the goal value with the Int cast first, then normalize with Int.cast_neg and mul_assoc; (3) rewriting with the reverse of zpow_natCast does NOT convert a natural-exponent power in the goal into zpow form, because the power and zpow instances do not match the rewrite pattern - an explicit congr/convert chain, or stating the derivative lemma over the zpow-shaped function and transporting, is required.

b3ecb37d44c8b9a7d59d6195853748c9a704765f.hook: A logarithmic integral uses an infinite penalty at zeros, and finiteness of its negative-part lintegral must be converted into an almost-everywhere nonvanishing hypothesis before ordinary real integration APIs apply.
b3ecb37d44c8b9a7d59d6195853748c9a704765f.name: finite negative logarithmic part excludes zeros almost everywhere
b3ecb37d44c8b9a7d59d6195853748c9a704765f.body: Make the extended-valued penalty AEMeasurable on the restricted measure by replacing the original function with its measurable representative, proving measurability of the zero-test `ite`, and transferring back by almost-everywhere congruence. Then `ae_lt_top'` turns a non-top lintegral into pointwise finiteness almost everywhere; at a zero the penalty simplifies to top, so that finite-value fact yields nonvanishing. This is the bridge needed before rewriting the custom negative part as `ENNReal.ofReal (-log |f|)` and applying positive/negative-part integral identities.

70ce298c61556d791c29b02fce370934127bedbb.hook: Boundary hypotheses are given as bounds or convergence at a parametrized point of a circle for the parameter in an open interval, while the library's Cauchy integral formula produces a contour integral, so the estimate and the formula are integrals against different measures.
70ce298c61556d791c29b02fce370934127bedbb.name: convert-the-contour-integral-to-a-parameter-set-integral-before-estimating-boundary-data
70ce298c61556d791c29b02fce370934127bedbb.body:
PATTERN. In problems where the data on a circle is handed to you as a parametrized family over an open real interval — open, typically, because a majorant blows up at the endpoint — the contour integral the library gives you and the integral your hypotheses talk about are not the same object. Do not try to carry the estimate on the contour side, and do not try to restate the hypotheses as contour data. Convert the contour integral ONCE, at the top, into a set integral over the same open parameter interval the hypotheses use, and then do every estimate downstream in parameter space. The payoff is that the kernel and the boundary function then live under one measure, so an L1 error bound on the boundary becomes a single application of the norm-of-integral estimate, and the kernel factor can be pulled out as a constant on each compact subset. Getting the measure alignment right first is what makes the analytic estimate short; attempting the estimate before the alignment produces goals that no rewrite closes.

LEAF. The conversion is three rewrites in this order. First unfold the circle integral, which is by definition an interval integral of deriv (circleMap c R) t smul q (circleMap c R t). Second, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le (with the positivity of the upper endpoint, e.g. Real.two_pi_pos.le) turns the oriented interval integral into a set integral over Ioc. Third, Measure.restrict_congr_set Ioo_ae_eq_Ioc.symm moves it to Ioo, matching the open interval of the hypotheses; the endpoint is null so nothing is lost, and this is the step that is easy to miss because Ioc and Ioo goals look interchangeable until a hypothesis fails to apply. deriv_circleMap and circleMap_zero then evaluate the Jacobian factor explicitly (for the unit circle centred at 0: exp (I * t) * I). The Cauchy formula to convert is DifferentiableOn.circleIntegral_sub_inv_smul: it wants differentiability on the CLOSED ball and the point in the OPEN ball, and it returns (2 * pi * I) smul f w, so afterwards divide by that constant with field_simp plus a nonvanishing proof assembled from Complex.ofReal_ne_zero.mpr Real.pi_ne_zero and Complex.I_ne_zero.

d932a9c7d7e13296a9425e49c1518a5297a5ecdd.hook: An invertible linear map has a commuting additive semisimple--nilpotent decomposition, and a proof needs a unique commuting semisimple--unipotent factorization.
d932a9c7d7e13296a9425e49c1518a5297a5ecdd.name: normalize-an-additive-jordan-decomposition-into-commuting-multiplicative-factors
d932a9c7d7e13296a9425e49c1518a5297a5ecdd.body: First show the additive semisimple part `S` is bijective: a vector in its zero eigenspace lies in the generalized zero eigenspace of the original automorphism, so some power of the injective automorphism kills it only if it is zero; finite-dimensional injective/surjective equivalence supplies bijectivity. Form `se := LinearEquiv.ofBijective S hb` and normalize with `U := se.symm * T`. Its difference from the identity simplifies to `se.symm.toLinearMap * N`; prove the inverse commutes with `N`, then use `Commute.isNilpotent_mul_left` for unipotence. For uniqueness, turn competing factors `A,B` into additive data with `M := B.toLinearMap - 1` and `D := A.toLinearMap * M`; commutation and nilpotence make `T = A + D` another additive decomposition. Additive uniqueness identifies `A` with `se`, and group cancellation identifies `B` with `U`. This replaces a search for a packaged multiplicative Jordan theorem with a transport through the already available additive uniqueness theorem.

81a1a168d5cc3bd6bd98e1665836d8f313f1c4fd.hook: applying a Mathlib lemma stated with algebraMap k (End k V) mu when your term is written as mu • 1, or rewriting under a dependent MapsTo proof argument
81a1a168d5cc3bd6bd98e1665836d8f313f1c4fd.name: restate-in-algebramap-spelling-with-show-when-rw-breaks-the-motive
81a1a168d5cc3bd6bd98e1665836d8f313f1c4fd.body: ARC (level api, witnessed). Mathlib states the restrict-to-invariant-subspace nilpotency lemmas (e.g. isNilpotent_restrict_maxGenEigenspace_sub_algebraMap) with algebraMap k (End k V) mu, not mu • 1. Rewriting your goal with rw [Algebra.algebraMap_eq_smul_one] fails with motive-is-not-type-correct when a MapsTo proof argument depends on the rewritten term. The working move is a 'show' that restates the goal in the algebraMap spelling, keeping the dependent proof term untouched. Separately, Set.MapsTo membership goals need rw [SetLike.mem_coe] before submodule membership lemmas fire. Also: IsAlgClosed on a field transfers through the standard reductions to invariant submodules and quotients, so it does not need re-proving per restriction.

00d5d9ae2164b3030702a427f9f11a0c29fbfcbe.hook: considering whether a Bochner integral's junk value for non-integrable functions can discharge an approximation or identity clause that looks too strong
00d5d9ae2164b3030702a427f9f11a0c29fbfcbe.name: junk-value-integral-loophole-dies-when-integrability-is-forced
00d5d9ae2164b3030702a427f9f11a0c29fbfcbe.body: Before hunting for a semantic loophole in an integral goal, check whether the surrounding hypotheses force genuine integrability. A typical false hope: an epsilon-approximation clause 'integral |u - phi|^2 < epsilon' might be attacked via the junk value Mathlib assigns when a function is not integrable (integral_undef). The loophole closes when the statement also hypothesises u is L2 (or measurable with an Lp bound) and phi is bounded with compact support inside a finite-measure set: then |u - phi|^2 is genuinely integrable, the integral is real, and no junk value is reachable. The reusable check: enumerate which hypothesis (measurability of the product, finiteness of the measure, boundedness of one factor) rules out non-integrability; only if none does is the junk-value route live.

19fb2e9b241bbe1dad92a6199c50d78cf31636ed.hook: The goal asks for the action of an arbitrary automorphism, while the available pointwise theorem describes the automorphism obtained by applying the inverse of a classification equivalence to an exponent.
19fb2e9b241bbe1dad92a6199c50d78cf31636ed.name: orient-kummer-automorphisms-by-rewriting-through-the-equivalence
19fb2e9b241bbe1dad92a6199c50d78cf31636ed.body: Let e be the automorphism-to-exponent equivalence. For arbitrary sigma, rewrite sigma as e.symm (e sigma) with e.symm_apply_apply, then specialize the inverse-direction action theorem to (Multiplicative.toAdd (e sigma)).val. A final simplification of e and Algebra.smul_def aligns the theorem with the pointwise multiplication goal. This uses the equivalence's packaged surjectivity and avoids manually proving that a separately chosen exponent represents sigma.

02fc96b0aa79cef22b74d1b7fdee675a78c01b95.hook: An analytic function on an open set strictly containing the closed unit disk must have Maclaurin coefficients tending to zero, and a naive search for a coefficient-decay lemma finds nothing directly usable.
02fc96b0aa79cef22b74d1b7fdee675a78c01b95.name: cauchy-estimate-on-larger-sphere-gives-geometric-coefficient-decay
02fc96b0aa79cef22b74d1b7fdee675a78c01b95.body: Leaf of math-formalization/compact-thickening-upgrades-pointwise-analyticity. Trigger: goal Tendsto (fun n => norm (iteratedDeriv n u 0) / n.factorial) atTop (nhds 0) from AnalyticOn u D with closedBall 0 1 subset D, D open. Move: (1) obtain delta from IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open on the closed unit ball, then cthickening_closedBall rewrites the thickening as closedBall 0 (1 + delta) subset D; (2) AnalyticOn.differentiableOn.diffContOnCl_ball upgrades to DiffContOnCl on ball 0 (1 + delta); (3) the constant C comes from compactness of the larger sphere: (isCompact_sphere 0 (1 + delta)).image_of_continuousOn of the boundary restriction, then isBounded_iff_forall_norm_le; (4) Complex.norm_iteratedDeriv_le_of_forall_mem_sphere_norm_le bounds each iterated derivative by C on that sphere, so the coefficient norm is at most C / (1 + delta) ^ n; (5) finish with tendsto_pow_atTop_nhds_zero_of_abs_lt_one on 1 / (1 + delta) and squeeze_zero'. Why it works: the thickening turns a boundary-touching hypothesis into a strictly larger radius, and Cauchy estimates on the larger sphere give geometric decay, which is exactly the squeeze needed; the whole chain is Mathlib-grounded, no artifact-local lemma required.

ca884cf5b1d225d13daae302d21827a1e20844f8.hook: A variational remainder needs a zero-boundary inequality between the integral of v squared and the integral of its derivative squared, but the exact Poincare or Wirtinger theorem is unavailable or has an awkward interface.
ca884cf5b1d225d13daae302d21827a1e20844f8.name: prove a short-interval Wirtinger bound from endpoint FTC estimates
ca884cf5b1d225d13daae302d21827a1e20844f8.body: Derive v(t)=integral from the left endpoint and also v(t)=-integral to the right endpoint using intervalIntegral.integral_deriv_eq_sub. Cauchy-Schwarz gives v(t)^2 at most t times the total derivative energy on the left and at most (L-t) times that energy on the right. Split the interval at L/2 and integrate the corresponding bounds to obtain integral v^2 at most L^2/4 times integral (v')^2. When L^2/4 is at most 1, this is the weaker unit-constant bound needed for nonnegativity. A self-contained integral Cauchy bound can be proved by integrating (f-c)^2 with c equal to the average.

65f93d745b2204aec53b5e218b9b963a112547bf.hook: A real or conjugate-symmetric weak formulation must be tested at one complex Fourier frequency, but an admissible probe necessarily also has support at its involutive partner.
65f93d745b2204aec53b5e218b9b963a112547bf.name: Reduce a conjugate-paired Fourier probe to a two-point sum
65f93d745b2204aec53b5e218b9b963a112547bf.body: For a non-fixed frequency k, build the admissible probe as the sum of two lp.single terms at k and -k, scaling each stored coefficient so the normalized physical coefficients are q and star q. Prove a pointwise if/else formula for the probe, then prove its physical coefficient is zero outside the Finset {k, -k}. Rewrite each tsum with tsum_eq_sum using that outside-support proof; the weak identity becomes an explicit two-term equality. The key side condition is k != -k, derived from k != 0 for integer-pair frequencies. This isolates the finite-support bookkeeping from the later choice q = 1 or q = Complex.I.

44ca5f0a8c984598fcc2cbf6bec726a56fb34977.hook: An explicitly enumerated typewriter or partition sequence must revisit every point at arbitrarily late indices, but the global index hides the stage and cell coordinates.
44ca5f0a8c984598fcc2cbf6bec726a56fb34977.name: Invert a diagonal cell enumeration at a chosen stage
44ca5f0a8c984598fcc2cbf6bec726a56fb34977.body: Choose a stage n large enough for both the desired index cutoff and the desired height. Recover the cell containing x by j = floor (n*x) away from the right endpoint, using j = n-1 when x = 1. Then encode the stage coordinates with the pairing map, for example k = pair (n-1-j) j. The inverse-pair equations recover stage n and position j; a lower bound of the form a+b <= pair a b makes k cofinal. The endpoint split is essential because floor (n*1) = n lies outside the cells indexed below n. In Lean, Nat.floor_le and Nat.lt_floor_add_one prove the two cell inequalities, while the endpoint branch is discharged by cast subtraction and division lemmas.

4dca73c3080fd7886257e866333ada2f86340a5d.hook: Justifying a series/integral or series/limit interchange where a naive term-for-term rearrangement of the infinite families is invalid, e.g. conditionally indexed or reflected pairings where reindexing shifts the summation index.
4dca73c3080fd7886257e866333ada2f86340a5d.name: interchange-limits-via-finite-partial-sums-endpoint
4dca73c3080fd7886257e866333ada2f86340a5d.body: Do not rearrange the infinite series directly; the invalid move observed and rejected was a term-for-term shifted pairing of the two families. The working protocol: prove each FINITE original-index partial sum equals a target partial sum minus an explicit endpoint term; prove the endpoint term tends to zero separately; pass to the limit only at the end. The interchange then needs only finite identities plus one vanishing-endpoint limit, followed by dominated convergence with a majorant uniform in the partial-sum index, obtained from the exact finite geometric-remainder factorization of the partial sums rather than from any infinite rearrangement. This converts a subtle rearrangement question into elementary finite algebra plus one limit.

bc4db2ba9fdd9f58d77c8e95197ff7bc5f78d322.hook: Needing a step function within ε of an L¹ function in integral norm on a finite restricted measure, when the approximation result available gives only a pointwise (or off-a-null-set) bound.
bc4db2ba9fdd9f58d77c8e95197ff7bc5f78d322.name: dyadic-step-density-from-pointwise-estimate-via-integral-mono-ae
bc4db2ba9fdd9f58d77c8e95197ff7bc5f78d322.body: Move: convert a pointwise bound to an L¹ bound with integral_mono_ae, never by trying to integrate the pointwise statement by hand. Concretely: obtain a pointwise |g t − s t| ≤ ε/2 holding on the restricted interval away from a null endpoint; package Integrable of |g − s| via (hgint.sub hs).abs with step-function integrability from integrable_finset_sum and (integrable_const _).indicator measurableSet_Ico; take the constant ε/2 as integrable_const; the a.e. hypotheses come from ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_Icc plus ae_iff for the missing endpoint singleton; then integral_mono_ae plus integral_const and measure.real univ = 1 (for volume.restrict (Icc 0 1): simp [Measure.real, Real.volume_Icc]) gives the integral bound with no loss. Chain two approximation layers with the triangle inequality inside the integral (abs_sub_le, integral_mono_ae, integral_add) so each layer needs only half the budget.

52e27064d926206ea089a8b88c89780a6af883f1.hook: An integral formula is only justified for functions satisfying a linearity-stable smoothness-and-support predicate, but the goal requires a linear map on the ambient function space.
52e27064d926206ea089a8b88c89780a6af883f1.name: extend-an-integral-functional-from-the-test-function-submodule
52e27064d926206ea089a8b88c89780a6af883f1.body: Form the admissible functions as a `Submodule`, define the formula as a linear map there, and prove its laws with `integral_add` and `Integrable.integral_smul` after exposing the subtype coercions with `change`. Then use `LinearMap.exists_extend`; for an admissible ambient function, package it as a subtype and specialize the extension equality with `DFunLike.congr_fun`. This certified route avoids trying to define possibly nonintegrable ambient integrals and still provides the required ambient linear map.

7d5a22869bcbbbd6fcc805ae2f6c1b10b3b9f1e7.hook: A finite-group action on an abstract finite type is known to be even, and the goal asks for a surjective homomorphism to the standard alternating group on `Fin n` while retaining the action kernel.
7d5a22869bcbbbd6fcc805ae2f6c1b10b3b9f1e7.name: upgrade-an-even-action-to-a-standard-alternating-quotient
7d5a22869bcbbbd6fcc805ae2f6c1b10b3b9f1e7.body: Restrict `MulAction.toPermHom` with `MonoidHom.codRestrict` to the alternating subgroup using the pointwise evenness proof. Prove the restricted kernel equals the original kernel by extensionality and `simp`. Compute the restricted range cardinality from `ker.card_mul_index` and `Subgroup.index_ker`; if it equals the finite alternating target's cardinality, use `Subgroup.eq_top_of_card_eq` and `MonoidHom.range_eq_top` to obtain surjectivity. Only then choose `Fintype.equivOfCardEq` from the abstract action type to `Fin n` and compose with `Equiv.altCongrHom.toMonoidHom`; its injectivity gives kernel equality by extensionality. This avoids rebuilding the action on `Fin n` and keeps the kernel calculation on the natural action type. Mined from a residual requiring a standard alternating quotient from an even Sylow conjugation action.

2fb2931f4e76db6440e5a768526c9efe24c59348.hook: The degree of a simple adjoin K⟮x⟯ has no finrank_eq lemma — read it off the adjoin's PowerBasis.
2fb2931f4e76db6440e5a768526c9efe24c59348.name: read-simple-adjoin-degree-from-its-power-basis
2fb2931f4e76db6440e5a768526c9efe24c59348.body: PATTERN — the obstacle. The degree of a simple intermediate-field adjoin over its base, `Module.finrank K (adjoin K {x}) = (minpoly K x).natDegree`, is not a named Mathlib lemma: `IntermediateField.adjoin.finrank_eq` and `finrank_adjoin_simple` are unknown identifiers, `exact?` returns nothing, and `PowerBasis.finrank` alone seems unusable because no PowerBasis for an adjoin appears to be advertised. The natural reaction is to assemble an ad-hoc power basis by hand (algebraMap/aeval image argument), which costs a compile cycle per wrong guess. PATTERN — the move. The fact is packaged, but as a PowerBasis rather than a finrank lemma: `IntermediateField.adjoin.powerBasis` (given `IsIntegral K x`) is defined with `dim := (minpoly K x).natDegree`, and `PowerBasis.finrank : Module.finrank R S = pb.dim` converts it. Over a field base, integrality of an algebraic element is available as an instance, so for a root of any nonzero polynomial the hypothesis is free. LEAF — names and exact shape (verified to elaborate against the pinned Mathlib, import-all): `IntermediateField.adjoin.powerBasis : {x : L} → IsIntegral K x → PowerBasis K ↥K⟮x⟯` — the coercion target is the adjoin subtype, so state the goal on `↥K⟮x⟯` or reach it by finrank congruence. `PowerBasis.finrank (pb : PowerBasis R S) : Module.finrank R S = pb.dim` — needs `[StrongRankCondition R]`, automatic for a field. Two-line close, which compiles verbatim: `have := (IntermediateField.adjoin.powerBasis hx).finrank; simpa using this` where the goal is `Module.finrank K (IntermediateField.adjoin K ({x} : Set L)) = (minpoly K x).natDegree`; `simpa` discharges the subtype-coercion mismatch.

b9109b71fe295fb3b1a17ce5a3f601736b68c569.hook: Intersections of ambient Sylow p-subgroups with a normal subgroup must be shown to be exactly the Sylow p-subgroups of that normal subgroup, or the Sylow count of the normal subgroup must divide the ambient Sylow count.
b9109b71fe295fb3b1a17ce5a3f601736b68c569.name: sylow-trace-restriction-to-normal-subgroup-via-transporter
b9109b71fe295fb3b1a17ce5a3f601736b68c569.body: PATTERN — why Sylow restriction to a normal subgroup has no one-liner. The natural statement — for K ⊴ G, the intersections P ⊓ K of ambient Sylow p-subgroups are exactly the Sylow p-subgroups of K — is NOT packaged. Verified against Mathlib source: `Sylow.exists_comap_subtype_eq` gives only the forward direction; `Sylow.comapOfKerIsPGroup` and `Sylow.comapOfInjective` both hypothesize P ≤ φ.range and do not yield the trace equality; `IsPGroup.inf_normalizer_sylow` treats normalizers only. The reverse direction is a transporter argument: extend a Sylow of K to an ambient Sylow, conjugate that extension to the given ambient Sylow, and use normality of K to see the conjugation restricts to an automorphism of K carrying one trace to the other. LEAF — spellings for the pieces that DO exist: `Sylow.isPretransitive_of_finite` (pretransitivity of conjugation on ambient Sylows of a finite group — this is the conjugation step), `Sylow.coe_smul` (how conjugation acts on the coercion), `Sylow.card_eq_index_normalizer` (counting via normalizer index). The hand-built part is restricting the ambient conjugation automorphism to K (it lies in the normalizer since K is normal) and transporting through the `Subgroup.map` / `⊓` encoding; for the counting corollary, make the trace map's fibers equicardinal via the transporter action on each fiber and finish with `Nat.card_congr` / `Nat.card_sigma` style counting. MINED FROM a Student attempt that verified the negative API facts by source inspection and identified `Sylow.isPretransitive_of_finite` as the intended route without exercising them in budget. PATTERN-ID COINED (new) because no existing pattern in the mathematics libraries covers group-theoretic Sylow restriction; nearest existing patterns concern fiber-counting (`equicardinal-fibers-from-equivariant-transitive-action`) but not the normality/transporter restriction step.

4474f1fa761f102454508fd8bfbfd08b3c36733e.hook: a cardinality fact proved as a Nat.card statement will not rewrite against a goal stated with Fintype.card on the same subtype
4474f1fa761f102454508fd8bfbfd08b3c36733e.name: one-cardinality-currency-per-proof
4474f1fa761f102454508fd8bfbfd08b3c36733e.body: Nat.card and Fintype.card statements about the same subtype carry different (data, not proof-irrelevant) Fintype instances, so rw/simp across them fails with instance mismatches. State every card equality in the proof in one currency and bridge deliberately with Nat.card_eq_fintype_card rewritten in one fixed direction, folding Finset.image-card arguments into that currency. Related trap: Nat.card_mono is about Set.Finite subsets and rejects a Subgroup.inclusion argument; use card divisibility (Subgroup.card_dvd_of_le) instead of monotonicity.

86c82c5371e1b14134083539b2e9b747cdb7632c.hook: A base-ring linear map or equivalence intertwines the distinguished operators defining a finitely generated algebra action, but the goal requires linearity over the whole algebra.
86c82c5371e1b14134083539b2e9b747cdb7632c.name: upgrade-generated-algebra-linearity-from-generator-commutation
86c82c5371e1b14134083539b2e9b747cdb7632c.body: Express each algebra scalar as a base-scalar polynomial in the generators, then prove scalar compatibility from additivity, base linearity, and commutation with every generator. For a one-generator square-zero quotient, coordinates have the form a + b*x, so `add_smul`, `mul_smul`, base-field linearity, and the identity f (x • v) = x • f v close `map_smul'`. If the underlying map is an equivalence, derive the inverse's base linearity and generator commutation by applying injectivity of the forward equivalence, rather than reproving them from coordinates. Scope: modules over a generated algebra. Before: build the target algebra-linear equivalence directly from an adapted basis. After: first construct a base-linear conjugacy of the generator action, then upgrade it to an algebra-linear equivalence. Level: domain. Confidence: high. Evidence: the certified quotient-module classification head compiles this upgrade after constructing a conjugacy of the square-zero action.

adaef06ad13f83af9fb7fd26958371ea042dbc06.hook: MemLp of an indicator power tail |x|^(-s) on 1 ≤ |x| for Lebesgue volume: integrableOn_Ici_rpow_iff does NOT exist — use integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_iff / integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_of_lt on Ioi 1 and cover the endpoint by ae-congruence or Ici = Ioi ∪ {1}; reflect the negative tail with Integrable.comp_neg or measurePreserving_neg.integrableOn_comp_preimage measurableEmbedding_neg; prove measurability with Measurable.ite because fun_prop fails on ite; get the power tail integral divergence conjunct by restricting to Ioi 1 and reading a < -1 back from integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_iff
adaef06ad13f83af9fb7fd26958371ea042dbc06.body:
RESIDUAL: `MemLp (fun x : ℝ => if 1 ≤ |x| then |x| ^ (-s) else 0) (ENNReal.ofReal p) volume` and `¬MemLp …  (ENNReal.ofReal q) volume` on ℝ with Lebesgue measure, given the scalar thresholds `-s * p < -1` and `-1 ≤ -s * q`. Three obstacles hit both independent closes on 2026-08-24 (Mathlib as pinned by apm-lean f7de6887): a phantom lemma name, the symmetric negative tail, and measurability of the `if`.

(1) THE NAMED LEMMA DOES NOT EXIST. Boundary comments cite `integrableOn_Ici_rpow_iff`; Mathlib only has the open-interval form `integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_iff (hc : 0 < c) : IntegrableOn (fun x => x ^ a) (Ioi c) ↔ a < -1` (Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/ImproperIntegrals.lean) and `integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_of_lt (ha : a < -1) (hc : 0 < c)`. Search for the `Ioi` name. Two ways to cover the closed tail `1 ≤ x`: (a) write the integrand as `(Ioi 1).indicator (fun x => x ^ a)`, pass IntegrableOn → Integrable by `(integrable_indicator_iff measurableSet_Ioi).2`, and absorb the single point `x = 1` by ae-congruence (`filter_upwards` with `∀ᵐ x, x ≠ 1`, obtained from `simp [ae_iff, measure_singleton]`); or (b) `Ici 1 = Ioi 1 ∪ {1}`, `integrableOn_union`, and `IntegrableOn.of_measure_zero (by simp)` for the singleton.

(2) NEGATIVE TAIL `x ≤ -1`. Do not integrate again — reflect the positive tail. Shortest: `hpos.comp_neg` for `hpos : Integrable ((Ioi 1).indicator …)`, then `(hpos.add hneg).congr` with a `by_cases 1 < x` / `by_cases 1 < -x` split using `abs_of_pos` / `abs_of_neg`. Alternative that also compiles: `((Measure.measurePreserving_neg volume).integrableOn_comp_preimage measurableEmbedding_neg).mpr hpos` — the `MeasurableEmbedding Neg.neg` argument is REQUIRED (omitting it is a type error), the lemma is an iff so choose `.mpr`, and the preimage `Neg.neg ⁻¹' Ici 1` must be rewritten to `Iic (-1)` by `ext x; simp; constructor <;> intro h <;> linarith`. Reassemble over `Iic (-1) ∪ Ici 1` with `integrableOn_union` and `MeasurableSet.union measurableSet_Iic measurableSet_Ici`.

(3) MEASURABILITY OF THE `if`. `fun_prop` fails on the unfolded `ite` ("No theorems found for ite"). Use `Measurable.ite (measurableSet_le measurable_const measurable_abs) hbranch measurable_const`, where the rpow branch is `by fun_prop` on `|x| ^ a`, or `measurable_of_continuousOn_compl_singleton 0` with `continuous_abs.continuousAt.rpow_const (Or.inl (abs_ne_zero.mpr hx))`. Then `.aestronglyMeasurable` is the first argument of `integrable_norm_rpow_iff`.

DIVERGENCE CONJUNCT: from `hmem : MemLp f (ENNReal.ofReal q) volume` take `(integrable_norm_rpow_iff … ).mpr hmem`, `rw [ENNReal.toReal_ofReal hq0.le]`, restrict with `.integrableOn` to `Ioi 1`, convert by `IntegrableOn.congr_fun` (needs `measurableSet_Ioi`) to `x ^ (-s * q)` using `abs_of_pos`, then `(integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_iff zero_lt_one).1` returns `-s * q < -1`, contradicting the scalar bound. The norm-power collapse is the same `Real.norm_eq_abs` / `abs_of_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg (abs_nonneg x) _)` / `(Real.rpow_mul (abs_nonneg x) _ _).symm` chain as in the sequence case; on the `else` branch use `Real.zero_rpow hp.ne'`.

4660a9f12701c78bef64c7bd93526914a7b08ef7.hook: Exact Mathlib signatures and file paths (pinned mathlib 5ee50502 / apm-lean f7de6887) for the MemLp power-law bridges: integrable_norm_rpow_iff (L1Space/Integrable.lean:224); integrable_count_iff gives Summable (‖f ·‖) NOT Summable f (line 757); the generic summable_nat_add_iff is the to_additive of multipliable_nat_add_iff in Topology/Algebra/InfiniteSum/NatInt.lean:221 (the nonrec NNReal copy in Topology/Instances/NNReal/Lemmas.lean:187 is not the one for real sequences); Real.summable_nat_rpow in Analysis/PSeries.lean:305; integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_iff / integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_of_lt in Analysis/SpecialFunctions/ImproperIntegrals.lean:132-136; Integrable.comp_neg, Measure.measurePreserving_neg, measurableEmbedding_neg are to_additive of comp_inv / measurePreserving_inv / measurableEmbedding_inv in MeasureTheory/Group — stop grepping for the declaring files, write the proof; the workspace build is warm (about 3 s per compile)
4660a9f12701c78bef64c7bd93526914a7b08ef7.body:
WHY THIS CARD: attempt 2 on this residual spent its whole turn grepping Mathlib for the declaring file of `summable_nat_add_iff` and never edited the proof. Every entry below was read from the pinned Mathlib checkout (lake-manifest rev 5ee50502, apm-lean f7de6887) on 2026-08-25; paths are relative to `.lake/packages/mathlib/`. Stop grepping — these are the declarations.

1. `integrable_norm_rpow_iff {f : α → β} {p : ℝ≥0∞} (hf : AEStronglyMeasurable f μ) (p_zero : p ≠ 0) (p_top : p ≠ ∞) : Integrable (fun x => ‖f x‖ ^ p.toReal) μ ↔ MemLp f p μ` — Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/L1Space/Integrable.lean:224 (a `lemma` in namespace MeasureTheory). Pass `(p := ENNReal.ofReal p)` explicitly.

2. `integrable_count_iff : Integrable f Measure.count ↔ Summable (‖f ·‖)` — same file, line 757. CORRECTION to the sibling counting-measure memory: the right-hand side is summability of the NORM `fun n => ‖f n‖`, not of `f`. For the integrand `fun n => ‖f n‖ ^ p` the goal after `rw [integrable_count_iff]` is therefore `Summable (fun n => ‖‖f n‖ ^ p‖)` — that outer norm is why the collapse lemma has the double `‖‖…‖ ^ r‖` shape; discharge it with `Real.norm_eq_abs` and `abs_of_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) _)`.

3. `summable_nat_add_iff {f : ℕ → G} (k : ℕ) : (Summable fun n => f (n + k)) ↔ Summable f` for a topological additive group G — generated by `@[to_additive]` from `multipliable_nat_add_iff` at Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/InfiniteSum/NatInt.lean:221, so grep for the MULTIPLICATIVE name. Use `(summable_nat_add_iff (f := fun n : ℕ => (n : ℝ) ^ s) 1)`; write `_root_.summable_nat_add_iff` if the `nonrec` NNReal copy at Mathlib/Topology/Instances/NNReal/Lemmas.lean:187 (stated for `ℕ → ℝ≥0`, NOT for real sequences) shadows it.

4. `Real.summable_nat_rpow {p : ℝ} : Summable (fun n => (n : ℝ) ^ p : ℕ → ℝ) ↔ p < -1` — Mathlib/Analysis/PSeries.lean:305 (namespace Real). Line 432 of the same file shows the canonical shift idiom `rw [← summable_nat_add_iff 1]`.
