5. `integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_of_lt {a c : ℝ} (ha : a < -1) (hc : 0 < c) : IntegrableOn (fun t : ℝ => t ^ a) (Ioi c)` (line 132) and `integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_iff {s t : ℝ} (ht : 0 < t) : IntegrableOn (fun x => x ^ s) (Ioi t) ↔ s < -1` (line 136) — Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/ImproperIntegrals.lean. No `Ici` variant exists.

6. Reflection of the negative tail — all three are `@[to_additive]` names, so grep the multiplicative parent: `Integrable.comp_neg` ← `Integrable.comp_inv [IsInvInvariant μ] (hf : Integrable f μ) : Integrable (fun t => f t⁻¹) μ`, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/Integral.lean:35; `Measure.measurePreserving_neg` ← `measurePreserving_inv (μ) [IsInvInvariant μ] : MeasurePreserving Inv.inv μ μ`, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/Measure.lean:331; `measurableEmbedding_neg` ← `measurableEmbedding_inv`, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Group/Arithmetic.lean:386. Then `MeasurePreserving.integrableOn_comp_preimage (h₁ : MeasurePreserving e μ ν) (h₂ : MeasurableEmbedding e) : IntegrableOn (f ∘ e) (e ⁻¹' s) μ ↔ IntegrableOn f s ν`, Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/IntegrableOn.lean:319.

e5b6d7165121e3d0b7a6a8baac96326fce4d618e.hook: when constructing an element of a bundled smooth compactly-supported function space and a residual note or memory says to route through fixed-support staging and inclusion constructors

e5b6d7165121e3d0b7a6a8baac96326fce4d618e.body: TestFunction is a plain four-field structure (function, smoothness, support, topological-support condition); when the support condition is against the full space, the anonymous constructor closes each field directly and the top-open-set field is discharged by subset of the whole space. 5ae986bc45726f829e161a8846d5b33d28be2b50.hook: A piecewise conjugate reflection is continuous across the real axis and holomorphic away from it, but no library theorem directly proves differentiability on the seam.
5ae986bc45726f829e161a8846d5b33d28be2b50.name: Morera reflection through rectangle splitting
5ae986bc45726f829e161a8846d5b33d28be2b50.body: Define the reflection by `if 0 ≤ z.im then f z else star (f (star z))`. Prove continuity by `ContinuousOn.union_of_isClosed` on closed upper and lower half-domains. For holomorphicity, express the rectangle boundary as `wedgeIntegral z w F + wedgeIntegral w z F`; rectangles contained in one half-plane vanish by `Complex.integral_boundary_rect_eq_zero_of_continuousOn_of_differentiableOn`, while a crossing rectangle is split at imaginary part zero using `intervalIntegral.integral_add_adjacent_intervals`. The two seam edges cancel, yielding `IsConservativeOn`; then apply `isConservativeOn_and_continuousOn_iff_isDifferentiableOn`. This is the constructive route when an exact Schwarz-reflection gluing theorem is absent.

03af359a77420b93e3d0c2c1debd2edce1f6c0f8.hook: when a base-linear map's kernel must equal a polynomial ideal to transport a quotient's cardinality, and restrictScalars/toSubmodule coercion walls appear
03af359a77420b93e3d0c2c1debd2edce1f6c0f8.name: quotient-card-via-coefficient-kernel-membership-bridge
03af359a77420b93e3d0c2c1debd2edce1f6c0f8.body: PATTERN — when a quotient-ring cardinality or quotient-module equivalence is transported across the kernel of a base-field linear map (e.g. a coefficient map p ↦ (coeff p 0, coeff p 1)), the kernel is a Submodule over the BASE ring while the quotient is by an Ideal over the BIG ring, and trying to coerce one structure onto the other's scalar ring is an elaboration trap, not a mathematical difficulty: `Submodule.toSubmodule` does not exist in Mathlib (the projection goes the other way, `Ideal.toSubmodule : Ideal R → Submodule R R`), and a partially-applied `Submodule.restrictScalars (R := base) I` mis-unifies the intermediate scalar ring and reports 'failed to synthesize Semiring ↥I', which reads like a missing-instance problem and invites retrying instances forever. The move that works: bridge at the SET-membership level — lower the ideal to a base-submodule with BOTH scalar rings explicit (`Submodule.restrictScalars (R := k) (S := A) I`), then prove the kernel equality with `Submodule.ext_iff` where each membership obligation is discharged by the ideal's own API. LEAF — spellings: `Ideal.mem_span_singleton` (a ∈ span {r} ↔ ∃ b, a = b * r, commutative ring) converts ideal membership into an existential; `Polynomial.X_pow_dvd_iff` (X ^ n ∣ f ↔ ∀ d < n, coeff d = 0) converts divisibility by a power of X into vanishing low coefficients, which is exactly the kernel condition of a truncation-to-low-coefficients map; with the kernel equality in hand, `LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange` (or `Submodule.quotKerEquivOfSurjective`) transports `Nat.card` of the quotient to the target, closed by `Nat.card_prod` and `Nat.card_zmod`. Scope: modules and quotients over polynomial rings / finite-dimensional algebras. Before: attempt a ring-hom first-isomorphism route (fails when the target ring is only a product — dual-number multiplication has cross terms, so map_mul' is false) or fight scalar coercion directly. After: state the kernel–ideal equality as a membership iff and keep every lemma in its native scalar ring. Mined from: a student attempt blocked at exactly this coercion wall with the mathematics already done. Rationale for coined pattern id math-formalization/bridge-ideal-and-base-linear-kernel-at-membership-level: no existing library pattern covers the Ideal-vs-Submodule scalar-ring bridge; the nearest patterns are generic strategy notions with no reviewed attachment, and the existing classify-square-zero-actions pattern addresses the decomposition route, not the cardinality transport.

f50fcc95be77d2625f84db6748155ea96e241ca8.hook: A simple field generated by a root must have automorphism-cardinality equal to its degree, while commutativity is available only for an ambient splitting field.
f50fcc95be77d2625f84db6748155ea96e241ca8.name: inherit-abelian-galois-structure-through-an-adjoin-embedding
f50fcc95be77d2625f84db6748155ea96e241ca8.body: Make the root integral, prove its minimal polynomial splits in the ambient splitting field by mapping the minimal-polynomial divisibility into the field, and obtain an algebra homomorphism from the simple adjoin with `IntermediateField.nonempty_algHom_adjoin_of_splits`. Package the ambient commutativity hypothesis as `IsAbelianGalois`, then use `IsAbelianGalois.of_algHom` to install the structure on the adjoin. Now `IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank` turns the automorphism count directly into the extension degree. This avoids formalizing a normalizer--stabilizer orbit merely to prove that every conjugate is represented. Rewrite rule: scope = simple subextensions embedded in abelian splitting fields; before = construct the normalizer orbit and compare its cardinality with roots in the adjoin; after = descend `IsAbelianGalois` along an algebra homomorphism and use the automorphism-cardinality theorem; level = proof shape; confidence = high; evidence-ids = certified solver head and base boundary departure. Mined from a residual equating a restricted root count, already identified with the adjoin's automorphism count, to the irreducible polynomial degree.

e4fa6ead08b819777155c7c03fe1dd55c8320af3.hook: Reaching for a Mathlib constant by translated prose name (e.g. CamelCase namespace guess) and getting unknown identifier, in any Lean proof using a semi-encapsulated construction.
e4fa6ead08b819777155c7c03fe1dd55c8320af3.name: grep-the-object-not-the-theorem-name
e4fa6ead08b819777155c7c03fe1dd55c8320af3.body: When a guessed constant name fails (e.g. an upper-case namespace guess for a construction whose file uses a lower-case namespace — the alternating-group KleinFour material lives under lowercase `alternatingGroup`, not `AlternatingGroup`), do not iterate name guesses: grep the library for the OBJECT (`grep -rln <object>` over Mathlib source) and read the file that defines it — the defining file exports exactly the packaged facts you need (here: a normality lemma and a card characterization of the Klein four subgroup that together refute simplicity of the degree-4 alternating group). The method transfers to any Mathlib area: file-level discovery of an object yields its packaged API, which is usually stronger than any single theorem name you were guessing.

1dc654df272305b3435ea555580058c5fbd3a59d.hook: A submodule of Fin n → M surjects onto a simple module, while the downstream theorem needs that simple module as a quotient of a submodule of one copy of M.
1dc654df272305b3435ea555580058c5fbd3a59d.name: reduce-a-simple-quotient-of-a-finite-power-by-kernel-or-range
1dc654df272305b3435ea555580058c5fbd3a59d.body: Induct on the number of coordinates and project to coordinate zero. If ker projection is not contained in ker quotient, the quotient map restricted to that kernel is nonzero and hence surjective by LinearMap.surjective_of_ne_zero; embed the kernel into the Fin n tail with LinearEquiv.ofInjective and recurse. If the containment holds, descend the quotient map with (LinearMap.ker f).liftQ and transport it across LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange, obtaining a surjection from the projection range, a submodule of M. Scope: modules over a ring with simple target. Before: try to transport an entire composition series through products and submodules. After: reduce the subquotient one coordinate at a time. Level: domain. Confidence: high. Evidence: the kernel/range induction compiled in the certified solver head without sorry axioms.

df4cb75afe70cd1c04289f226bf80fcf45539fb1.hook: Uniform local ODE segments exist, but a single function on an unbounded half-line must be defined and proved differentiable, including at every segment boundary.
df4cb75afe70cd1c04289f226bf80fcf45539fb1.name: glue recursively chosen Picard segments across a floor-indexed mesh
df4cb75afe70cd1c04289f226bf80fcf45539fb1.body: Choose each local segment, recursively define the next state as its endpoint, and define the global candidate by evaluating the segment selected by a Nat.floor-based mesh index. Prove the floor specification on half-open mesh cells, then establish local eventual equality with one segment. At a mesh boundary obtain left and right HasDerivWithinAt facts; endpoint compatibility makes both derivatives equal to the vector field at the shared value, and HasDerivWithinAt.union after Iic_union_Ici yields HasDerivAt. This turns fixed positive local lifespan into a global half-line solution without a packaged maximal-solution API.

bcc7198fef75ee35b60a32e09475fb8cf21b776c.hook: Proving a finite group embeds in Equiv.Perm (Fin n) for n the sum of subgroup indices, when explicit permutation construction from a generator seems required
bcc7198fef75ee35b60a32e09475fb8cf21b776c.name: embed-group-in-symmetric-group-via-coset-sum-action
bcc7198fef75ee35b60a32e09475fb8cf21b776c.body: Do not hand-roll explicit disjoint cycles from a cyclic-generator isomorphism: Mathlib exposes no monoid-hom lifting from the image of a generator, and the construction runs to hundreds of lines. Instead let the group act on the disjoint sum of its coset spaces (quotients by subgroups of the needed indices); the action kernel is trapped in the intersection of the subgroups (normalCore_eq_ker plus normalCore_le, no normality hypothesis needed) and coprime cardinalities kill it. Transport the faithful action to Equiv.Perm (Fin n) with the standard faithful-action helper. Witnessed by a zero-error zero-sorry compile.

bf95183d2b1fa505a2c18b9496a86e8f672a3abf.hook: A split extension is generated by cyclic kernel and complement generators, the possible actions have been classified, and a noncommutativity hypothesis must eliminate the trivial action.
bf95183d2b1fa505a2c18b9496a86e8f672a3abf.name: reject the trivial cyclic action by generation and noncommutativity
bf95183d2b1fa505a2c18b9496a86e8f672a3abf.body: Parent pattern: math-formalization/classify-cyclic-actions-through-the-generator-image. If the conjugation homomorphism sends the complement generator to the identity automorphism, evaluate that equality at the kernel generator and unfold `Subgroup.normalizerMonoidHom` to obtain that the two generators commute. Rewrite the cyclic-generator hypotheses through `MonoidHom.map_zpowers`, `Subgroup.range_subtype`, and `Subgroup.closure_union` to show their two-element closure is top. Install `Subgroup.closureCommGroupOfComm` on that closure; since it is top, any alleged noncommuting ambient pair lifts to the closure and contradicts `mul_comm`. Thus noncommutativity selects the nontrivial classified action without an element census. Rewrite rule: scope = split extensions generated by two cyclic subgroups; before = prove the conjugation action is nontrivial by enumerating ambient elements; after = show a trivial generator action makes the generating closure commutative; level = domain; confidence = high. Mined from a certified residual where the final classification required choosing between the trivial and inversion actions.

582cc6f0e126d67205f5d52c234807b721feb7df.hook: When a parameter derivative is itself an integral and must be integrable over parameters bounded away from a singular endpoint.
582cc6f0e126d67205f5d52c234807b721feb7df.name: prove tail integrability by a product-measure majorant
582cc6f0e126d67205f5d52c234807b721feb7df.body: View the differentiated kernel as a function on the product of parameter and integration-variable spaces. Bound its norm by the product x^(-2) * |f y|, prove the two factors integrable separately on the restricted measures, combine them with `Integrable.mul_prod`, and obtain integrability of the iterated integral with `Integrable.integral_prod_left`. A positive lower cutoff makes x^(-2) integrable via `integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_of_lt`; the original L1 hypothesis supplies the y-factor. Finally use almost-everywhere congruence with the derivative-under-the-integral identity. This avoids trying to establish parameter integrability pointwise without a single Tonelli/Fubini majorant.

07b9a3dcba327a9e0791ff9f3e158b5ae6308958.hook: A dilated probability kernel gives an approximate identity, but the goal is convergence in the quotient space `Lp` and a direct pointwise estimate is unavailable.
07b9a3dcba327a9e0791ff9f3e158b5ae6308958.name: fixed-kernel-lp-average-by-translation-continuity
07b9a3dcba327a9e0791ff9f3e158b5ae6308958.body: Normalize the dilation first so the varying kernels become one fixed integrable kernel. Represent translation by `Lp.compMeasurePreserving` and obtain continuity of the resulting `Lp`-valued map from `Continuous.compMeasurePreservingLp`. For each fixed integration variable, continuity makes the translation difference tend to zero; probability-kernel nonnegativity and translation isometry bound its norm by the integrable scalar majorant `k z * (2 * ‖F‖)`. Then `tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence` proves the Bochner average tends to zero in `Lp`. This packages the usual approximate-identity argument without requiring a pointwise representative during the convergence step.

6f30a2e46b17ebf9d68037a45b2e8409e868f3c1.hook: when a goal asks to prove a concrete permutation is a 3-cycle and decide/native_decide fail on it
6f30a2e46b17ebf9d68037a45b2e8409e868f3c1.name: three-cycle-from-transposition-products
6f30a2e46b17ebf9d68037a45b2e8409e868f3c1.body: Proving a concrete permutation is a 3-cycle: IsThreeCycle synthesizes no Decidable instance, and a pointwise binder statement fails decide with 'Expected type must not contain free variables'. Derive instead: write the permutation as a product of two transpositions sharing a point and apply Equiv.Perm.isThreeCycle_swap_mul_swap_same (reordering factors with swap_comm as needed); state pointwise orbit-step lemmas as top-level forall statements, which then decide cleanly.

32bfb64028ee33e94b580c6d3948e13eaab9bfe2.hook: A Galois-correspondence construction lives as an intermediate field of an extension type, while the desired maximality statement quantifies over intermediate fields in a common ambient algebraic closure.
32bfb64028ee33e94b580c6d3948e13eaab9bfe2.name: transport-an-abelian-galois-subfield-across-comap-map-equivalences
32bfb64028ee33e94b580c6d3948e13eaab9bfe2.body: For an ambient subfield K below E, set K0 := K.comap E.val and first prove K0.map E.val = K with IntermediateField.map_comap_eq_self after rewriting E.fieldRange_val. Build an F-algebra equivalence K0 ≃ₐ[F] K by composing IntermediateField.equivMap K0 E.val with IntermediateField.equivOfEq of that equality. Once IsAbelianGalois is installed on K from the hypotheses, IsAbelianGalois.of_algHom applied to the equivalence's toAlgHom installs it on K0. The same transport works from a mapped fixed field back through the symmetric equivMap. This lets fixed-field and fixing-subgroup theorems run inside E while the final containment is returned to the ambient closure by rewriting the map/comap equality and applying IntermediateField.map_mono.

30dfa5c993637703c23be0f646715ad16959ea6f.hook: When bounding a set integral by a pointwise bound that holds only on the integration set, not globally
30dfa5c993637703c23be0f646715ad16959ea6f.name: setintegral-mono-vs-mono-on-pointwise-bounds
30dfa5c993637703c23be0f646715ad16959ea6f.body: `setIntegral_mono` in current Mathlib takes two IntegrableOn arguments and a GLOBAL pointwise <= (everywhere), so it cannot consume a bound proved only for x in the integration set s. Use `setIntegral_mono_on` with the set's measurability and the restricted inequality instead.

7909b9c94ebe373a273d5b4c7bf4433dff70b042.hook: Closing an integral identity whose obstruction is scalar bookkeeping - a (1/pi)*integral = value equation, or exp (ofReal (-s)) vs exp (-ofReal s) mismatches - and field_simp or congr 1 keeps failing under the integral binder
7909b9c94ebe373a273d5b4c7bf4433dff70b042.name: state-scalar-cast-identities-as-standalone-have-not-fieldsimp-over-integrals
7909b9c94ebe373a273d5b4c7bf4433dff70b042.body: Before: field_simp / congr 1 applied directly to an equation bearing an integral binder; rw also fails to unify MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul under the binder. After (witnessed across attempts 1-2): (1) state the scalar identity as an explicit standalone have and rewrite with it - MeasureTheory.integral_const_mul must be an explicit have, rw will not unify the pattern under an integral binder; (2) normalize casts on hypothesis AND goal in one push_cast before any congr step - congr 1 on Complex.exp arguments requires push_cast to align ofReal arithmetic first; (3) RCLike.real_smul_eq_coe_smul converts R-smul to C-mul, and real-part extraction needs RCLike.re / RCLike.re_to_complex reconciliation before any .re simp set, else it lands on normSq junk because integral_re returns a generic RCLike.re, not syntactically Complex.re; (4) exp fusion needs explicit exp_add rewrites - direct congr-1 fails on cast-of-compound vs compound-of-cast mismatches. Casting here is a syntactic prerequisite of the closing step, not cleanup: doing it late means doing it twice, and the failure is mislabelled as 'simp made no progress'.

81426adb00c965f92658a54cc260de46ab3f8ba8.hook: A convergence theorem is available only for Lp elements (e.g. raw integral coefficients against an orthonormal family tend to zero for every MemLp function) but the goal concerns a merely Integrable function paired with a uniformly bounded a.e.-measurable test family.
81426adb00c965f92658a54cc260de46ab3f8ba8.name: extend-test-function-convergence-from-Lp-approximants-to-L1-by-bounded-truncation
81426adb00c965f92658a54cc260de46ab3f8ba8.body: Trigger: convergence known on Lp (here Lp 2 over a finite measure) while the target function is only Integrable. Move: sandwich with level truncations h k x = max (-(k:R)) (min (k:R) (f x)). Each h k is AEStronglyMeasurable and a.e. bounded by k, so MemLp.of_bound puts it in Lp 2 on the finite measure; tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence with dominator 2 * |f| gives Integral |f - h k| -> 0. The uniform test bound ||g n|| <= M converts that single L1 estimate into a uniform one: ||Integral (f - h k) * g n|| <= M * Integral |f - h k| (Integrable.bdd_smul for integrability, then norm_integral_le_of_norm_le and integral_const_mul). Pick k with Integral |f - h k| < epsilon / (2 * (M + 1)) so the truncation error is < epsilon / 2 uniformly in n; the Lp theorem handles h k itself, giving the limit for f. Reason it works: on a finite measure space, bounded measurable truncations of an integrable function lie in every Lp simultaneously and are L1-dense in L1, so a uniformly bounded dual pairing cannot distinguish the L1 limit from its truncations. Mine witness: certified solver head closing the bridge theorem with Lean exit 0, zero sorry warnings, no axioms beyond propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound.

3342e8b600b9c0afa993830cd2322312b30e31f6.hook: when a Lean goal mixes Matrix.toLin' with Module.End predicates, or dot-notation on toLin' fails to elaborate
3342e8b600b9c0afa993830cd2322312b30e31f6.name: matrix-toLin-conversion-spelling-traps
3342e8b600b9c0afa993830cd2322312b30e31f6.body: PATTERN (Mathlib matrix-to-endomorphism layer). Goals mixing matrices and Module.End facts fail twice at spelling before any mathematics happens; handle the conversion layer explicitly before planning the proof. LEAF (Mathlib around v4.29). First, dot-notation on Matrix.toLin' results does NOT elaborate; writing (Matrix.toLin' A).IsSemisimple fails with the error that the environment does not contain LinearMap.IsSemisimple, because toLin' has head symbol LinearMap; write the full name Module.End.IsSemisimple (Matrix.toLin' A). Second, Matrix.toLin'_mul rewrites (M * N).toLin' to an End-multiplication goal that simp alone leaves open; close it with Module.End.mul_eq_comp or LinearMap.mul_toLin' rather than more simp. Third, to transport IsSemisimple (or similar End predicates) across a conjugation, build the linear equiv from the conjugating matrix with Matrix.toLinearEquiv (Pi.basisFun K n) (Matrix.isUnit_iff_isUnit_det.mp hT) and use LinearEquiv.isSemisimple_iff with the intertwining equation e comp f = g comp e proved from toLin'_mul plus Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul.

454fa7c4792430b595b9e3a750ebda0f372e7136.hook: rw failing on defeq structure projections or algebraMap coercions; bridge with show/have; open Complex for I
454fa7c4792430b595b9e3a750ebda0f372e7136.name: defeq-syntactic-bridging-in-lean-rewrites
454fa7c4792430b595b9e3a750ebda0f372e7136.body: Pattern: when rw fails on terms that are equal by definitional equality but not syntactically equal, bridge with show (change the goal to the rewritable syntactic form) or have (state the instance-level fact, then simp only on it) instead of hunting for a differently-spelled lemma. Concrete instances from complex-number formalization: (1) rw with AlgEquiv.commutes cannot rewrite phi applied to ofReal z.re because the ofReal coercion does not syntactically match algebraMap -- fix with an explicit pointwise have. (2) rw with Complex.conj_re cannot rewrite (conjAe z).re because conjAe z is a structure projection, not syntactically starRingEnd applied to z -- fix with show to (starRingEnd C z).re then rw. (3) In a standalone lake env lean file without open Complex, a bare I is silently auto-bound as a fresh local of type C, making I.re irreducible to norm_num and rw -- several iterations lost before the context line revealed it; always open Complex or write Complex.I. (4) Complex.ext_iff with named a := arguments type-checks the argument against the wrong field; extract the equality first. Provenance: mined from f75 student-attempt-1 tactic-level failure list.

17c106bf5130305c18cf8669e8153c96f8ed4f65.hook: In any Lean/Mathlib proof over Q (or a structure with num/den projections), rewriting a variable by its num/den quotient definition; the rewrite fires everywhere including inside the projections themselves.
17c106bf5130305c18cf8669e8153c96f8ed4f65.name: rat-num-den-set-before-quotient-rewrite
17c106bf5130305c18cf8669e8153c96f8ed4f65.body: rw with the quotient-defining lemma (e.g. Rat.num_div_den) on a variable x rewrites x everywhere, INCLUDING inside x.num and x.den, producing nested ((x.num / x.den).num) projections that field_simp cannot undo. Fix: abstract the projections first (set a := x.num; set c := x.den), then rewrite the variable as a quotient of the abstracted atoms. Also verify the lemma's orientation in your snapshot with an isolated example: in this snapshot it is stated as (q.num : Z) / q.den = q, i.e. the projection direction, not the variable direction, so the reverse arrow is what introduces the nesting. Domain-level: any definitional lemma that mentions a term's own sub-projections must not be applied to the bare term.

ddd857291c958cb6550cb203b7a78b7a45394262.hook: A concrete alternating group must be shown nonsolvable, and Mathlib exposes its commutator subgroup theorem rather than a ready degree-specific nonsolvability theorem.
ddd857291c958cb6550cb203b7a78b7a45394262.name: derive-nonsolvability-from-perfectness-with-the-isperfect-api
ddd857291c958cb6550cb203b7a78b7a45394262.body: Install `Group.IsPerfect` by supplying the equality `commutator_alternatingGroup_eq_top` at the required finite degree, then apply `Group.IsPerfect.not_isSolvable`. This avoids constructing an embedded smaller simple group or developing simplicity merely to refute solvability. Mined from a residual where the finite quotient was already constructed and only target nonsolvability remained.

21c89a67818ea21ca80737ce9ec92f91f0cff42e.hook: A proof has a Mathlib circle Cauchy formula, but dominated convergence is formulated for integrals over a fixed real angular interval and the endpoint convention does not syntactically match.
21c89a67818ea21ca80737ce9ec92f91f0cff42e.name: normalize-circle-cauchy-formula-to-fixed-angular-measure
21c89a67818ea21ca80737ce9ec92f91f0cff42e.body: Start from `DifferentiableOn.circleIntegral_sub_inv_smul` after restricting differentiability from the ambient disk to the relevant closed ball. Unfold `circleIntegral`, orient the interval with `intervalIntegral.integral_of_le`, and rewrite the restricted measures using `Measure.restrict_congr_set Ioo_ae_eq_Ioc.symm`. Then `simpa only [deriv_circleMap, circleMap_zero, smul_eq_mul, mul_assoc, mul_comm (Complex.I : ℂ)]` exposes the same fixed-domain angular integrand expected by dominated convergence. The endpoint rewrite is legitimate because the interval conventions differ only on a null singleton.

9d80d515e88506287c603e09448f680b3651ea79.hook: Affinely reparametrized integrand and a canonical improper limit lemma: reparametrize with smul_integral_comp_mul_sub, not a change-of-variables theorem
9d80d515e88506287c603e09448f680b3651ea79.name: affine-reparametrization-to-canonical-sinc-limit
9d80d515e88506287c603e09448f680b3651ea79.body: Rewrite rule. Scope: integrals of affinely reparametrized integrands over symmetric truncations when a library or construction-target lemma computes the canonical improper limit. Before: apply a change-of-variables theorem or restate the library limit by hand. After: rewrite the Lebesgue integral as an interval integral (MeasureTheory.integral_Icc_eq_integral_Ioc, intervalIntegral.integral_of_le), push the constant scaling out with intervalIntegral.smul_integral_comp_mul_sub (its c • f x + c' shape matches affine arguments directly), split with intervalIntegral.integral_add; each piece is then literally the canonical integral at a shifted endpoint and ring closes the endpoint bookkeeping. Level: domain. Confidence: 0.8. Provenance: certified head 6a96cff2f745981b34ec58efa8761c30a59251ed tends each shifted sinc window to the ConstructionTargets.Sinc canonical value with no substitution theorem.

b4075f5c0d24e37c6f35f844314dc5689ff785b5.hook: Almost-everywhere convergence under an integrable majorant has to be upgraded to ‘the integrals of the norm differences tend to zero’, and the dominated-convergence obligations do not match the majorant hypothesis as it was given.
b4075f5c0d24e37c6f35f844314dc5689ff785b5.name: dominated-convergence-of-norm-differences-needs-the-limit-bounded-and-the-bounds-swapped
b4075f5c0d24e37c6f35f844314dc5689ff785b5.body:
PATTERN. Convergence in L1 of a sequence to its pointwise limit is not dominated convergence applied to the sequence; it is dominated convergence applied to the REAL-valued sequence of norm differences, whose limit is the constant 0. Restating it that way makes the theorem apply, and then exposes three obligations that are not in the hypotheses you were handed. Budget for all three; each one on its own can look like a missing lemma.
(1) The dominator is twice the majorant, not the majorant. The norm difference is bounded through the triangle inequality by the bound on the sequence plus the bound on the limit, so the domination hypothesis needs 2*M and its integrability comes from scaling the majorant's.
(2) The limit inherits the majorant, but only by proof. You are given a bound on each term and NOT on the limit; get it by passing to the limit in the norms — a limit of a sequence that is eventually below a constant is below that constant.
(3) To do (2) at a point you need the bound for ALL indices at that point, but the hypothesis is a family of almost-everywhere statements indexed by n, i.e. the quantifiers are in the wrong order. A countable family of almost-everywhere statements does hold almost everywhere simultaneously, but not definitionally: you must swap them explicitly before filter_upwards can hand you all of them at one point. This is the step most likely to stall a proof that otherwise looks finished, because the two statements print almost identically.

LEAF. Swap the quantifiers with eventually_countable_forall (used in the .2 direction: from ‘for each i, almost every x’ to ‘almost every x, for each i’); it needs the index type Countable and the filter a CountableInterFilter, which the almost-everywhere filter of any measure is. Pass to the limit in the norms with le_of_tendsto' applied to the .norm of the pointwise convergence. Then close with MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence, whose five arguments are the dominator (fun x => 2 * M x), the measurability of each difference (obtained as ((hF n).sub hmeas).norm, so you need the limit's measurability FIRST — this is why the selection step must come before this one), the integrability hM.const_mul 2, the domination, and the pointwise convergence to 0. Two shape mismatches at the end: the outer norm on a real number needs Real.norm_eq_abs with abs_of_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) before the triangle calc, and the conclusion arrives as the integral of the zero function, so finish with simpa rather than exact.

8fb66a4a39c5a5752699e3bb417598af0a24f53f.hook: when a kernel tail on an infinite-measure half-line needs compact/tail splitting and power decay
8fb66a4a39c5a5752699e3bb417598af0a24f53f.name: compact-tail-split-and-rpow-decay-for-halfline-integrability
8fb66a4a39c5a5752699e3bb417598af0a24f53f.body: A constant domination bound is wrong on a half-line of infinite measure (mono into a constant fails); the route is a compact/tail split — the closed half-line equals a compact interval union an open ray — with the compact piece from continuity (ContinuousOn.integrableOn_compact) and the tail from a pointwise power-decay bound (absolute kernel value at most (integral of |f|) * x^(-2)), closed by integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_of_lt. Leaf facts: setIntegral_mono in current Mathlib takes two IntegrableOn arguments and a global inequality, so a bound holding only on the subset needs setIntegral_mono_on; rpow/inverse mismatches resolve through Real.rpow_neg and norm_num.

3e9010e8e80098d6c24b9aafaaa674d21286ca90.hook: A relative automorphism of a simple prime-degree extension may move a generator whose prime power lies in the base, and direct classification of all conjugates is awkward.
3e9010e8e80098d6c24b9aafaaa674d21286ca90.name: exclude moved generators by a cyclotomic degree obstruction
3e9010e8e80098d6c24b9aafaaa674d21286ca90.body: For a relative automorphism σ and nonzero generator g with g^3 in the base, set u = σ(g) / g. The fixed-cube equation gives u^3 = 1. If u ≠ 1, factor u^3 - 1 to obtain u^2 + u + 1 = 0. Show u is not in the base (in an embedded-real setting, nontrivial solutions of that quadratic cannot be real), bound natDegree (minpoly E u) by 2 using minpoly.dvd, exclude degree 1 with IntermediateField.finrank_adjoin_simple_eq_one_iff, and conclude the adjoin has relative finrank 2. Module.finrank_mul_finrank through that intermediate field then contradicts an ambient relative finrank of 3. Thus every relative automorphism fixes g. This turns a missing Kummer-style exclusion theorem into a local cyclotomic subfield and tower-degree argument.

00ce8364dd1d0052ef05acab08b252324b21b2d0.hook: A prime divides the cardinality of a finite commutative group, but the library offers no direct theorem producing a subgroup of that prime index.
00ce8364dd1d0052ef05acab08b252324b21b2d0.name: obtain a prime-index kernel from finite abelian coordinates
00ce8364dd1d0052ef05acab08b252324b21b2d0.body: Use `CommGroup.equiv_prod_multiplicative_zmod_of_finite` to expose cyclic coordinates and rewrite the group cardinality as their finite product. `Prime.dvd_finset_prod_iff` selects a coordinate modulus divisible by the prime. Compose the decomposition equivalence with `Pi.evalMonoidHom` at that coordinate and with `ZMod.castHom` to modulus `p`; prove the composite surjective from `Function.surjective_eval`, the decomposition equivalence, and `ZMod.castHom_surjective`. Its kernel has the desired index by `Subgroup.index_ker`, `MonoidHom.range_eq_top.mpr`, and the cardinality of `ZMod p`. For a surjective quotient map, pull this kernel back and transfer the index using `Subgroup.index_comap_of_surjective`.

f7baf57f4ca310975bb811a028b5131cd7c02fe2.hook: A dominated-convergence proof needs a bound independent of a small nonnegative parameter for the absolute logarithm of a squared radius plus the parameter squared.
f7baf57f4ca310975bb811a028b5131cd7c02fe2.name: uniform logarithmic bound for quadratic regularization
f7baf57f4ca310975bb811a028b5131cd7c02fe2.body: For `r > 0` and `0 ≤ ε ≤ 1`, prove `|Real.log (r ^ 2 + ε ^ 2)| ≤ 2 * |Real.log r| + Real.log 2` by splitting on `r ≤ 1`. In the small-radius branch, monotonicity gives `2 * log r ≤ log (r² + ε²) ≤ log 2`; in the large-radius branch, `1 ≤ r` fixes the signs and `r² + ε² ≤ 2*r²`, after which `Real.log_mul` and `Real.log_pow` expose the desired estimate. This turns the regularized logarithm into the limiting logarithmic singularity plus a bounded error.

345c2019915b4d94eb241eec6b353a1710963d1b.hook: when proving a subspace defined as an iInf/intersection of invariant subspaces is itself invariant under a commuting family

345c2019915b4d94eb241eec6b353a1710963d1b.body: PATTERN (linear-algebra formalization). For generalized eigenspaces the component invariance comes from Module.End.mapsTo_maxGenEigenspace_of_comm, applied after rcases eq_or_ne splits the reflexive case (that one needs Commute.refl). 009b4af87f62b5dd2dcda0798b0a2f3f3951b2b1.hook: a theorem spelled with a module-prefix namespace fails as unknown identifier though the module header cites it that way

b52e62e5db550a495bbef841ec6cb86c3bdce434.body: PATTERN — the obstacle. Base cases: abelian via `isSolvable_of_comm` (V4 through `IsKleinFour.exponent_two` commutativity), quotient of prime order via `isCyclic_of_prime_card` + `IsCyclic.commGroup`. Card bookkeeping: `Subgroup.card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card_subgroup`, `alternatingGroup.card_of_card_eq_four`, `alternatingGroup.kleinFour_card_of_card_eq_four`; normality/identity instances from `alternatingGroup.normal_kleinFour` and `alternatingGroup.kleinFour_isKleinFour`, both requiring `Nat.card (Fin 4) = 4` by simp. f6ff96e61479734ef614b5758b13d76b77731a77.hook: When holomorphic functions have dominated almost-everywhere convergent boundary traces and the goal is locally uniform convergence on the interior disk.

f6ff96e61479734ef614b5758b13d76b77731a77.body: Select the almost-everywhere pointwise limit, obtain L1 convergence of boundary traces by dominated convergence, and define its Cauchy transform. On each closed subdisk of radius r < 1, reverse-triangle separation on the unit circle gives a uniform kernel factor (1-r)^(-1), so the interior sup error is bounded by a constant times the boundary L1 error. Assemble these closed-subdisk estimates with tendstoLocallyUniformlyOn_iff, then apply TendstoLocallyUniformlyOn.differentiableOn for holomorphy of the limit.

38fe1471cfd1f4f9e1be053589c48c7b190b6b4c.body: For finite a b : ENNReal, ((a : EReal) - (b : EReal)) = ↑(a.toReal - b.toReal); prove it by the ENNReal.ofReal_toReal round-trip on both sides rather than hunting for a library coe lemma. 30019edab9e930b20c8cb273a4fb65729a25b64a.hook: An entire complex function has all iterated derivatives at a center equal to zero above a finite cutoff, but the target asks for one polynomial agreeing with the function globally.
30019edab9e930b20c8cb273a4fb65729a25b64a.name: reconstruct a global polynomial from a finite Taylor tail
30019edab9e930b20c8cb273a4fb65729a25b64a.body: Build the polynomial as the finite sum of monomials whose coefficients are `iteratedDeriv k f 0 / k!`. Obtain the local power-series sum from `AnalyticAt.hasFPowerSeriesAt`; tail vanishing lets `tsum_eq_sum` identify that series with the finite polynomial near the center. Finally promote eventual local equality to global equality with `AnalyticOnNhd.eq_of_eventuallyEq`, using `AnalyticOnNhd.eval_polynomial` for the polynomial side. This avoids searching for a packaged generalized Liouville theorem.

b884fe5146701675e4064196e56a4ce9b0895cb3.hook: A goal compares ((k : ℕ) : ℝ) / (2 ^ n : ℕ) cell endpoints — proving dyadic cells disjoint, equal, or nested — and direct real algebra with the casts stalls.

b884fe5146701675e4064196e56a4ce9b0895cb3.body: Rewrite rule. Scope: order facts about Ico cells with Nat.cast-div endpoints in Lean/Mathlib. Before: push casted-ℝ inequalities through field_simp/nlinarith, which fails or leaves cast side-goals. After: transfer the order to ℕ immediately — (div_lt_div_iff_of_pos_right (by positivity)).mp converts a/2^n < b/2^n into ((a : ℕ) : ℝ) < ((b : ℕ) : ℝ), exact_mod_cast returns to ℕ, and omega closes, including the two-sided sandwich forcing two cell indices equal; an even/odd parity contradiction then finishes exclusion arguments (Nat.not_even_iff_odd / Nat.not_odd_iff_even). a2f06a4261fb78c28abcef0f801bced7e4fc350c.hook: A finite extension has an injectively parameterized family of algebra automorphisms whose parameter count matches the extension degree, but surjectivity onto all automorphisms is still missing.
a2f06a4261fb78c28abcef0f801bced7e4fc350c.name: upgrade an explicit automorphism family by matching cardinalities
a2f06a4261fb78c28abcef0f801bced7e4fc350c.body: Install `FiniteDimensional K L`, use `AlgEquiv.card_le` for the upper bound on `Nat.card (L ≃ₐ[K] L)`, and combine it with the injected parameter family and its computed cardinality. `Nat.bijective_iff_injective_and_card` then upgrades the family map to a bijection without constructing inverse parameters for an arbitrary automorphism. c95ab37a1e0ef58360e398a6f37006e26573a651.hook: Every member of a concrete automorphism family fixes a candidate intermediate field, and the remaining direction asks whether every jointly fixed element lies in that field.
c95ab37a1e0ef58360e398a6f37006e26573a651.name: identify fixed elements after proving automorphism count equals finrank
c95ab37a1e0ef58360e398a6f37006e26573a651.body: View the concrete automorphisms as equivalences over the candidate intermediate field. Once their parameterization is bijective and `Nat.card (L ≃ₐ[K] L) = Module.finrank K L`, install `IsGalois K L` with `IsGalois.of_card_aut_eq_finrank`. Rewrite joint fixedness as membership in `IntermediateField.fixedField ⊤`, use surjectivity to replace an arbitrary K-automorphism by a concrete one, then close with `IsGalois.fixedField_top` and `IntermediateField.mem_bot`. Scope: finite extensions with a concrete full automorphism family. Before: attempt direct rational-function invariant classification. After: turn equality of automorphism count and degree into Galois structure, then use the fixed-field theorem. Level: domain. Confidence: high. Evidence: kernel checking accepted the fixed-field equivalence and the axiom audit reported only standard foundational axioms.

88e93443f706cdf26b0f2af9602055f714005467.body: Current-Mathlib leaf facts: dot notation on IntegrableOn (e.g. hf.mul_bound) fails because IntegrableOn is not reducible for dot resolution — use prefix application such as Integrable.mul_bdd; one_div_le_one_div_of_le replaces inv_le_inv_of_le; Measurable.pow now takes a measurable-exponent argument (fun_prop closes it); a.e. statements under volume.restrict need (ae_restrict_iff measurableSet_Ioi).mpr (ae_of_all volume ...) rather than ae_of_all directly; Filter.eventually_of_forall is now Filter.Eventually.of_forall; Set.indicator_of_not_mem is Set.indicator_of_notMem; ContinuousOn.inv is ContinuousOn.inv0.

1ec14207f3149849e9a8482225accc7c2d82d01d.body: In the tendsto/deriv-atTop regime, several plausibly-named lemmas are absent and the working replacements are: 'isOpen_lt_mem_nhds' does not exist — use Tendsto.eventually (Iio_mem_nhds h); 'mem_atTop_sets' does not exist — use eventually_atTop.mp, and note the result is threshold-form (∀ b ≥ N), not a destructurable predicate; 'tendsto_id_atTop_atTop' does not exist — rw [tendsto_atTop_atTop] with the iff characterization; the triangle inequality is abs_add_le (not abs_add) and it does not fire on a - b until the negation is rewritten first; tendsto_const_nhds under Tendsto.sub leaves a metavariable limit — pin it with (show Tendsto (fun _ => c) atTop (nhds c) from tendsto_const_nhds).

b9207180feb67f190bfe586b8dcb89e7386cfcc0.name: obtain a uniform Picard lifespan with state-dependent radius bounds
b9207180feb67f190bfe586b8dcb89e7386cfcc0.body: For a vector field with linear growth, let the closed-ball radius grow with the center, bound the field on that ball by another affine expression in the center norm, and choose these expressions so the Picard duration inequality has a fixed positive lower bound. e32e70aa1bcadc02ca644978a51814c9c6df1a31.body: Use `IsPGroup.disjoint_of_ne` to prove the Sylow factors disjoint. 9506a6be78d512ce152854e1e5b5ff3a300dfbb2.name: recover-complex-differentiability-from-conservativity-and-continuity
9506a6be78d512ce152854e1e5b5ff3a300dfbb2.body: Prove `Complex.IsConservativeOn f U` by showing every rectangular boundary integral vanishes, then combine it with `ContinuousOn f U`. For open `U`, `Complex.isConservativeOn_and_continuousOn_iff_isDifferentiableOn` converts these two facts into `DifferentiableOn ℂ f U`; use openness to pass from the within-set result to `DifferentiableAt` at an interior point. This is the Mathlib-facing Morera route when a local formula is not differentiable by inspection at a gluing seam.

5ada577d168c686b97fac94980f70541be69674f.hook: A finite-dimensional classification reduces to a square-zero linear operator, but no directly usable Jordan-form theorem packages the required decomposition.
5ada577d168c686b97fac94980f70541be69674f.name: square-zero-conjugacy-from-adapted-complements
5ada577d168c686b97fac94980f70541be69674f.body: Use LinearMap.range_le_ker_iff to place range T inside ker T. Choose a complement A of the range inside the kernel and a complement B of the kernel in the whole space via Submodule.exists_isCompl, then assemble coordinates with Submodule.prodEquivOfIsCompl and Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe. The restriction of T to B is bijective onto range T; LinearEquiv.ofBijective packages that fact. Consequently, square-zero endomorphisms on spaces of equal finrank are conjugate whenever their ranges have equal finrank. This replaces a missing packaged Jordan decomposition with the exact block invariant needed by module-classification proofs.

034a79eb711a143976f40a045a216406fecaf584.hook: A construction needs the total integral as a continuous linear functional on `TestFunction`, but the obvious integral is only an unbundled function.
034a79eb711a143976f40a045a216406fecaf584.name: Continuous total integration on TestFunction via stagewise L1 maps
034a79eb711a143976f40a045a216406fecaf584.body: Use `TestFunction.limitCLM` to assemble the global functional. On a compact stage `K`, give the restricted finite measure the instance `Fact (volume (K : Set E) < ⊤)`, map `ContDiffMapSupportedIn` to bounded continuous functions, then to `L1` for `volume.restrict K`, and compose with `L1.integralCLM`. Prove the stage application formula by `ContinuousLinearMap.comp_apply`, `L1.integral_eq_integral`, and `setIntegral_eq_integral_of_ae_compl_eq_zero`, using `tsupport_subset` outside `K`.

f0986fea8eab2f698b3280ff3003e88f28c94e9b.body: Those convenience lemmas are absent in some Mathlib builds. c1e7e6bec817b4e164b9d616b56f0ed032bddfbe.hook: To prove a normal subgroup of a large alternating group is top, the available global generator theorem needs one three-cycle in the subgroup, but the starting element has arbitrary support.
c1e7e6bec817b4e164b9d616b56f0ed032bddfbe.name: reduce-alternating-group-normality-to-computed-small-support-commutators
c1e7e6bec817b4e164b9d616b56f0ed032bddfbe.body: Choose a three-cycle that does not commute with a nonidentity subgroup element; their commutator remains in the normal subgroup and has support at most six by support-of-product and conjugation bounds. 1dad9835e397faf2b28fcaa990c069051145c559.hook: Evaluating a set integral over a bounded interval (MeasureTheory setIntegral over Icc/Ioc) with the FTC/antiderivative lemmas, where the set-integral and interval-integral APIs do not talk to each other and the expected bridging lemma name does not exist.

1dad9835e397faf2b28fcaa990c069051145c559.body: There is no setIntegral_icc-style conversion lemma; the bridge is `MeasureTheory.integral_Icc_eq_integral_Ioc` followed by `← intervalIntegral.integral_of_le` (with the endpoint ordering fact supplied). On the interval side, evaluation by an antiderivative goes through `intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt`, whose argument order is HasDerivAt-family FIRST and IntervalIntegrable SECOND — the reverse of what the name suggests — and which needs explicit named arguments (a:=..) (b:=..) (f:=..) (f':=..) because the derivative produced by the HasDerivAt chain (e.g. HasDerivAt.div_const normalizing cos(2*t)*(2*1)/2) is not syntactically a bare cos(2*t); state the derivative fact in exactly the normalized shape or supply f' explicitly. ad3a612cca7739623fed5a89ff290a2f5676f8aa.hook: A Kummer theorem needs an IsSplittingField instance on a concrete simple adjoin subtype generated by a radical.
ad3a612cca7739623fed5a89ff290a2f5676f8aa.name: splitting-field-instance-for-a-simple-radical-adjoin
ad3a612cca7739623fed5a89ff290a2f5676f8aa.body: Let L be the intermediate-field adjoin and alphaL its canonical generator. Prove alphaL lies in the rootSet of X^p-C a from the radical equation. Use X_pow_sub_C_splits_of_isPrimitiveRoot for splitting. For isSplittingField_iff_intermediateField, prove adjoin F {alphaL} = top via IntermediateField.lift_injective and lift_adjoin_simple, then show this singleton adjoin is bounded by the adjoin of the polynomial rootSet because alphaL is a root. 522a530efd5814b59a5715ada0dfa87b66898601.hook: A finite Galois extension has the right degree, but the goal requires an explicit automorphism-group equivalence and an exhaustive list of intermediate fields.
522a530efd5814b59a5715ada0dfa87b66898601.name: classify-intermediate-fields-through-a-concrete-root-action
522a530efd5814b59a5715ada0dfa87b66898601.body: Build the automorphism action on a finite indexed family of conjugate generators by transporting the canonical action on the polynomial root set through an equivalence with the index type. Prove faithfulness by showing that fixing a small generating subfamily forces an algebra automorphism to be the identity; when source and target finite groups have equal cardinality, upgrade the injective monoid hom to a MulEquiv. For the field classification, map each fixing subgroup through that MulEquiv, use a concrete subgroup census, and rewrite fixed fields with IntermediateField.fixedField_fixingSubgroup and fixingSubgroup_fixedField. Proper fixed-field identities can be proved by containment plus degree: compute subgroup cardinality, use finrank_fixedField_eq_card and Module.finrank_mul_finrank, then apply IntermediateField.eq_of_le_of_finrank_eq. Mined from a residual asking for a full intermediate-field census after the splitting field and its degree were already established.

d8ecbb2031df6711924a54b75d8cf01c8a5e837e.hook: When HasDerivAt.pow / HasDerivAt.div leave goals about ((fun z => z+y)^(n+1)) x or unnormalised reciprocal powers
d8ecbb2031df6711924a54b75d8cf01c8a5e837e.name: pi-and-pow-beta-redexes-after-hasderivat-combinators
d8ecbb2031df6711924a54b75d8cf01c8a5e837e.body: HasDerivAt chain combinators produce Pi-application beta-redexes and power forms simp does not fold automatically. `simp only [Pi.pow_apply]` unfolds the function-power redex; mismatch between -(n+1)*f/(x+y)^(n+2) and raw HasDerivAt.div output needs a short identity via pow_succ/pow_two/ring. simpa normalizes 1/(x+y) to (x+y)^(-1), so STATE the target HasDerivAt in the reciprocal-power form the tactic will produce, and end field_simp goals with a trailing ring (field_simp alone leaves trivial residue like 1 = x+1-x).

af8d80a068d2bb8d40b16adfa766006a11819584.hook: A finite Galois correspondence goal identifies uniqueness of intermediate fields of one relative degree with Galoisness, while the available APIs speak separately about subgroup order, Sylow uniqueness, subgroup normality, and fixed fields.
af8d80a068d2bb8d40b16adfa766006a11819584.name: transport restricted Galois uniqueness through Sylow normality
af8d80a068d2bb8d40b16adfa766006a11819584.body: Turn each field of the target relative degree into a Sylow subgroup with `Sylow.ofCard`: rewrite the fixing subgroup cardinality using `IsGalois.card_fixingSubgroup_eq_finrank`, and discharge the full prime-part condition with `Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity` plus the automorphism-group finrank formula. For uniqueness implies Galoisness, use the singleton hypothesis to identify the fixed fields of arbitrary Sylow subgroups, then `Sylow.ext` after rewriting each subgroup by `IntermediateField.fixingSubgroup_fixedField`; this gives a `Subsingleton (Sylow p G)` instance, hence normality by `Sylow.normal_of_subsingleton`, and `InfiniteGalois.normal_iff_isGalois` finishes. Conversely, convert Galoisness to normality of the fixing subgroup, transfer it to the constructed Sylow value, install `Unique (Sylow p G)` with `Sylow.unique_of_normal`, and prove the field singleton by set extensionality, `Subsingleton.elim` on the corresponding Sylow values, and `IsGalois.fixedField_fixingSubgroup`. Rewrite rule: scope = finite Galois correspondence restricted by a prime-power relative degree; before = seek a packaged restricted correspondence or manually chase order-isomorphism images; after = construct the Sylow subtype from its cardinality and transport uniqueness through `Subsingleton`/`Unique` instances; level = proof shape; confidence = high; evidence-ids = certified solver head and base boundary departure.

f562de37d0373b19a680f8abd4825f8022300646.hook: when an integrability goal for a swapped kernel integral needs Fubini-Tonelli on a half-line
f562de37d0373b19a680f8abd4825f8022300646.name: kernel-integral-integrability-by-tonelli-and-pointwise-kernel-bound
f562de37d0373b19a680f8abd4825f8022300646.body: To show the integral over a half-line of the absolute value of an inner kernel integral is finite, do not look for a one-step integral swap: first bound the iterated integral pointwise (absolute value of the inner integral is at most the integral of the absolute value), then swap the order over the product of the two half-lines using Tonelli on the nonnegative integrand, and evaluate the inner integral of the kernel alone — for x at least a, the kernel (x+y)^(-2) has total mass a^(-1); the pointwise kernel bound (a+y)^(-1) at most a^(-1) is what makes the swap finite.

537762ed0032013cbb1977c3157d4468d616ba17.hook: A change-of-variables or reflection step leaves truncation endpoints that are definitionally equal but syntactically different, e.g. a negated inverse versus the inverse of a negation, and repeated endpoint rewrites fail with pattern not found.
537762ed0032013cbb1977c3157d4468d616ba17.name: defeq-endpoints-need-no-rewrite
537762ed0032013cbb1977c3157d4468d616ba17.body: Stop rewriting. When the surrounding lemma application elaborates, definitional equality closes the goal with no endpoint rewrite at all; rewrites like rewriting the negated-inverse form into the inverse-of-negated form fail on occurrence-matching although the two shapes are defeq. Repeated pattern-not-found on two visibly-equal endpoint shapes is the signature that defeq should be left to do the work.

551d14cf8b7671ede5f461c1b7f6bfd47469de33.hook: when a named Mathlib lemma fails to exist or an algebra-hierarchy coercion blocks a rewrite, retrieve the substitute
551d14cf8b7671ede5f461c1b7f6bfd47469de33.name: mathlib-api-name-shape-traps-with-substitutes
551d14cf8b7671ede5f461c1b7f6bfd47469de33.body: Mathlib tactic/API name-and-shape traps confirmed by compilation failure on a polynomial group-action problem, with working substitutes: (1) `isUnit_of_dvd` does not exist - use `isUnit_of_dvd_unit`. (2) `prime_iff` does not exist - `Prime` unfolds definitionally to an And-triple, so `refine <_,_,_>` splits it directly. (3) `map_C` is not a valid rewrite through an `AlgEquiv` - replace with `AlgEquiv.commutes` + `MvPolynomial.algebraMap_eq` + `C_mul` + `ring`. (4) `MulEquiv.irreducible_iff` needs `.mpr` (not `.mp`) when transporting `Irreducible pi` to `Irreducible (g pi)`. (5) `Finset.prod_val` is stated as `s.1.prod = s.prod id` and needs a trailing `rfl` for eta. (6) Subtype-valued dvd witnesses cannot be `rcases ... with <k, rfl>`-substituted - use `obtain` + `rw`. Also: no `Multiset.countP_le_one` of any shape exists; prove a countP <= 1 bound by Multiset induction (empty/cons constructor names, not zero/cons) from `nodup` plus pairwise-equality of Associated-classified elements. General domain: Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of ring-theoretic divisibility and unit-group arguments.

5d599c2dff7a3a0b1fcd8411a89f96d3f57554eb.hook: Materializing a finite abelian group as independent cyclic subgroups from the packaged ZMod direct-sum equivalence.
5d599c2dff7a3a0b1fcd8411a89f96d3f57554eb.name: finite-abelian-direct-sum-from-zmod-equivalence
5d599c2dff7a3a0b1fcd8411a89f96d3f57554eb.body: PATTERN — the obstacle. Depositing a finite abelian group as a direct sum of cyclic subgroups in a custom encoding (a family of cyclic subgroups that is independent — iSupIndep — and whose supremum is ⊤) has no one-shot Mathlib theorem; the library packages the structure as an EQUIVALENCE to a direct sum of ZMods, and the work is transporting the decomposition across that equivalence. PATTERN — the move. Obtain the packaged decomposition, push each coordinate into G as the range of the composite homomorphism (equivalence inverse composed with DirectSum.of), prove each range cyclic by surjectivity onto the range, and transfer independence and supremum along the equivalence, converting additive-subgroup lattice facts to module lattice facts where the API lives. LEAF — spellings (pinned Mathlib, compiled in the source artifact). AddCommGroup.equiv_directSum_zmod_of_finite' G returns ⟨ι, hι, n, hn, ⟨e⟩⟩ with e : G ≃+ ⨁ i, ZMod (n i). For each i take f i := e.symm.toAddMonoidHom.comp (DirectSum.of (fun i ↦ ZMod (n i)) i) and A i := (f i).range; cyclicity is isAddCyclic_of_surjective (f i).rangeRestrict (AddMonoidHom.rangeRestrict_surjective (f i)). Independence: rewrite with iSupIndep_map_orderIso_iff (AddSubgroup.toIntSubmodule : AddSubgroup G ≃o Submodule ℤ G) then apply iSupIndep_iff_finset_sum_eq_zero_imp_eq_zero; supremum-⊤ from the equivalence's surjectivity. MINED FROM a residual where the finite-abelian half of a direct-sum clause stayed sorry in the custom iSupIndep encoding. No problem identifiers are needed to apply this.

184224fa867d5243078fda332225026ef1451221.hook: Order p·q cyclicity: prove both Sylows normal, derive commutativity, finish with IsZGroup.of_squarefree — no semidirect products.
184224fa867d5243078fda332225026ef1451221.name: order-pq-cyclicity-via-doubly-normal-sylow-and-zgroup-exponent
184224fa867d5243078fda332225026ef1451221.body: PATTERN — the obstacle. 'Every group of order p·q (p < q primes, p ∤ q − 1) is cyclic' is packaged nowhere in Mathlib; a proposed semidirect-product/MulAut route fails because the library does not hand over the action and a ZMod equivalence conclusion is ill-typed. The compiled route avoids semidirect products entirely. PATTERN — the move. (1) Show BOTH Sylow subgroups unique: Sylow.card_dvd_index gives n_p ∣ q and n_q ∣ p; card_sylow_modEq_one plus the hypotheses (p ∤ q−1 kills the n_p = q case; p < q kills the n_q = p case) force both counts to 1. (2) Uniqueness gives normality via Sylow.normal_of_subsingleton. (3) Normal coprime cyclic complements commute: Subgroup.isComplement'_of_coprime decomposes every element as a pair, Subgroup.commute_of_normal_of_disjoint supplies the cross commutations, IsCyclic.commutative.comm the within-factor ones — the group is commutative. (4) Squarefree card gives IsZGroup.of_squarefree, IsZGroup.exponent_eq_card and IsCyclic.of_exponent_eq_card finish with IsCyclic G. Conclude IsCyclic G; do NOT state a G ≃* ZMod (p*q) equivalence. LEAF — spellings (pinned Mathlib, GroupTheory/Sylow.lean, GroupTheory/SpecificGroups/ZGroup.lean, compiled in the source artifact). Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity with Nat.factorization_mul closes the individual Sylow cards p and q; Subgroup.card_mul_index / index_mul_card close the indices; Nat.card_eq_one_iff_unique upgrades count-one to Subsingleton; the squarefree side condition is Nat.squarefree_mul of the two prime squarefrees. MINED FROM a residual that left the order-pq conjunct open after searching for a packaged classification; the pinned artifact closes it exactly this way. No problem identifiers are needed to apply this.

10303a4a34f6611bfba5913a235c8b0974456d85.hook: conjugation action on Sylow conjugates gives hom to S_k with controlled kernel; avoid premature Fin k transport
10303a4a34f6611bfba5913a235c8b0974456d85.name: sylow-conjugation-action-hom-without-premature-fin-transport
10303a4a34f6611bfba5913a235c8b0974456d85.body: PATTERN — the obstacle. Conclusions of the shape 'a group of order m with a nonnormal Sylow p-subgroup admits a hom to S_k with controlled kernel' (conjugation on the k Sylow p-subgroups): agents try to hand-transport `MulAction.toPermHom` across an equivalence to `Equiv.Perm (Fin k)` while simultaneously deriving the normal-Sylow-q conclusion, and the transport plumbing does not fit a 30-minute budget. PATTERN — the move. Keep the action abstract: let G act by conjugation on `{P : Sylow p G}` (the subtype itself); the kernel is the intersection of normalizers, bounded via fixed-point characterization (`Sylow.isPGroup'.sylow_mem_fixedPoints_iff`-style); count conjugates with `card_sylow_modEq_one` and `card_dvd_index` so k is forced; kernel size from Nat.card divisibility inside Equiv.Perm of a k-element type. Introduce an `equivFinOfCardEq`-style reindexing only as the LAST step if the goal literally demands `G →* Equiv.Perm (Fin k)`. LEAF — verified absent: no packaged order-24 classification theorem; `MulAction.toPermHom` is the action-to-hom bridge; Sylow arithmetic lives under `Sylow.` with `card_sylow_modEq_one` / `Nat.card_dvd_index`. These names were located but not compile-verified; check signatures before use. MINED FROM a Student attempt that left the order-24 action conjunct as sorry because transport-plus-conclusion did not fit the budget.

3074204f23b2b4ba9a6e92c87f35eb0b9b8492f0.hook: counting elements of order p: sigma-partition over Sylow p-subgroups, not direct enumeration
3074204f23b2b4ba9a6e92c87f35eb0b9b8492f0.name: count-prime-order-elements-by-sylow-sigma-partition
3074204f23b2b4ba9a6e92c87f35eb0b9b8492f0.body: PATTERN: To count elements of exact order p in a finite group, build an explicit bijection from a sigma type over the Sylow p-subgroups: (Σ Q : Sylow p G, {x : ↥Q // x ≠ 1}) ≃ {g : G // orderOf g = p}. Why it works: every element of order p lies in some Sylow p-subgroup (zpowers of the element is a p-subgroup, then Sylow containment), and two subgroups of order p sharing a non-identity element coincide (both equal zpowers of the shared element), so the pieces are disjoint. LEAF: the coincidence step cannot use Finite.injective_iff_bijective — it is stated for endofunctions (alpha -> alpha) only and fails to elaborate on coercions like ↥(zpowers g); use Fintype.equivOfCardEq or Finite.injective_iff_surjective_of_equiv. Then Nat.card {g // orderOf g = p} = Nat.card (Sylow p G) * (p - 1) under ∀ P : Sylow p G, Nat.card P = p.

0f5e02ae3a0362b366300b24980a740e1ed1932d.hook: A tactic or lemma name that should exist fails with unknown identifier, or a parse error appears far from its cause in a proof using ENNReal/EREal notation.
0f5e02ae3a0362b366300b24980a740e1ed1932d.name: mathlib-v4-29-rename-and-notation-traps
0f5e02ae3a0362b366300b24980a740e1ed1932d.body: Witnessed renames against Mathlib v4.29: measurable_ite -> Measurable.ite (set-membership form), measurable_ennreal_ofReal -> Measurable.ennreal_ofReal, integral_mul_left -> integral_const_mul, Filter.eventually_of_forall -> Filter.Eventually.of_forall, measurableSet_univ -> Measure.restrict_apply_univ, le_or_lt -> le_or_gt. Notation traps: the scoped ENNReal unicode notation fails with 'expected token' unless `open scoped ENNReal` (or the ENNReal prefix) is used, and the spurious instance errors appear far from the cause; absolute-value bars do not nest, so |log |f x|| must be written abs (Real.log (abs (f x))); lt_top/strict hypotheses elsewhere mis-elaborate when the final ne argument is given inline — rewrite with lt_top_iff_ne_top and contradiction instead.

35204bb58026d39869c690da96f72ec0453b56f6.hook: When pulling a constant out of a set integral with integral_const_mul and the rewrite does not fire
35204bb58026d39869c690da96f72ec0453b56f6.name: integral-const-mul-parse-shape-workaround
35204bb58026d39869c690da96f72ec0453b56f6.body: `integral_const_mul` only matches unrestricted integrals AND an integrand parsed as (c * f a)/d, not c * (f a/d). For set integrals use `integral_smul` backwards (scalar multiplication is defeq to constant multiplication on R), then a pointwise `setIntegral_congr_ae` to reshape the integrand, `smul_eq_mul`, and close against the target definition with a defeq rfl.

4ce57b61a29c47958c6f0caa28feafcb9858d9cd.hook: when a subgroup of an alternating group must be shown to equal the whole group and closure brute force or 3-cycle combinatorics stalls
4ce57b61a29c47958c6f0caa28feafcb9858d9cd.name: alternating-closure-via-preprimitivity
4ce57b61a29c47958c6f0caa28feafcb9858d9cd.body: Prove the subgroup IsPretransitive via isPretransitive_iff_base at one base point (enumerate the orbit with the powers of a cycle as a standalone top-level decidable proposition), upgrade to IsPreprimitive with MulAction.IsPreprimitive.of_prime_card when the degree is prime, then apply Equiv.Perm.alternatingGroup_le_of_isPreprimitive_of_isThreeCycle_mem with one explicit three-cycle member. Lean traps: Subgroup.pow_mem takes the subgroup first (Subgroup.pow_mem _ hc7 k); Subgroup.closure has no computable Decidable instance even on a finite group, so never brute-force closure equalities; Subgroup.map_top does not exist — for the subtype map use <- MonoidHom.range_eq_map, Subgroup.range_subtype; fin_cases <;> native_decide fails with 'free variables' because the subtype property stays a metavariable — use a quantified decidable statement instead.

b7f73a89229c7f653e40fa68d090107018168edc.hook: A set integral is over an unbounded complement, while the integrand contains a compactly supported function whose topological support is known to lie in a compact set.
b7f73a89229c7f653e40fa68d090107018168edc.name: localize-an-outer-integral-to-the-declared-support-compact
b7f73a89229c7f653e40fa68d090107018168edc.body: Use setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero to replace the unbounded domain S by K ∩ S: outside K, tsupport containment and subset_tsupport force the function value to vanish. Then norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const applies on K ∩ S, whose measure is finite by compactness, and measureReal_mono replaces its measure by volume.real K. This exposes a support-dependent constant without requiring the original complement to have finite measure.

fd6f7493d70f2e5676924e47cd2723903baac4d0.hook: Constructing a Prime witness or transporting irreducibility across an equivalence: silent field swaps and applied-the-wrong-way iff lemmas.
fd6f7493d70f2e5676924e47cd2723903baac4d0.name: prime-constructor-field-order-and-iff-transport-direction
fd6f7493d70f2e5676924e47cd2723903baac4d0.body: Prime unfolds definitionally to an And-triple ordered (p != 0, not IsUnit p, forall dvd_or_dvd): supplying the first two bullets in the other order compiles the anonymous constructor into wrong projections and produces confusing unit errors, and there is no prime_iff to lean on - refine the triple directly. For irreducibility transport across an equivalence, the iff is stated Irreducible (e x) <-> Irreducible x, so the image-from-source direction is the .mpr (writing .mp gives a backwards application). Round-tripping Prime through Irreducible uses Prime.irreducible then irreducible_iff_prime.mp; prime_iff_irreducible does not exist. Divisibility witnesses: a dvd b unfolds to exists c, b = a * c - twice I supplied a * c = b and got a goal about 1; orient the equation, and remember which side a cancellation lemma cancels on (mul_left_cancel₀ vs mul_right_cancel₀).

5bdb7c7fc417a4e91b45b78d9e960416cb5f621b.hook: A rewrite that clears a division or an inverse inside an inequality is refused — either the name is not found or the pattern is not found — while establishing the positivity, endpoint and change-of-variables side conditions of an integrability estimate whose bounds are quotients.
5bdb7c7fc417a4e91b45b78d9e960416cb5f621b.name: clear-a-division-inside-an-inequality-with-the-subscript-zero-family-and-denominator-positivity

33dafbda9fa47402046fc0bef447b741849d1ee8.hook: A linear operator on compactly supported smooth test functions has support-dependent bounds, so direct continuity in the global LF topology is opaque.
33dafbda9fa47402046fc0bef447b741849d1ee8.name: LF test-function continuity via fixed-support stages
33dafbda9fa47402046fc0bef447b741849d1ee8.body: Factor the operator on each compact support stage `K` through a compact output stage `K'`. Prove the stage map continuous with `WithSeminorms.continuous_of_isBounded` and `Seminorm.IsBounded.of_real`, giving a finite source-seminorm set and constant for every target seminorm. Then apply `TestFunction.continuous_iff_continuous_comp` and compose the stage map with `TestFunction.ofSupportedInCLM`. For primitive-type operators, split order zero (an integral or L1 estimate) from successor orders (differentiate once, then bound the preceding input derivative).

772bf03e1b0b9422976f53b6e9e2e1857db2fea5.hook: when a Lean set-integral subtraction shows a metavariable constant or beta-equivalent exact failures
772bf03e1b0b9422976f53b6e9e2e1857db2fea5.name: set-integral-subtraction-notation-maximal-extension
772bf03e1b0b9422976f53b6e9e2e1857db2fea5.body: PATTERN: In Lean/Mathlib measure theory, a difference of two set integrals written `∫ x in s, f x - ∫ x in s, g x` does NOT parse as two integrals being subtracted: set-integral notation extends maximally right, so this is ONE set integral whose integrand is `f x - ∫ x in s, g x`. Symptom: `Tendsto.sub h tendsto_const_nhds` leaves a metavariable for the "constant", and `exact` on a beta-equivalent statement fails repeatedly with type mismatches that look like a unification or beta-reduction bug but are parenthesization. LEAF: always parenthesize explicitly — write `(∫ x in Ω, F) - (∫ x in Ω, G)` — before debugging anything else; suspect this trap whenever an integral difference produces an unexpected integrand type or a stuck metavariable. Mined from a weak-convergence Tendsto proof that cost ~10 compile iterations before the root cause was found.

1e879934b3d7dd61a1e75e18124baf5a2bcf152b.hook: A finite family has already been shown to span a finite-dimensional module, its cardinality equals the module finrank, and the goal requires a basis with those exact vectors and index order.
1e879934b3d7dd61a1e75e18124baf5a2bcf152b.name: turn a prescribed spanning family into a basis at matching finrank
1e879934b3d7dd61a1e75e18124baf5a2bcf152b.body: Use `basisOfTopLeSpanOfCardEqFinrank` on the prescribed indexed family. Prove its `top ≤ span (range v)` premise by rewriting `top` as the span of any convenient existing basis, then show each old basis vector lies in the candidate span; polynomial identities can make this membership calculation much easier than proving linear independence directly. Supply the cardinality equality from the known finrank. The resulting basis evaluates definitionally to the original family, so `simp` recovers the requested ordered basis equations.

924d7f1c477674b2c637083fb48f1ffe1f65449d.hook: An automorphism is defined over the ground field and fixes the generator of an intermediate adjoin, but a rigidity lemma expects an automorphism over that intermediate field.
924d7f1c477674b2c637083fb48f1ffe1f65449d.name: repackage an automorphism over a fixed simple intermediate field
924d7f1c477674b2c637083fb48f1ffe1f65449d.body: Prove ∀ e : E, σ (e : S) = e with IntermediateField.adjoin_induction. The generator case is the supplied fixed-element equation, the ground-field case is σ.commutes, and the addition, inverse, and multiplication cases follow from map laws. Then define τ : S ≃ₐ[E] S by reusing σ and setting commutes' := fun e => hfixE e. A relative rigidity theorem can now be applied to τ, transferring its conclusion back to σ without constructing a restriction map or proving equality of bundled morphisms.

6659f5f6e96c2eedd2fbe974f8d9fb14e63750de.hook: lp finite approximants from hasSum_single over Finsets, never metric-box exhaustion
6659f5f6e96c2eedd2fbe974f8d9fb14e63750de.name: extract-finite-lp-approximants-from-has-sum
6659f5f6e96c2eedd2fbe974f8d9fb14e63750de.body: Pattern: to approximate an lp element by finitely supported elements over a countable index type, do NOT build a metric exhaustion (ℓ∞-balls or coordinate boxes): a bare countable type carries no metric and has no reason for such balls to be finite, and even on a lattice type Mathlib exposes no ready-made "box partial sums tendsto tsum" lemma to hunt for. Extract the finite approximants from summability itself. Leaf: lp membership supplies summability of the pointwise norms; `lp.hasSum_single` (together with `HasSum` / `SummationFilter.unconditional` / `Metric.tendsto_atTop`) reconstructs the element as a sum of `lp.single` components over Finsets, giving norm convergence along finite sets directly. Where a pointwise involution constraint (e.g. conjugate symmetry) must survive truncation, replace the Finset by its union with its image under the involution; `Finset.subset_union_left` transports the tail estimate to the symmetric hull. For tsum tail bounds the real-valued order lemma is `Summable.tsum_le_tsum` (it requires explicit summability witnesses on both sides, not the bare inequality goal), and once support finiteness is established `tsum_eq_sum` collapses the infinite sum.

ff16c1e044246ea4e3945cb0eab2fbcfbfd9edc7.hook: To prove a continuous piecewise-holomorphic function conservative, a rectangle may lie on one side of the gluing seam, touch it, or cross it.
ff16c1e044246ea4e3945cb0eab2fbcfbfd9edc7.name: split-seam-crossing-rectangles-to-prove-conservativity
ff16c1e044246ea4e3945cb0eab2fbcfbfd9edc7.body: Normalize endpoint order first. Rectangles strictly on either side are handled by `DifferentiableOn.isConservativeOn`; seam-touching rectangles use the corresponding one-sided zero-boundary-integral lemma. For a crossing rectangle, split its boundary integral along the seam, prove interval integrability of the vertical sides from continuity, and cancel the two subrectangle integrals. Finally handle reversed endpoint order by swapping the rectangle and using commutativity of addition. This finite case split supplies the rectangular-integral premise for `Complex.IsConservativeOn` without differentiating the piecewise definition on the seam.

c11e17ed86da66d4bdaa6dc933dc9d4fbb726bcc.hook: An arbitrary splitting-field instance supplies roots of a reciprocal quartic, but the target asks for explicit square-root generators and no packaged API extracts them.
c11e17ed86da66d4bdaa6dc933dc9d4fbb726bcc.name: recover quadratic generators from a reciprocal root
c11e17ed86da66d4bdaa6dc933dc9d4fbb726bcc.body: Choose a root x using IsSplittingField.splits and prove x is nonzero from the polynomial's constant term. Rearrange the root equation to express x⁻¹ as a polynomial in x, then use (x - x⁻¹) / 2 and (x + x⁻¹) / 2 as the hidden quadratic generators. In Lean, clear the powers of 2 with div_pow and div_eq_iff, normalize with ring_nf, and use linear_combination of the root equation and a polynomial multiple of it to certify the two square equations.

59b40939718595bed2f7356c4082c6d0be7d5135.hook: Lean reports failed to synthesize a Module/Module.Finite instance inside a lemma application on a type ascribed through an abbreviation, while the same instance synthesizes in an isolated inferInstance at statement level.
59b40939718595bed2f7356c4082c6d0be7d5135.name: abbrev-vs-def-instance-synthesis-in-application-position
59b40939718595bed2f7356c4082c6d0be7d5135.body: The abbreviation unfolds at instances transparency only in some elaboration positions, creating instance-argument diamonds a haveI will not unify with. Fix: @-application passing each instance as inferInstanceAs cast to the non-abbreviated spelled-out def form of the type (the abbrev spelling fails in argument position where the def spelling succeeds); if diamonds persist across the module structure, set set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false before the theorem — Mathlib's own files in this area set exactly that option. Witnessed: attempt-1 called the same obstruction a hard blocker; attempt-2/3 fixed all instance and range-unification failures this way and the file compiled with zero sorry.

959f12bafb6f0808548764e4352be8518f399d10.hook: coefficient determination at infinity by comparing remainders with monomials under filter-valued lhopital
959f12bafb6f0808548764e4352be8518f399d10.name: asymptotic-coefficients-via-filter-lhopital-remainder-comparison
959f12bafb6f0808548764e4352be8518f399d10.body: Pattern: to determine or kill the coefficients of a real asymptotic expansion at +infinity, compare the remainder after the known partial sum with the next monomial x^(-n) and apply filter-valued l'Hopital; uniqueness of limits then forces the coefficient. Why this class of task stalls: the plan is usually clear, but the obstruction is plumbing - assembling the derivative of the finite partial sum, establishing eventual nonvanishing of the comparison monomial's derivative, and getting the hypothesis shape of the library's l'Hopital lemma right. Leaf: HasDerivAt.lhopital_zero_atTop (Mathlib Analysis/Calculus/LHopital.lean, HasDerivAt namespace) takes EVENTUAL hypotheses (for eventually all x in atTop, HasDerivAt f (f' x) x, for eventually all x in atTop, g' x != 0, both functions tending to 0 at atTop) and a derivative-quotient tendsto, and concludes a function-quotient tendsto to an ARBITRARY filter l - so an atTop/atBot derivative quotient contradicts a finite function limit via tendsto_nhds_unique. The derivative of a finite partial sum comes from HasDerivAt.fun_sum (Mathlib Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/Add.lean), which yields HasDerivAt for a Finset-indexed sum from per-term HasDerivAt facts - do not assemble it by hand. Eventual nonvanishing of the derivative of x -> x^(-n) on atTop is a filter_upwards step with eventually_ne_atTop 0: the derivative is nonzero away from 0.

77e081f60ea5b51edee83e9d7fc959a32720b41a.hook: when FTC or intervalIntegrable fails for an integrand continuous only on the segment
77e081f60ea5b51edee83e9d7fc959a32720b41a.name: segment-local-interval-integrability-and-signed-congr-for-ftc
77e081f60ea5b51edee83e9d7fc959a32720b41a.body: Continuous.intervalIntegrable fails when the integrand is not continuous on the whole line (pole elsewhere); use ContinuousOn.intervalIntegrable with the pole-free continuity established only on the segment (ContinuousOn.div or its div0 variant on the closed segment). The FTC computation goes through intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt; field_simp alone can leave a trivial arithmetic goal — a trailing ring closes it. For transporting an integral equality through IntegrableOn.congr, the pointwise equality must be the UN-signed value, not just a norm equality: state a standalone signed-value lemma first, then congr-transport integrability.

bc3fc791cb4dacb58a9ff0ac82fa14940629f079.hook: when a square-zero endomorphism on a finite-dimensional vector space must be decomposed into blocks and no Jordan-form API is found
bc3fc791cb4dacb58a9ff0ac82fa14940629f079.name: square-zero-classification-by-adapted-complements-dim4
bc3fc791cb4dacb58a9ff0ac82fa14940629f079.body: Pattern: classify a module over k[X]/(X^2), or any space with a square-zero endomorphism T with T.comp T = 0, not by searching for a Jordan or block decomposition API but by adapted complements: range T is contained in ker T via LinearMap.range_le_ker_iff; choose a complement of range T inside ker T and a complement of ker T in the whole space with Submodule.exists_isCompl; build coordinates with Submodule.prodEquivOfIsCompl and Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe. T restricted to the outer complement is an equivalence onto range T, so finrank of range T determines the module type. Leaf: LinearMap.range_le_ker_iff requires T.comp T = 0 stated as a composite; Submodule.exists_isCompl gives a p with IsCompl s p; Submodule.prodEquivOfIsCompl on IsCompl p q gives a product equivalence to V; Submodule.comapSubtypeEquivOfLe on p contained in q; LinearMap.finrank_range_add_finrank_ker. Rank-nullity on dimension 4 forces rank 0, 1, or 2, and each case gives exactly one product type: two cyclic blocks, one cyclic plus two trivial, or all trivial.

908ebb49f0a9663e4a5b415b4ccc0c68431179d1.hook: MemLp of a power-law sequence (n+1)^(-s) for counting measure Measure.count: no packaged lemma exists, so chain integrable_norm_rpow_iff -> integrable_count_iff -> Summable, collapse the norm power ‖‖a^e‖^p‖ to a^(e*p) with Real.norm_eq_abs / abs_of_nonneg (Real.rpow_nonneg) / Real.rpow_mul, shift the successor index with summable_nat_add_iff, then Real.summable_nat_rpow; ENNReal.ofReal side goals (ofReal_eq_zero, toReal_ofReal) only after 0 < p by linarith; the ¬MemLp conjunct goes through .mpr and Real.summable_nat_rpow.not
908ebb49f0a9663e4a5b415b4ccc0c68431179d1.body:
