5924b1000ee829d900b581755731f8dd64a59be8.body: Feed the family of normality proofs to `Sylow.directProductOfNormal`. Pull the two ambient elements back through this multiplicative equivalence, rewrite both ambient products using `apply_symm_apply` and `map_mul`, and reduce equality of the dependent-product values by `funext`. At each prime coordinate, apply the corresponding Sylow subgroup's commutativity proof. This replaces a global element decomposition argument with coordinatewise equality along the library's direct-product equivalence.

e1b8b51db644a1d20ba4cee3b4afbf5170ade85e.hook: A maximal-ideal argument for a polynomial ring needs the contraction along constant polynomials to be maximal, but the theorem is gated by an `IsJacobsonRing` instance for the coefficient ring.
e1b8b51db644a1d20ba4cee3b4afbf5170ade85e.name: Supply a Jacobson-ring instance to contract maximal polynomial ideals
e1b8b51db644a1d20ba4cee3b4afbf5170ade85e.body: Before rebuilding the contraction argument, provide the coefficient-ring instance expected by `Polynomial.isMaximal_comap_C_of_isJacobsonRing`. For the integers, `isJacobsonRing_iff_prime_eq` reduces this to showing every prime ideal equals its Jacobson radical: a nonzero prime ideal is maximal by `Ideal.IsPrime.isMaximal`, while the bottom ideal case follows from `Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot` and `Int.isUnit_iff`. Installing that result locally lets the polynomial theorem turn the contraction of a maximal ideal along `C` into a maximal ideal, after which residue-field and principal-ideal APIs apply.

97f40f4b6a037a5f9a5ad58562de7a36b5bbfc06.hook: Extracting an order fact (nonnegativity, nonpositivity) from a hypothesis like x ∈ Iic 0 or x ∈ Ioi 0 inside an integrand rewrite, or reaching for Filter.eventuallyOf_forall / a Le field projection directly
97f40f4b6a037a5f9a5ad58562de7a36b5bbfc06.name: interval-membership-returns-membership-not-order-projection
97f40f4b6a037a5f9a5ad58562de7a36b5bbfc06.body: Before (attempt 1 tactic-failure register): hx.le used as a nonpos proof fails with a Real.le field error; Filter.eventually_of_forall does not exist as named. After: (1) Set.mem_Iic gives the membership fact, not an order projection - use (Set.mem_Iic.mp hx) as the nonpos proof rather than projecting a Le out of the membership term; (2) the a.e. pointwise-rewrite path is MeasureTheory.ae_of_all volume, not the Filter namespaced eventually_of_forall; (3) inner-product identities like inner R x v = x*v need simp [inner, mul_comm] rather than a single inner lemma. These are signature-shape facts about Mathlib's interval and measure API that cost compile cycles each time they are rediscovered by error.

aeb1f81cf030d14fb0204cb0cec338a5cc7caadb.hook: Conjugating a subgroup by a group element (`g • H` or `MulAut.conj g • H`), transporting a Sylow subgroup along an automorphism, or rewriting `g • (P ⊓ K)` where K is normal.
aeb1f81cf030d14fb0204cb0cec338a5cc7caadb.name: subgroup-pointwise-action-lives-on-mulaut-under-pointwise-locale
aeb1f81cf030d14fb0204cb0cec338a5cc7caadb.body: PATTERN — why conjugation-by-a-group-element on `Subgroup G` fails to typecheck. There is NO instance `HSMul G (Subgroup G)`: the pointwise action on subgroups is a SCOPED instance behind `open Pointwise`, and even with the locale open the natural actor for automorphism-type statements is `MulAut G` (via `MulDistribMulAction`), not `G`. Syntactically `g • (P : Subgroup G)` only typechecks through `Sylow.pointwise_smul_def`. The move: rebuild every conjugation step with `MulAut.conj g` (and `MulAut.conjNormal g` when acting on a normal subgroup), `open Pointwise`, and unfold through `Sylow.pointwise_smul_def` / `Subgroup.pointwise_smul_def`. LEAF — further traps verified in a successful Sylow-restriction proof: (1) `Sylow.map` for a monoid hom does NOT exist; to transport a Sylow along an automorphism of the subgroup, use the `(K ≃* K)` MulAction on `Sylow p K` (that instance does exist). (2) `Subgroup.smul_inf` and `Subgroup.Normal.conj_smul_eq_self` only rewrite after first converting the Sylow coercion with `Sylow.coe_subgroup_smul`; the map/comp transport then still needs an explicit ext-level hom equality proof. (3) `Sylow.exists_comap_subtype_eq` remains the packaged forward direction; the reverse direction is the conjugation/transporter argument above, supported by `Sylow.isPretransitive_of_finite` and `Sylow.coe_smul`. MINED FROM a Student attempt that used the transporter-route memories verbatim in strategy but spent most of its budget rebuilding the action spelling.

b0336d1c7971ee2bafd2ec80c9b54eeb650aed72.hook: when a presented or def-wrapped group must be shown non-solvable (or any property transferred along a surjection)
b0336d1c7971ee2bafd2ec80c9b54eeb650aed72.name: nonsolvability-via-surjection-to-alternating
b0336d1c7971ee2bafd2ec80c9b54eeb650aed72.body: To show a presented group is not solvable, exhibit a surjection onto a known non-solvable concrete group (an alternating group A_n, n at least 5, non-solvable by Equiv.Perm.not_solvable) and use solvable_of_surjective contrapositively: a solvable preimage forces a solvable image, so a non-solvable image witnesses non-solvability of the domain. When the domain's solvability goes through a def-wrapped predicate, instance search fails; supply the hypothesis with letI _inst : IsSolvable G := h before the exact rather than relying on inference.

3af3fe3a780be635d871bbf87d3e7a3659b65676.hook: A decreasing scale sequence partitions points into shells, and domination is meant to come from the first cap that is saturated on each shell.
3af3fe3a780be635d871bbf87d3e7a3659b65676.name: align shell estimates with the next saturated series term
3af3fe3a780be635d871bbf87d3e7a3659b65676.body: If a shell is indexed by δ (n + 1) < x ≤ δ n, the cap at index n + 1 is the term known to equal one. Therefore the continuity estimate available from x ≤ δ n must already be bounded by the coefficient at index n + 1. State the scale estimate with that shifted coefficient before choosing the scales; then the domination step is a direct comparison with one nonnegative summand of the infinite series, discharged by `Summable.sum_le_tsum` on the singleton `{n + 1}`. Keeping the shell index, estimate index, and saturated-term index explicit prevents an off-by-one gap that later monotonicity cannot repair.

a0f3a60744a43418389c5c391e5d0067af92277a.hook: subgroup Fintype: Fintype.ofFinite chain; avoid Nat.card_eq_fintype_card rewrites on coercions
a0f3a60744a43418389c5c391e5d0067af92277a.name: subgroup-fintype-of-finite-not-subgroup-fintype
a0f3a60744a43418389c5c391e5d0067af92277a.body: Two coercion traps when computing orders of subgroup carriers in Lean/Mathlib finite-group files. (1) There is no `Subgroup.fintype` constructor name; `inferInstance` also fails for `Fintype ↑H` even when `Finite G` holds. The working chain is `haveI : Finite ↑H := inferInstance; haveI := Fintype.ofFinite ↑H` -- derive `Finite` for the carrier, then manufacture the `Fintype` noncomputably. (2) Rewriting with `Nat.card_eq_fintype_card` on goals about the coercion of a Sylow/Subgroup term (e.g. the coercion of `default : Sylow p H`) fails with elaboration errors like 'cannot coerce to sort': the lemma's sort metavariable binds to the subgroup term rather than its carrier. Fix by not rewriting at all -- bind the subgroup with `set T := default` and use `Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity` applied to a `Nat.card ↑H` hypothesis directly, mirroring any existing hScard pattern in the file. General rule: for cardinality goals about subgroup carriers, work in `Nat.card ↑_` terms and never route through `Fintype.card` rewrites.

1666e9323430dc4574350b8286e579a00abe0c73.hook: Goal is DifferentiableAt of a function built with Function.update or set-equal-if at a filled singularity; rw [Function.update_of_ne] inside the goal fails and a by_cases elaborates against a lambda-bound variable leaving a stuck TopologicalSpace metavariable.
1666e9323430dc4574350b8286e579a00abe0c73.name: differentiability-transfer-through-filled-singularity-via-eventuallyEq
1666e9323430dc4574350b8286e579a00abe0c73.body: Do not rewrite the update inside the goal: with a set-introduced function the update term is not syntactically present and Function.update_of_ne mismatches. Instead prove a punctured-nhds eventual equality ((Function.update h p v) =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] p] h) via Function.update_apply / if_neg, then transport with DifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq (capital Eq; congr_of_eventually_eq does not exist). State the differentiability of the pole term as a hypothesis-indexed lemma on z ≠ p rather than branching by_cases at the pole. Also DifferentiableOn obligations need .differentiableWithinAt appended to DifferentiableAt facts; differentiable-implies-analytic detours can be replaced by Complex.differentiableOn_compl_singleton_and_continuousAt_iff + DifferentiableOn.analyticOnNhd in one application.

d8a0e7d666f22ca21f1c98eb05402ff29cc6ee6f.hook: Applying filter_upwards directly to an Eventually statement over nhds within (≠) of a point, or using Filter.mono to weaken a ball membership into the punctured filter.
d8a0e7d666f22ca21f1c98eb05402ff29cc6ee6f.name: punctured-nhds-eventually-needs-nhdsWithin-iff-first
d8a0e7d666f22ca21f1c98eb05402ff29cc6ee6f.body: filter_upwards does not intro on a punctured-nhds eventual statement: rw [eventually_nhdsWithin_iff] first, then filter_upwards introduces one binder with the membership reading as t ≠ w after simpa. For weakening a ball-membership into 𝓝[≠] x, the Filter.mono direction is wrong anyway (𝓝[≠] x ≤ 𝓝 x goes the other way); instead rewrite via eventually_nhdsWithin_iff and use isOpen_ball.mem_nhds with field syntax (isOpen_ball.mem_nhds h, not isOpen_ball x r hmem). Also isOpen_ne is applied as isOpen_ne.mem_nhds, not (isOpen_ne x).mem_nhds.

2c4ed465a26e9957eb68013833bfab6501faf771.hook: Retrieve when `decide` cannot reduce a finite kernel on matrices, but the mapped-identity condition is coordinatewise.
2c4ed465a26e9957eb68013833bfab6501faf771.name: Count an oversized matrix kernel through scalar coordinate fibers
2c4ed465a26e9957eb68013833bfab6501faf771.body: Forget the general-linear-group wrapper by an explicit equivalence from the homomorphism kernel to matrices whose image is the identity. Rewrite the matrix subtype as iterated scalar fibers using `Equiv.subtypeEquiv`, `Equiv.subtypePiEquivPi`, and `Equiv.piCongrRight`. Prove the small scalar fibers have constant cardinality, then close the total count with `Fintype.card_pi`; this keeps each decision small and kernel-checked.

b4964cf2543f163d1661c661a969bc9320118e90.hook: A simple subgroup of a finite group is assumed to have an index too small for an injective coset action, but the ambient group rather than the subgroup supplies the action.
b4964cf2543f163d1661c661a969bc9320118e90.name: turn-small-index-subgroups-normal-via-the-coset-kernel
b4964cf2543f163d1661c661a969bc9320118e90.body: Apply simplicity to the normal core viewed as a normal subgroup of the candidate subgroup. If that core were bottom, `Subgroup.normalCore_eq_ker` and `MonoidHom.ker_eq_bot_iff` would make the ambient coset action injective. Compare the ambient cardinality with the factorial of the subgroup index; when the inequality is impossible, the core is nontrivial, hence top inside the simple subgroup. Transport `normalCore.subgroupOf = top` back to `normalCore = H`, which supplies `H.Normal`. This replaces a missing minimal-index theorem with the reusable kernel-and-cardinality argument.

51b661621740ed0e1f7643833978ec317900efe4.hook: Finishing a counting theorem by exhibiting a bijection on fibers or a sigma type, or converting an equicardinal-fiber product formula into a numeric equality.
51b661621740ed0e1f7643833978ec317900efe4.name: equiv-placeholder-and-sigma-counting-finishers
51b661621740ed0e1f7643833978ec317900efe4.body: PATTERN — proof-shape traps when finishing an equicardinal-fiber counting argument with an explicit equivalence. (1) `exact` REFUSES `?_` placeholders inside an anonymous constructor `⟨f, g, ?_, ?_⟩`; use `refine ⟨f, g, ?_, ?_⟩` and then discharge the remaining goals — `exact` on a term with placeholders is a hard elaboration error, not a goal split. (2) When the fiber transport or sigma-type bijection is awkward to invert by hand, use `Equiv.ofBijective`: injectivity of `Subgroup.map` on an injective hom plus a choice-function surjectivity argument; do not build the inverse by anonymous constructor, since Sigma eta is not `rfl` and the two-sided inverse laws will not close by `simp`. (3) The counting corollary comes out ADDITIVE: `Fintype.card_sigma` yields a `∑`, not a `∏`, so the finisher is `Finset.sum_congr` then `Finset.sum_const` (mind that it produces an ℕ-smul `•`, not a `*`) then `Finset.card_univ`, and only then `mul_comm`. LEAF — with the constant-fiber hypothesis in scope the numeric step is `simp [Fintype.card_sigma, Finset.sum_const, Finset.card_univ]`-shaped modulo the smul-to-mul bridge. MINED FROM a Student attempt whose strategy memories matched the residuals verbatim while these three finishing moves consumed the remaining budget.

ef568c59aaa3f8eca4a94223aa7fa8cd4d64a871.hook: Lean linear-algebra work in current Mathlib: check the namespace of toSpanSingleton, liftQ, add_apply, induction_on' case names, (Polynomial F) parentheses, and Ideal-vs-Submodule routing before elaborating.
ef568c59aaa3f8eca4a94223aa7fa8cd4d64a871.name: mathlib-linear-algebra-api-name-drift
ef568c59aaa3f8eca4a94223aa7fa8cd4d64a871.body: In current Mathlib (as pinned by the apm Lean toolchain) the module/linear-algebra namespace has drifted relative to common muscle memory; route kernel/range/span arguments through these exact names: the scalar-span map is LinearMap.toSpanSingleton (NOT Module.toSpanSingleton, which does not exist); apply/zero simp lemmas are LinearMap.add_apply / LinearMap.zero_apply (NOT Module.End.add_apply / Module.End.zero_apply); the quotient-lifting map is Submodule.liftQ (NOT LinearMap.liftQ); Polynomial.induction_on' names its cases add and monomial, not h_add/h_monomial; writing F[X] as an explicit ring argument parses as function application - write (Polynomial F); and comparing an ideal of Polynomial F with a submodule forces routing through restrictScalars, since Ideal (Polynomial F) and Submodule F (Polynomial F) are different types with no automatic identification. All six were hit and worked around in one finite-dimensional-algebra formalization session.

a4b1decb2f8231fa6762be5cbeb235dd4cfd4090.hook: An arbitrary splitting field of a polynomial over a finite field needs an exact degree, and the roots have a simple multiplicative-order relation that controls a small iterate of Frobenius.
a4b1decb2f8231fa6762be5cbeb235dd4cfd4090.name: compute finite splitting degree from Frobenius action on roots
a4b1decb2f8231fa6762be5cbeb235dd4cfd4090.body: Prove the chosen Frobenius iterate fixes each root by rewriting Frobenius iteration as a power and reducing its exponent modulo the roots' multiplicative order. Extend rootwise equality to the whole splitting field with IsSplittingField.adjoin_rootSet and Algebra.adjoin_induction. Prove the smaller Frobenius iterate is nonidentity by evaluating it at a primitive root. Then orderOf_eq_prime gives the Frobenius order, and FiniteField.orderOf_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic identifies that order with Module.finrank. This direct route avoids constructing a canonical finite-field extension or separately excluding every smaller degree.

d632b319f7977f60f900f0cfbaabaf6014af13da.hook: Over a non-pinned Mathlib snapshot, familiar complex/tsum lemma names fail with unknown constant: Complex.norm_eq_abs, Complex.abs_sq, Complex.abs_mul, Complex.norm_sq_eq_re, tsum_le_tsum, tsum_const_mul, isClosed_inter
d632b319f7977f60f900f0cfbaabaf6014af13da.name: mathlib-snapshot-complex-tsum-lemma-renames
d632b319f7977f60f900f0cfbaabaf6014af13da.body: In this Mathlib snapshot (lean toolchain v4.29.0-rc8 era) a working replacement set, compile-witnessed: Complex.norm_eq_abs / Complex.abs_sq / Complex.abs_mul -> Complex.normSq_eq_norm_sq + Complex.normSq_apply; products of conjugates decomposed via Complex.mul_re / Complex.conj_re / Complex.conj_im; tsum_le_tsum (bare, real-valued) -> Summable.tsum_le_tsum hkey hf hg with the three summability arguments; tsum_const_mul -> Summable.tsum_mul_left; isClosed_inter -> IsClosed.inter. Rule of practice: when an error message blames casts or elaboration but the real failure is a name lookup, grep the pinned source instead of re-running coercion tactics; the error text for a missing constant reads like a coercion problem.

22f8b428634f2f8eacfd79b25cc2782ca2dbfe5e.hook: A candidate abelian Galois subextension must be placed below the commutator fixed field, and direct transport of every automorphism is unwieldy.
22f8b428634f2f8eacfd79b25cc2782ca2dbfe5e.name: abelian-subfield-containment-by-reversing-galois-correspondence
22f8b428634f2f8eacfd79b25cc2782ca2dbfe5e.body: Rewrite field containment with IntermediateField.le_iff_le, then rewrite the fixing-subgroup goal backwards with Subgroup.Normal.quotient_commutative_iff_commutator_le. Let IsGalois.normalAutEquivQuotient for the candidate fixed field expose the quotient; Function.Surjective.mul_comm applied to the inverse equivalence transfers the candidate automorphism commutation law to that quotient. Scope: finite Galois intermediate fields. Before: construct restriction maps and chase mapped fields. After: reduce maximality to commutator containment and quotient commutativity. Level: domain. Confidence: high. Evidence: a kernel-checked solver head closed the formerly open universal-property residual with this rewrite.

15a5d7512099dd70a2cc84bae1bd6469c6dbcb6a.hook: Five consecutive unknown-constant probes for plausible lemma names, each costing a compile cycle, in an area where Mathlib certainly has the result
15a5d7512099dd70a2cc84bae1bd6469c6dbcb6a.name: probe-lemma-names-by-grep-not-by-guess-and-compile
15a5d7512099dd70a2cc84bae1bd6469c6dbcb6a.body: When guessed lemma names return unknown constant repeatedly (normality-from-commutativity variants, center-quotient characterisations, action-faithfulness), stop guessing: grep the Mathlib source tree for the area's vocabulary. The grep both ends the loop and supplies the exact spelling and hypotheses of the real lemma, which may need a detour (e.g. a center-kernel-to-cyclic-quotient lemma living in the cyclic-groups file, far from where the goal suggests looking). Obstacle-prose memory queries in parallel did not break the loop; API-name queries and source grep did.

c8d6c9f7b5a0a2e36047a597eb5f6d28c8a71f77.hook: classify automorphisms of C over R by the image of I; the dichotomy ref-or-conjAe via carrier decomposition
c8d6c9f7b5a0a2e36047a597eb5f6d28c8a71f77.name: complex-real-algebra-automorphism-dichotomy
c8d6c9f7b5a0a2e36047a597eb5f6d28c8a71f77.body: Pattern: to classify the R-algebra automorphisms of C (or any field automorphism group presented by a generator), do not search for a group-classification lemma -- there is none in Mathlib. Determine the image of the generator instead: I satisfies I^2 = -1, so (phi I)^2 = -1 forces phi I = plus-or-minus I (via normSq and nlinarith on the imaginary part), and the carrier decomposition phi z = ofReal z.re + ofReal z.im * (phi I) (Complex.re_add_im plus commutation on R-scalars) transfers the dichotomy to every point, giving exactly phi = AlgEquiv.refl or phi = Complex.conjAe. Leaf: the reusable API is Complex.conjAe (the nontrivial R-algebra equiv), Complex.adjoin_I : R[I] = top for the adjoin half, I_mul_I, map_pow, map_neg; the real-coefficient fact is best stated as an explicit have hcom : forall x : R, phi (ofReal x) = ofReal x from AlgEquiv.commutes (defeq) rather than rewriting with commutes directly. A z^2 = -1 implies z = I or z = -I lemma is one nlinarith away and worth banking before the hard bridges. Provenance: mined from f75 student-attempt-1 residual (automorphism dichotomy proved in scratch, packaging/adjoin half unreached).

100aefc728724070d435be514a35fce17054fa7d.hook: when Lean proofs over iterated quotient rings hit timeouts, bogus HasQuotient goals, or missing Ideal.map_singleton
100aefc728724070d435be514a35fce17054fa7d.name: quotient-ring-lean-elaboration-traps
100aefc728724070d435be514a35fce17054fa7d.body: Pattern: elaboration traps in iterated quotient and span computations do not look like errors at reading time; they surface as deterministic timeouts or misleading error text, so the fix is structural parenthesization and proof splitting, not tactic changes. Leaf, four verified pitfalls in Mathlib quotient-ring proofs: first, chained unparenthesized quotient notation parses right-associatively and produces bogus HasQuotient instance goals; always write explicit parentheses such as ((ZMod 2)[X] quotient I) quotient (map mk J). Second, a type ascription inside a set literal, {X : (ZMod 2)[X]} without parentheses, binds the whole set literal and yields a misleading not-a-field-of-structure error; parenthesize the ascribed element. Third, a rewrite into a goal whose type sits under a long DoubleQuot or quotEquivOfEq chain can trigger a deterministic whnf timeout at 200000 heartbeats; the fix is to split the proof into small have steps isolating the rewrite from the heavy ring-equivalence chain, because the timeout comes from re-elaborating the chain, not the rewrite. Fourth, Ideal.map_singleton does not exist in current Mathlib; use simp only [Ideal.map_span, Set.image_singleton] instead.

885b33ca875472d1775db9ad9228b19560e78e71.hook: When an integrand is built from f(y)/(x+y) style division over the reals and AEStronglyMeasurable.div or ContinuousOn.inv fails
885b33ca875472d1775db9ad9228b19560e78e71.name: no-measurable-div-or-continuouson-inv-on-real-integrands
885b33ca875472d1775db9ad9228b19560e78e71.body: `AEStronglyMeasurable.div` and `ContinuousOn.inv` need GroupWithZero/ContinuousInv instance shapes that do not synthesize on expected real-valued forms, so they fail outright. Build the fact structurally: express the integrand as f * reciprocal via `.mul` with `Measurable.inv` (or fun_prop), then transport to the original division form with an a.e. congruence (`setIntegral_congr_ae` / EventuallyEq). For continuity use ContinuousOn.div on components or `ContinuousOn.inv0` where zero-separation is available.

b074989585898dbfaa01897ed3a4bc4b764cbde6.hook: A Sylow subgroup of prime order is self-normalizing in a finite group with a faithful transitive action on p points, and an explicit count of order-p elements or intersections of Sylow subgroups looks necessary.
b074989585898dbfaa01897ed3a4bc4b764cbde6.name: replace Sylow element partitioning with transfer and primitivity
b074989585898dbfaa01897ed3a4bc4b764cbde6.body: Use cyclicity of the prime-order Sylow subgroup to turn self-normalization into normalizer P ≤ centralizer P, then take the kernel N of MonoidHom.transferSylow. Its transfer complement is normal. Prime cardinality makes the transitive action primitive; if N were nontrivial, faithfulness prevents every point from being fixed, so normal-subgroup quasi-primitivity makes N transitive. The stabilizer-index formula would give p ∣ Nat.card N, contradicting MonoidHom.not_dvd_card_ker_transferSylow. Thus N = ⊥ and the complement equation yields P = ⊤. Rewrite rule: scope = faithful transitive prime-degree actions with a self-normalizing prime-order Sylow subgroup; before = partition and count elements of order p across Sylow subgroups; after = apply transfer to obtain a normal complement and eliminate it by primitivity; level = proof shape; confidence = high; evidence-ids = certified solver head and base boundary departure.

37c7ec578c1f5c449bf31742f332d4efd63858d6.hook: build embeddings into S_(m+n) via faithful action on the sum of two coset spaces
37c7ec578c1f5c449bf31742f332d4efd63858d6.name: coset-sum-faithful-action-embedding
37c7ec578c1f5c449bf31742f332d4efd63858d6.body: PATTERN (domain-level): To embed a finite group G into a symmetric group S_(m+n) where m and n are the cardinalities of two quotient coset spaces, do NOT try to construct explicit disjoint cycles from a cyclic-generator isomorphism - Mathlib exposes no packaged MonoidHom or lifting API from a cyclic group determined by a generator image, and hand-rolling the iso plus cycle construction runs to hundreds of lines. Instead let G act faithfully on the disjoint sum (Sum) of the two coset spaces (for example G acting on the quotient by Q of card p and the quotient by P of card q); the kernel of the sum action is trapped in the intersection of the two normal cores, and coprimality or cardinality arguments kill it, often without any normality hypothesis. This yields an embedding into Equiv.Perm of a type of card m+n with a short proof. LEAF (how, exact names): the action kernel is bounded via Subgroup.normalCore_eq_ker plus normalCore_le (the kernel of each coset-action hom is the normal core); injectivity then via MonoidHom.ker_eq_bot_iff; transport to a concretely indexed S_n via an equivFinOfCardEq and permCongrHom helper of the embeds-fin-of-faithful-action shape. PROVENANCE (mined-from): an attempt that first tried the disjoint-cycle-from-generator route, found no lifting API, abandoned it, and closed the goal via the coset-sum action.

14cc44ce096cd4d2b47bafadc80e54fb2f4d44ec.hook: A maximum-modulus argument needs a norm bound on the whole frontier of a ball, but the hypotheses bound the function only on arcs cut out by a strict open condition (upper and lower semicircles by sign of the imaginary part), leaving finitely many frontier points uncovered where the condition degenerates.
14cc44ce096cd4d2b47bafadc80e54fb2f4d44ec.name: extend-frontier-norm-bound-to-arc-degenerate-points-by-continuity-limit
14cc44ce096cd4d2b47bafadc80e54fb2f4d44ec.body: Trigger: frontier-uniform bound required, hypotheses only per-arc on an open condition, so trichotomy leaves equator-type points where neither hypothesis applies. Move: split frontier membership by lt_trichotomy on the sign and dispose of covered arcs directly; for each leftover point build an explicit sequence u n = Complex.exp (((1 / ((n : ℝ) + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I) (or its negation), which lies on the circle (Complex.norm_exp), lies in the covered arc for every n (imaginary part via Complex.exp_ofReal_mul_I_im and Real.sin_pos_of_pos_of_lt_pi with 0 < 1/(n+1) < π), and converges to the point (continuity of exp composed with tendsto_one_div_add_atTop_nhds_zero_nat). Compose ContinuousOn with tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff to keep values in the closed ball, take norms, and close with le_of_tendsto. Reason it works: continuity on the closed ball makes the arc bound closable in the frontier; no hypothesis strengthening and no semicircle-aware theorem search is needed.

353332afd063ec959f2a9cc550a0bd649650c58d.hook: An irreducible cubic splitting field needs a bundled equivalence between its automorphism group and the full permutation group on three roots, but no direct cubic discriminant theorem is available.
353332afd063ec959f2a9cc550a0bd649650c58d.name: identify a prime-degree cubic Galois group through its root action
353332afd063ec959f2a9cc550a0bd649650c58d.body: Use `Polynomial.Gal.galActionHom_bijective_of_prime_degree'` on the canonical splitting field. Supply irreducibility and prime degree, count all roots over an algebraic closure with `Polynomial.card_rootSet_eq_natDegree`, and prove that not all roots lie in the base embedding by bounding the base-field root set. Turn bijectivity into a `MulEquiv` with `MulEquiv.ofBijective`, identify the finite root set with `Fin 3` using `Fintype.equivOfCardEq`, and conjugate permutations with `Equiv.permCongrHom`. Finally transport the result to any abstract splitting field and recover its degree from `IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank`.

1bb6597a2e19853abbc56dd7abe8c17bc0141703.hook: when rw fails with 'Did not find occurrence' on terms equal by a rfl or definitional coercion lemma
1bb6597a2e19853abbc56dd7abe8c17bc0141703.name: normalize-rfl-forms-before-rewriting
1bb6597a2e19853abbc56dd7abe8c17bc0141703.body: When two terms are equal only by a rfl-lemma (Sylow.coe_ofCard is the instance), a rewrite with that equation can fail with 'Did not find occurrence': the goal carries the term in its unexpanded definitional form while the rewrite pattern is the expanded constructor form. Normalize first — rewrite the definitional direction so the pattern you then attack is syntactically present — and only then apply the equality. This is the cast-normalization discipline (normalize casts/coercions before further rewriting) instantiated for definitional coercions of structured constructors (Sylow, submonoid, subgroup coes) rather than numeric casts: normalization is a syntactic prerequisite of the rewrite, not cleanup.

ddf0dcd15431f69726ec963bcb74f8046e07dce1.hook: Embedding between equal-cardinality groups: pull known normal subgroups back by comap instead of rederiving them.
ddf0dcd15431f69726ec963bcb74f8046e07dce1.name: pull-back-normal-subgroup-along-order-equal-embedding
ddf0dcd15431f69726ec963bcb74f8046e07dce1.body: PATTERN — when a subgroup embedding f : G ->* H has Nat.card G = Nat.card H, injectivity plus equal cardinality makes f bijective, so G is isomorphic to H and every structural fact about H (normal subgroups, solvability, simplicity classification) transfers to G by preimage. The move that is easy to miss: do NOT reprove the structure in G; take the known normal subgroup N of H (e.g. the alternating group inside the symmetric group) and form Subgroup.comap f N — it is normal because normality pulls back along any homomorphism, proper because f is surjective and N is proper, nontrivial because f is injective and N is nontrivial. That triple is exactly a non-simplicity witness. LEAF — the equal-card step: injectivity plus Nat.card equality gives bijectivity (e.g. via Finite.card_eq_of_bijective-style counting or Fintype.card equality and Function.Injective.eq_card_of_card_le routes); the preimage spelling is Subgroup.comap_normal, which turns (N.Normal) into ((Subgroup.comap f N).Normal) for any MonoidHom f. MINED FROM a Student attempt that identified a Sylow case as needing G isomorphic to S_5 but did not attempt the transport, leaving the case open.

9aaa95a0952866c155d8aa04c2ede1e462ae20b6.hook: A closed `Nat.factorization` calculation compiles with `native_decide`, but terminal axiom validation forbids the native evaluation axiom.
9aaa95a0952866c155d8aa04c2ede1e462ae20b6.name: remove nativeDecide axioms from closed factorization calculations
9aaa95a0952866c155d8aa04c2ede1e462ae20b6.body: Replace the computation with a certified rewrite chain: use `Nat.factorization_def` at the prime, rewrite the integer as prime times cofactor, apply `padicValNat_base_mul`, and close the cofactor valuation with `padicValNat.eq_zero_of_not_dvd`; `norm_num` discharges primality and divisibility side conditions. Mined from residual: retain a closed Sylow-cardinality computation while removing an axiom rejected by validation.

14299e6708e4e3a01dceafe38831c9a9d5302879.hook: A finite-permutation degree bound should follow from the order of one image element, but direct cycle construction or classification would be cumbersome.
14299e6708e4e3a01dceafe38831c9a9d5302879.name: cycleType lcm and sum API for permutation degree bounds
14299e6708e4e3a01dceafe38831c9a9d5302879.body: Use `Equiv.Perm.lcm_cycleType` to turn divisors of `orderOf σ` into divisors of the multiset lcm. Extract a witnessing cycle length by induction with `Multiset.lcm_cons` and `Prime.dvd_or_dvd_of_dvd_lcm`; use `Multiset.dvd_lcm` for the reverse bound on each cycle length. For two distinct witnesses, move one into `s.erase a` with `Multiset.mem_erase_of_ne` and bound their sum by `s.sum`. Finish with `Equiv.Perm.sum_cycleType` and `σ.support.card_le_univ`.

67171a7b489b0f1e3d1800b55b6996a93258a8db.hook: rw fails "motive is not type correct" under dependent instances, or omega stalls on nonlinear divisibility: use helper lemmas and explicit Nat lemmas.
67171a7b489b0f1e3d1800b55b6996a93258a8db.name: dependent-instance-motive-and-omega-limits-push-to-pure-helper-lemmas
67171a7b489b0f1e3d1800b55b6996a93258a8db.body:
PATTERN - the obstacle. Two tactic failures that look like proof errors but are engine limits. (1) DEPENDENT-INSTANCE MOTIVES: any `rw` that abstracts a variable (a prime `q`, or `Nat.card G`) inside a hypothesis whose type also mentions an object typed over that variable (e.g. `P : Sylow q G`, whose type mentions `q`/`G` through instances) fails with "motive is not type correct". This bites `rw [hcardG] at this`, `rw [← hPcard]`, `rw [hqp] at hmul` — rewriting is not plain arithmetic substitution under dependent instances. (2) OMEGA'S NONLINEAR LIMIT: `omega` closes linear ℕ arithmetic but cannot perform nonlinear cancellation (`idx * p = p * (p+2) ⟹ idx = p+2`) or divisibility contradictions (`p ∣ p+1 ⟹ False`); feeding it these either fails silently or hangs the branch.

PATTERN - the move. For (1): move the whole variable-substitution into standalone PURE-NUMBER helper lemmas (statements only about ℕ literals/variables, no subgroup-typed objects) where `subst` is safe, then apply the helper to the numeric consequences; state the multiplicative facts via a `calc` chain so no hypothesis rewriting is needed in the main proof. Note `subst hqp` with `hqp : q = p` eliminates `p` (the LAST name bound in scope order), not `q` — pass `hqp.symm` when you need the other one. For (2): preemptively name the explicit Nat lemma instead of hoping for `omega`: cancellation via `Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_right` (side condition `0 < p` from `hp.pos`), divisibility differences via `Nat.dvd_sub` (`(a ∣ b) (a ∣ c) : a ∣ b - c`), contradiction from `p ∣ p+1` via `Nat.dvd_one.mp`/`hp.not_dvd_one`-style one-lemma closes. Reserve `omega` for genuinely linear goals.

41248f51c139d25f54fea057fdd1ece1b2d83102.hook: Finite group to show non-simple: derive the Sylow-count candidate set numerically first, then per-case cheapest closers.
41248f51c139d25f54fea057fdd1ece1b2d83102.name: sylow-count-enumeration-dispatch-for-non-simplicity
41248f51c139d25f54fea057fdd1ece1b2d83102.body: PATTERN — why non-simplicity of a concrete finite group stalls: the proof requires a case split on the number of Sylow p-subgroups, but the numeric candidate set is never derived in Lean, so the split has nothing to branch on. The move: derive card P = p^a from Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity, card(Sylow p G) divides the index (Sylow.card_dvd_index) and is congruent to 1 mod p (Sylow.card_sylow_modEq_one); the divisibility list then forces a small finite candidate set for Nat.card (Sylow p G) — do this arithmetic before touching any case. Then dispatch each numeric case by its CHEAPEST closer, not uniformly: k=1 -> Nat.card_eq_one_iff_unique -> Subsingleton -> Sylow.normal_of_subsingleton gives a normal Sylow subgroup (nontrivial, and not top whenever the p-part is proper); small k with k! < card G -> the faithful conjugation/coset action embeds G into Perm of k points, contradicting the card bound; k = index -> the embedding has equal cardinalities, so transfer structure by pulling a known normal subgroup back along the embedding instead of reproving it. LEAF — the faithful-action card bound needs MulAction.toPermHom with MonoidHom.ker_eq_bot_iff for injectivity and Nat.card_perm + Nat.card_fin for the factorial arithmetic (a bare rwa on Nat.card_perm leaves (Nat.card (Fin k)).factorial — close with simp only [Nat.card_perm, Nat.card_fin]). MINED FROM a Student attempt on a group-simplicity problem that closed only the k=3 case inside budget because the enumeration and the other closers were each reinvented from scratch. RATIONALE FOR COINED PATTERN ID: no existing math-formalization pattern covers Sylow-count numeric enumeration and per-case dispatch for non-simplicity; the nearest existing patterns cover only forcing n_p = 1 or counting elements, not the full candidate-set-then-dispatch shape.

a27ab2d966566f3b06c1fdb00bc13249e377e311.hook: A finite group acts transitively on its Sylow subgroups, the action kernel lies in a chosen stabilizer, and the required kernel cardinality is not available as a packaged theorem.
a27ab2d966566f3b06c1fdb00bc13249e377e311.name: Squeeze a permutation-action kernel by its stabilizer and ambient cardinality
a27ab2d966566f3b06c1fdb00bc13249e377e311.body: Use `Sylow.card_eq_index_normalizer` to compute the chosen Sylow normalizer, then identify that normalizer with the Sylow subgroup by containment plus equal finite cardinality. An element of the action kernel fixes the chosen Sylow point, so `Sylow.smul_eq_iff_mem_normalizer` places the kernel inside that Sylow subgroup and makes its cardinality divide a prime power. Enumerate only the divisors of that prime power: the largest case makes the Sylow subgroup normal, while the unit case makes the permutation action injective and is impossible when `Nat.card G` exceeds `Nat.card_perm` of the action set. This squeezes the kernel to the remaining divisor without enumerating group elements.

120e27f929fcf92e3f2449a149748eafcb9ddad5.hook: An abstract finite algebraic extension of the reals must be identified with the complex numbers because a separable polynomial cannot split over the reals.
120e27f929fcf92e3f2449a149748eafcb9ddad5.name: eliminate the real splitting-field branch by counting roots
120e27f929fcf92e3f2449a149748eafcb9ddad5.body: Apply `Real.nonempty_algEquiv_or` to the canonical splitting field. In the real branch, transport `IsSplittingField` along the proposed algebra equivalence, obtain `Splits`, and combine `Polynomial.card_rootSet_eq_natDegree` with separability. Refute that branch by an independent upper bound on the number of real roots, for example via `Polynomial.card_rootSet_le_derivative`. The remaining branch supplies an equivalence with the complex numbers; install the concrete splitting-field instance using `Polynomial.IsSplittingField.of_algEquiv`, then compute automorphisms there and transport them with `AlgEquiv.autCongr`.

f4d0de629b549ddbd0ad39518b189b0789cea268.hook: Sylow counting constraints do not force n_q = 1 when q ∤ |G|; the degenerate branch is structural (order 1 ⇒ subgroup = ⊥).
f4d0de629b549ddbd0ad39518b189b0789cea268.name: sylow-degenerate-prime-branch-is-structural-not-arithmetic
f4d0de629b549ddbd0ad39518b189b0789cea268.body:
PATTERN - the obstacle. In a Sylow-counting argument (prove `Nat.card (Sylow q G) = 1`, typically to feed `Sylow.normal_of_subsingleton` via `Nat.card_eq_one_iff_unique`), the counting congruence `n_q ≡ 1 [MOD q]` plus index divisibility does NOT suffice in the degenerate branch where `q ∤ |G|`. Pure arithmetic admits spurious counts there — e.g. order 15 with q = 2 admits n odd dividing 15, so 3 passes congruence-and-divisibility while no Sylow 2-subgroup count of 3 exists — so the branch genuinely needs a structural fact, not stronger counting.

PATTERN - the move. Split the argument into: (a) `q ∣ |G|` — the counting congruence plus index divisibility DOES force the count to 1 when the factorization has few primes (split q's divisibility through the prime factors, `Nat.factorization` arithmetic); (b) `q ∤ |G|` — go structural: `Nat.factorization_eq_zero_of_not_dvd` makes every Sylow q-subgroup have cardinality one, hence equal `⊥` (`Subgroup.card_eq_one_iff`-style / `eq_bot_of_card_eq_one`), and uniqueness holds because all such subgroups are THE bottom subgroup — `Subsingleton` by `Sylow.ext`/uniqueness of ⊥, not by counting. Do not burn budget searching for a counting route in the degenerate branch; there isn't one.

9d063833d332c870c070818298975f7ed338749f.hook: Building an Equiv or anonymous structure ⟨f, g, ?_, ?_⟩ with tactic placeholders inside the constructor, or counting sigma-type fibers
9d063833d332c870c070818298975f7ed338749f.name: exact-rejects-placeholders-anonymous-constructors-need-refine
9d063833d332c870c070818298975f7ed338749f.body: exact refuses ?_ placeholders inside an anonymous constructor: use refine ⟨f, g, ?_, ?_⟩ and discharge the bullets. A sigma-type bijection rarely closes by rfl/Equiv eta; use Equiv.ofBijective with an explicit injectivity argument (e.g. injectivity of mapping along a subgroup subtype) and a choice-function surjectivity argument. Fintype.card_sigma yields an additive sum, so fiber-count products become ∑-goals: Finset.sum_congr, Finset.sum_const (which produces an ℕ-smul •), and Finset.card_univ, then mul_comm.

b944290b4db1abd3ee7478a3c3e7801521e4faf4.hook: A finite group has a normal cyclic subgroup, but cyclicity or commutativity is blocked by the possible conjugation action of the quotient on that subgroup.
b944290b4db1abd3ee7478a3c3e7801521e4faf4.name: trivialize a finite conjugation action by coprime index bounds
b944290b4db1abd3ee7478a3c3e7801521e4faf4.body: Use the subgroup's normalizer conjugation homomorphism into `MulAut H`. Its kernel is the centralizer, and `QuotientGroup.kerLift_injective` together with `Subgroup.card_dvd_of_injective` shows that the centralizer index divides `Nat.card (MulAut H)`; `Subgroup.index_dvd_card` also makes it divide the ambient group order. If those two cardinalities are coprime, `Nat.eq_one_of_dvd_coprimes` forces the centralizer index to be one, hence `H ≤ Subgroup.center G`. A cyclic central quotient can then be lifted to a commutative group via `commGroupOfCyclicCenterQuotient`; any remaining cyclicity criterion can be applied in the commutative setting.

6e0f9af3d5a37b8956d608dd2ed2d6a0d9fa4f23.hook: A finite group already has an exhaustive conjugacy-class classification, and the goal is to identify every normal subgroup without a decidable enumeration of subgroups.
6e0f9af3d5a37b8956d608dd2ed2d6a0d9fa4f23.name: classify a normal subgroup by representative membership
6e0f9af3d5a37b8956d608dd2ed2d6a0d9fa4f23.body: Normality makes membership constant on each conjugacy class: unpack `IsConj`, apply `Subgroup.Normal.conj_mem`, and use symmetry for the reverse implication. Split on membership of one representative from each nonidentity class. Generator theorems such as `Equiv.Perm.closure_isSwap` and `Equiv.Perm.closure_three_cycles_eq_alternating` turn positive cases into lower bounds; the exhaustive class disjunction turns negative cases into upper bounds. Finish named-subgroup cases with `le_antisymm`. This avoids union-cardinality bookkeeping when representative classes and suitable generators are already available.

3cfa0cc4f4d02c33bc6599e9d630eb1ee312440b.hook: Sylow case dispatch: check k! < |G| per candidate before branching; surviving cases need intersection counting or index arguments.
3cfa0cc4f4d02c33bc6599e9d630eb1ee312440b.name: sylow-case-closer-ladder-cost-order
3cfa0cc4f4d02c33bc6599e9d630eb1ee312440b.body: PATTERN — the Sylow-count case dispatch ladder has a cost order, and the factorial bound is only the SECOND rung: check BEFORE branching whether k! < card G actually holds for every candidate k; when k! >= card G the faithful-action embedding closes nothing and the case survives to the end of the proof. The rungs, in rising cost: (1) uniqueness k=1 -> Nat.card_eq_one_iff_unique -> Subsingleton -> Sylow.normal_of_subsingleton; (2) faithful-action card bound k! < card G; (3) k = index -> order-equal embedding -> pull a known normal subgroup back by Subgroup.comap; (4) when the bound fails, intersect-Sylow element counting (if all pairwise Sylow intersections were trivial, |P|*(k-1) plus smaller-Sylow contributions plus 1 exceeds |G|, forcing two Sylows to intersect nontrivially; the normalizer of that intersection then has index dividing several small factors) — this last rung needs pairwise-intersection cardinality plumbing, so budget for it explicitly rather than discovering it mid-case. Also: before planning an image-in-alternating-group index argument, check whether the library actually proves simplicity (or the needed index facts) for that specific alternating group; if it does not, the index route is not cheap and rung (4) is the real route. LEAF — the failing arithmetic to check up front for a group of order 120: 6! = 720 >= 120 so the candidate n5 = 6 is NOT closable by the card bound; 3! = 6 < 120 closes n2 = 3; 5! = 120 = |G| makes n2 = 5 an equal-card case (rung 3); n2 = 15 survives rungs 1-3 and needs rung 4. MINED FROM a Student attempt that expected the factorial closer to finish a Sylow case and discovered at the case itself that k! >= |G|, with the surviving case needing intersection counting there was no budget left for.

a13c048f48a4964cad4200c979d7df865192f0e0.hook: A linear map preserves a subspace and has triangular matrices on the restriction and quotient, but the target requires one `Fin`-indexed triangular basis of the ambient space.
a13c048f48a4964cad4200c979d7df865192f0e0.name: make-sumQuot-bases-triangular-after-Fin-reindexing
a13c048f48a4964cad4200c979d7df865192f0e0.body: Use `Module.Basis.sumQuot` to combine the subspace and quotient bases. For `Matrix.BlockTriangular id`, split row and column indices into the four `Sum` cases: the diagonal cases reduce to the restriction and `Submodule.mapQ`; invariance makes the lower-left coefficient vanish via `Module.Basis.sumQuot_repr_inr_of_mem`; and the remaining cross-order premise contradicts the placement of the two summands. Reindex first with `finSumFinEquiv`, then with `finCongr` for the finrank equality. Expand `LinearMap.toMatrix_apply`, `Module.Basis.repr_reindex_apply`, and `Module.Basis.reindex_apply` when transporting the coefficient equations.

c852119274f3fc921b83c4c19b52fe404fc82bc4.hook: A finite-group action has been transported to permutations of four points, and kernel-image arithmetic shows that its range has cardinality twelve.
c852119274f3fc921b83c4c19b52fe404fc82bc4.name: Identify an alternating-group image through index two
c852119274f3fc921b83c4c19b52fe404fc82bc4.body: Compute the range index from `range.card_mul_index` after rewriting the ambient permutation-group cardinality with `Nat.card_perm`. Once the index is two, use `Equiv.Perm.eq_alternatingGroup_of_index_eq_two` to identify the range directly with the alternating group. Define the desired map with `codRestrict`; prove surjectivity by rewriting membership through the range equality, and compare kernels extensionally with `MonoidHom.mem_ker`. This avoids choosing or classifying the twelve permutations individually.

6e08aa455bdff265c2b6ec636db611e31bad07f2.hook: when #check on Equiv.Perm.commutator_alternatingGroup_eq_top fails as unknown constant while hunting a perfectness/simplicity fact for alternating groups
6e08aa455bdff265c2b6ec636db611e31bad07f2.name: root-namespace-commutator-alternating-group-lemma
6e08aa455bdff265c2b6ec636db611e31bad07f2.body: commutator_alternatingGroup_eq_top is declared in the ROOT namespace (Perfect section after 'end Equiv.Perm'), not under Equiv.Perm.*. One #check round trip on the unqualified root name settles it; do not conclude the lemma is absent and reroute the proof around a lemma that exists under a different qualification. Same trap class as card_support_eq_three_iff (root, not Equiv.Perm.).

47eb3bb58a6a42571d298901ef67282c8befbf03.hook: lp eval continuity and coercion API: norm_apply_le_norm, coeFn_* rewrites, completeSpace_coe
47eb3bb58a6a42571d298901ef67282c8befbf03.name: lp-evaluation-continuity-and-coercion-api
47eb3bb58a6a42571d298901ef67282c8befbf03.body: Pattern: continuity of Fourier/coordinate evaluation u ↦ u k on `lp (fun _ => ℂ) 2` must be packaged by hand; the PiLp name (`PiLp.continuous_apply`) does not exist in the lp spelling (`lp.continuous_apply` is an unknown constant). Leaf: the bound is `lp.norm_apply_le_norm hp f i` (requires `hp : 1 ≤ p`), giving ‖f i‖ ≤ ‖f‖; package the eval as `LipschitzWith 1` via `lipschitzWith_iff_dist_le_mul`. Coercion frictions that cost real time on any lp problem: `map_sub` FAILS on the lp function coercion — rewrite first with `lp.coeFn_sub` (and siblings `lp.coeFn_add`, `lp.coeFn_smul`, `lp.coeFn_zero`), then apply `Pi.sub_apply`; `ENNReal.two_ne_zero` does not exist for the literal `(2 : ℝ≥0∞)` (use `by simp`); and the `1 * dist` cast mismatch between ℝ≥0 and ℝ resists `one_mul`/`gcongr`/`exact_mod_cast` — close it with `.trans_eq (by push_cast; ring)`. For closedness/completeness of a subtype of lp: the closed-subtype-is-complete lemma is `IsClosed.completeSpace_coe`, NOT `IsClosed.completeSpace` (which the environment does not contain).

d3fc248d8e12b7c9bb728c27853d5ea1d0d78b16.hook: A periodic or symmetric real function has an integrable singular majorant on one fundamental subinterval, but the goal asks for integrability on a full period.
d3fc248d8e12b7c9bb728c27853d5ea1d0d78b16.name: transport-integrability-across-finite-symmetry-partitions
d3fc248d8e12b7c9bb728c27853d5ea1d0d78b16.body: Promote the local IntegrableOn result to IntervalIntegrable, transport it with comp_sub_left or comp_add_right, use IntervalIntegrable.congr to rewrite by exact symmetry identities, normalize affine endpoints with ring, and join adjacent pieces with trans. Convert back to IntegrableOn only after assembling the full interval. This avoids fragile repeated measurable-set union proofs and works when singular endpoints are harmless almost everywhere.

789a8b69da5463a2a1f6a2e2fa2abd90e3c7190c.hook: rw fails to rewrite under a structure projection or an algebraMap coercion: rw [AlgEquiv.commutes] cannot rewrite 'φ ↑z.re' because the ofReal coercion does not syntactically match the algebraMap pattern; rw [Complex.conj_re] cannot rewrite (conjAe z).re because the bundled-equiv projection is not syntactically starRingEnd z.
789a8b69da5463a2a1f6a2e2fa2abd90e3c7190c.name: defeq-show-before-rw-on-coercions-and-projections
789a8b69da5463a2a1f6a2e2fa2abd90e3c7190c.body: When a rewrite lemma's LHS does not match because the goal carries a definitionally-equal but syntactically-different form, bridge with an explicit `show`: `show ... = (starRingEnd ℂ z).re` then rw, or introduce `hcom : ∀ x, φ (ofReal x) = ofReal x := fun x => AlgEquiv.commutes φ x` (defeq) and `simp only [hcom]`. Never fight the coercion with more rewrite lemmas — one defeq-show realigns the syntax. Also: Complex.ext_iff named args misfire ('Type mismatch ... expected Prop'); extract the equality first, then nlinarith on e.g. (z.im-1)(z.im+1)=0 instead of hunting a sq_eq_one variant that does not exist.

aa11a72d8339961423214bbf31f7c8fff00ff8fd.hook: A polynomial relation is known only on a proposed cyclic generator, but a quotient calculation needs the kernel of its scalar-span map to equal the annihilator of the whole polynomial module.
aa11a72d8339961423214bbf31f7c8fff00ff8fd.name: orbit-generator-relation-to-global-annihilator
aa11a72d8339961423214bbf31f7c8fff00ff8fd.body: Rewrite rule — scope: polynomial evaluation on a spanning orbit; before: try to prove bounded powers linearly independent from degree inequalities; after: prove that any polynomial killing the generator kills every orbit vector by commuting its evaluation with powers of the endomorphism, extend from the orbit range using `Submodule.span_le`, and identify the generator kernel with `Module.annihilator`; level: domain technique; confidence: high; evidence-ids: certified solver diff and direct Lean closure. The reverse inclusion is immediate from `Module.mem_annihilator`. Once the kernels agree, the quotient/range finrank calculation recovers the minimal-polynomial degree without coefficient-level relation bookkeeping.

e968b2374a79781a53ff519220810a4ded1fbb04.hook: under a Lean budget, skeleton-then-compile beats API pre-verification; let errors drive lookups
e968b2374a79781a53ff519220810a4ded1fbb04.name: compiler-driven-api-lookup-over-preverification
e968b2374a79781a53ff519220810a4ded1fbb04.body: Pattern: under a fixed attempt budget in Lean, do not spend it on API pre-verification (grep rounds confirming lemma names and signatures) before writing any compiling proof line. Write the full proof skeleton with sorry at each unknown first, compile, and let the compiler errors drive each API lookup -- an error names the exact goal shape a lemma must match, so each lookup is one candidate instead of a survey. Measured cost of the opposite order (f75 student-attempt-2): most of a 30-minute budget went to verifying galActionHom, autCongr, of_algEquiv, Eisenstein absence, and Rat.reduced names before any proof line existed, leaving no time to iterate on the actual obstacle. Sequencing rule: skeleton first, lookups on demand, bank each compiling piece before the next. Provenance: mined from f75 student-attempt-2 process-failure entry.

c2b82fd6b2c46c169186409d9ba731bc39442a55.hook: A point-subtracted singular integral must satisfy a compact-support-dependent bound by the sum of global suprema of a test function and its first derivative.
c2b82fd6b2c46c169186409d9ba731bc39442a55.name: split-a-regularized-singular-integral-into-derivative-and-support-costs
c2b82fd6b2c46c169186409d9ba731bc39442a55.body: Near the singular point, rewrite the subtracted numerator through `dslope`; the remaining sign factor has norm at most one, and `convex_univ.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le` bounds the slope by the derivative `sSup`. On the complement, first use `setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero` to restrict integration to the intersection with the prescribed compact support, then apply `norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const` and `measureReal_mono`. The certified witness obtains a constant of the form fixed local measure plus `volume.real K`, so enclosing the compact set in a separate interval is unnecessary.

9e37c18fa38e3fcfc454880ad3f43046dba0774d.hook: A concrete `Nat.factorization n p = k` goal must be proved without native evaluation, and direct simplification leaves `padicValNat` unevaluated.
9e37c18fa38e3fcfc454880ad3f43046dba0774d.name: certify concrete prime exponents by divisibility bounds
9e37c18fa38e3fcfc454880ad3f43046dba0774d.body: Install `Fact (Nat.Prime p)`, unfold the factorization just far enough to expose `padicValNat`, and bound the valuation from both sides using `padicValNat_dvd_iff_le`: prove `p^k ∣ n` for the lower bound and refute `p^(k+1) ∣ n` for the upper bound. After those divisibility facts are discharged by `norm_num`, `omega` identifies the valuation exactly. This proof shape is kernel-certified and works even when the cofactor-oriented valuation rewrite chain is awkward.

c385254f4d3f2d7c0b763598bb0b8b62ba52b1cf.hook: An infinite family of distinct nonzero eigenvalues is bounded away from zero, and the library exposes the eigenvalue and compact-image APIs but no packaged spectral-finiteness theorem.
c385254f4d3f2d7c0b763598bb0b8b62ba52b1cf.name: compactness contradiction from an invariant finite-span flag
c385254f4d3f2d7c0b763598bb0b8b62ba52b1cf.body: Enumerate the spectral values with `Infinite.natEmbedding`, convert each nonzero spectral value using `IsCompactOperator.hasEigenvalue_iff_mem_spectrum`, choose eigenvectors, and obtain linear independence with `Module.End.eigenvectors_linearIndependent'`. Let `V n` be the span of the first `n` eigenvectors; `FiniteDimensional.span_of_finite` and `Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional` make each stage closed, while linear independence makes each successor proper. Apply `riesz_lemma_of_lt_one` to the comap of `V n` in `V (n+1)` to choose unit vectors uniformly far from the preceding span. Prove the spans invariant under the operator and show `A y - μ n • y ∈ V n` on the successor span. The eigenvalue norm lower bound then yields pairwise-separated operator images. Finally use `IsCompactOperator.image_closedBall_subset_compact`, `IsCompact.tendsto_subseq`, and `Metric.cauchySeq_iff'`; the convergent subsequence contradicts the separation. This is the reusable bridge from infinitely many eigenvalues away from zero to failure of compactness.

b2defb6e69e1aa681540f51aa2e73132c1a65e57.hook: Applying the mean-value/slope lemma exists_deriv_eq_slope on a compact interval to extract a point where deriv equals the secant slope.
b2defb6e69e1aa681540f51aa2e73132c1a65e57.name: exists-deriv-eq-slope-argument-order
b2defb6e69e1aa681540f51aa2e73132c1a65e57.body: exists_deriv_eq_slope takes (f, hab : a < b, ContinuousOn f [a,b], DifferentiableOn f (a,b)) in that order and returns c ∈ (a,b) with deriv f c = (f b - f a)/(b - a). Misordered first attempts fail with errors that look mathematical but are not: 'expected ?m < ?m' (passing the interval before the strict inequality) and 'hypothesis of sort Prop but expected ℝ → ℝ' (passing a hypothesis where the function is expected). Check the signature with #check before re-ordering the mathematical argument.

af019a75d85ca93683e361610612b896dd4a1669.hook: A linear-in-distance estimate is known only near a distinguished point, while continuity on a compact domain gives only a constant bound away from it.
af019a75d85ca93683e361610612b896dd4a1669.name: Patch a local linear estimate with compact boundedness
af019a75d85ca93683e361610612b896dd4a1669.body: Let the local estimate hold for `d z < r` with `0 < r`, and let `q z ≤ M` globally with `0 ≤ M`. Split on `d z < r`. Inside, retain the local coefficient `K`. Outside, `r ≤ d z` and nonnegativity give `M = (M / r) * r ≤ (M / r) * d z`; therefore `K + M / r` works on both regions. In Lean, the key rewrites are `div_mul_cancel₀ M hr.ne'`, `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left`, and a final coefficient comparison by `mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right`.

1b83fec0094eb874bd98a3761c603461f4697b35.hook: You are about to project a parity lemma off an Even/Odd hypothesis on naturals (h.not_odd, h.not_even, h.even_iff_not_odd) and the elaborator rejects it as an invalid field or unknown identifier.
1b83fec0094eb874bd98a3761c603461f4697b35.name: parity-dot-notation-is-existential-use-rcases-omega
1b83fec0094eb874bd98a3761c603461f4697b35.body: Even and Odd on Nat are plain existential definitions, so dot-notation lemma names do not exist off them even when the underlying fact is true. Do not probe dot notation; rcases both parity hypotheses into their witnesses and close the linear contradiction with omega. Note omega closes a False goal outright, so any trailing simp afterwards fails with 'No goals to be solved' — that is success, not failure. Witnessed compiling clean across three attempts after the replacement.

707b5b1388b874bb3235fa0b1273aa6e9592f8cc.hook: After evaluating a set integral of a constant over a real interval with integral_const, the goal retains an ENNReal coercion such as ofReal (b - a) or ofReal (pi/2) that simp alone does not remove, blocking a numeric closing step.
707b5b1388b874bb3235fa0b1273aa6e9592f8cc.name: clean-the-ennreal-ofreal-coercion-left-by-integral-const-with-a-nonneg-side-fact
707b5b1388b874bb3235fa0b1273aa6e9592f8cc.body: integral_const on a real interval expresses the value through volume and leaves an ENNReal-to-real coercion of the interval length. Do not hunt for an ofReal_eq_coe-style lemma name; instead establish the length nonnegativity as a side fact (0 <= pi/2, or sub_nonneg of ordered endpoints), then `simp` with that fact in scope reduces the coercion to the plain real arithmetic, after which norm_num/omega-style numeric closure applies. Pattern: prove the real ordering fact first, then simplify the coercion, rather than rewriting the coercion itself.

47333a5740ab229ca65dce278198be062a632edd.hook: A coset action must be shown faithful, its kernel is a normal core, and the stabilizer subgroup has prime cardinality.
47333a5740ab229ca65dce278198be062a632edd.name: prime-order normal core dichotomy for coset faithfulness
47333a5740ab229ca65dce278198be062a632edd.body: Regard the normal core as a subgroup of the prime-order stabilizer and apply the bottom-or-top dichotomy for subgroups of a prime-cardinality group. Transport bottom back to a trivial ambient core; transport top back to equality with the stabilizer and hence normality. A known non-normality hypothesis eliminates the top case, so the coset-action kernel is bottom and the action is faithful.

a14ebba9e779c4e2daf926118c6be150825fd9d1.hook: Riesz vectors are far from earlier invariant spans, but compactness concerns their operator images and a quantitative separation bound is still missing.
a14ebba9e779c4e2daf926118c6be150825fd9d1.name: derive operator-image separation from the eigenvalue shift modulo an earlier span
a14ebba9e779c4e2daf926118c6be150825fd9d1.body: For eigenvalues `mu n` and `V n` the span of earlier eigenvectors, prove both `A (V n) <= V n` and `A y - mu n • y ∈ V n` for `y ∈ V (n+1)` by `Submodule.span_induction`. For `m < n`, scale the difference between `A (w m)` and the shift remainder of `w n` by `(mu n)⁻¹` to obtain an element `u ∈ V n`; algebra gives `mu n • (w n - u) = A (w n) - A (w m)`. The Riesz lower bound on `w n - u`, multiplied by the spectral cutoff below `norm (mu n)`, yields pairwise separation of the operator images. This was mined from a residual where distinct nonzero eigenvalues had already supplied a strict finite-span flag.

72788bc5027193a12e096d23b0f066aa6b98dd55.hook: Some subgroup has the needed cardinality, but a normalizer argument requires a container of that cardinality around one prescribed Sylow subgroup.
72788bc5027193a12e096d23b0f066aa6b98dd55.name: align a subgroup container by Sylow conjugacy before bounding the normalizer
72788bc5027193a12e096d23b0f066aa6b98dd55.body: Choose a Sylow subgroup of the available container, map it into the ambient group, and use `MulAction.exists_smul_eq` on ambient Sylow subgroups. Map the entire container by the corresponding `MulAut.conj`; `MulEquiv.subgroupMap` preserves cardinality and the mapped inclusion identifies the chosen Sylow subgroup with the prescribed one. Prove the prescribed subgroup normal inside the conjugated container by index arithmetic or Sylow counting. Then `Subgroup.normal_subgroupOf_iff_le_normalizer` places the container below the ambient normalizer, and `Subgroup.card_dvd_of_le` converts containment to the divisibility that selects a normalizer-cardinality alternative. Rewrite rule: scope = finite-group normalizer dichotomies; before = try to force the originally supplied container to contain the fixed Sylow subgroup; after = conjugate the whole container to align its Sylow subgroup first; level = proof shape; confidence = high; evidence-ids = certified solver head. Mined from residual: refine a two-valued normalizer-cardinality conclusion using existence of subgroups of the candidate cardinalities.

8c4b182c82eaab7ba6184242f05015206bed3b67.hook: A perfect finite group would have a subgroup of small index, so its coset action lands in a symmetric group known to be solvable.
8c4b182c82eaab7ba6184242f05015206bed3b67.name: exclude-small-index-subgroups-by-perfect-image-in-a-solvable-symmetric-group
8c4b182c82eaab7ba6184242f05015206bed3b67.body: Use `MulAction.toPermHom` on the cosets. The range inherits `Group.IsPerfect` from the source and `IsSolvable` from the ambient symmetric group. A nontrivial perfect group cannot be solvable, so the range is subsingleton. Transitivity of the coset action then makes the coset type subsingleton, contradicting the asserted index. For a concrete small degree, transport the symmetric group along an equivalence with `Fin k` and establish solvability there.

4c9b10178bb6b483f7324e4ccae0af89d2a31491.hook: A lintegral finiteness bound must exclude a level set of f almost everywhere, but f is only AEStronglyMeasurable under an Integrable hypothesis, so the level set itself is nonmeasurable and indicator/lintegral_mono routes fail.
4c9b10178bb6b483f7324e4ccae0af89d2a31491.name: prove-ae-nonvanishing-of-aesm-function-via-strongly-measurable-representative
4c9b10178bb6b483f7324e4ccae0af89d2a31491.body: Do not bound the indicator of the level set of f: MeasurableSet synthesis fails since f need not be measurable. Instead destructure the AEStronglyMeasurable hypothesis directly (it is an existential over StronglyMeasurable g plus an a.e. equality; there is no projection lemma), build the branchy target function as a mirror on g (which IS measurable), transfer the a.e. property from f to the mirror under the restricted measure via ae_restrict_iff and Filter.Eventually on the a.e.-equality, then close with AEMeasurable.congr and ae_lt_top on the measurable representative. The nonmeasurability of the level set of a merely a.e.-measurable function is the whole obstruction; the measurable representative is the whole cure.

138989c30a568258d71ab9ca13572a3ae96408d4.hook: Some subgroup has the needed cardinality, but a normalizer argument requires a container of that cardinality around one prescribed Sylow subgroup.
138989c30a568258d71ab9ca13572a3ae96408d4.name: align a subgroup container by Sylow conjugacy before bounding the normalizer
138989c30a568258d71ab9ca13572a3ae96408d4.body: Choose a Sylow subgroup of the available container, map it into the ambient group, and use `MulAction.exists_smul_eq` on ambient Sylow subgroups. Map the entire container by the corresponding `MulAut.conj`; `MulEquiv.subgroupMap` preserves its cardinality. After proving the prescribed subgroup is normal in the conjugated container, `Subgroup.normal_subgroupOf_iff_le_normalizer` yields containment in the ambient normalizer, and `Subgroup.card_dvd_of_le` turns containment into the divisibility that selects a normalizer-cardinality alternative. Rewrite rule: scope = finite-group normalizer dichotomies; before = try to make the originally supplied container contain the fixed Sylow subgroup; after = conjugate the container to align its Sylow subgroup first; level = proof shape; confidence = high; evidence-ids = certified solver head. Mined from residual: refine a normalizer-size dichotomy using existence of a subgroup of one candidate size.

17e8bb0a9d91139ecbdf0468bbf5fb5add291f05.hook: A linearly independent eigenvector sequence gives finite spans V n and the proof needs unit vectors in V (n+1) uniformly separated from V n.
17e8bb0a9d91139ecbdf0468bbf5fb5add291f05.name: apply Riesz lemma inside each successor span
17e8bb0a9d91139ecbdf0468bbf5fb5add291f05.body: Give `V n` finite dimension with `FiniteDimensional.span_of_finite`, then obtain `IsClosed (V n : Set X)` from `Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional`. To use `riesz_lemma_of_lt_one` at a successor stage, work in the normed subtype `V (n+1)` and set its closed proper subspace to `Submodule.comap (V (n+1)).subtype (V n)`. Closedness is transported by `(hVclosed n).preimage continuous_subtype_val`; properness is witnessed by the next independent eigenvector. The resulting subtype vector has norm one and is far from every earlier-span vector after coercion. This was mined from a residual requiring a Riesz-separated sequence from an invariant flag of finite eigenvector spans.

4b11888448add52a2dfbc2170e35b196cf308c13.hook: A finite-dimensional endomorphism goal relates the span of one vector's iterates to the degree of the minimal polynomial, while a direct bounded-Krylov independence proof has poor library support.
4b11888448add52a2dfbc2170e35b196cf308c13.name: cyclic-orbit-span-via-annihilator-quotient
4b11888448add52a2dfbc2170e35b196cf308c13.body: Treat the evaluation type as a module over the polynomial ring. Obtain an element whose `LinearMap.toSpanSingleton` kernel equals the module annihilator, rewrite that annihilator as `Ideal.span {minpoly F T}`, and compose `Submodule.quotEquivOfEq` with `LinearMap.quotKerEquivRange`. After restricting scalars, `finrank_quotient_span_eq_natDegree` computes the cyclic range's field dimension. Map this range back through `Module.AEval'.of T` and identify it with the span of the powers by `Module.AEval'.X_pow_smul_of`; equality with ambient finrank then gives topness via `Submodule.eq_top_of_finrank_eq`. This avoids manufacturing a bounded Krylov basis and transfers to any polynomial-action cyclicity problem with an identifiable annihilator.

5365d5dfbe1a7750e51f8ec9566d029a1203382c.hook: A finite group acts faithfully on exactly p points, p is prime, and p divides the group order; the obstacle is proving that a Sylow p-subgroup has order exactly p.
5365d5dfbe1a7750e51f8ec9566d029a1203382c.name: bound Sylow order through a faithful prime-degree permutation action
5365d5dfbe1a7750e51f8ec9566d029a1203382c.body: Apply Subgroup.card_dvd_of_injective to MulAction.toPermHom to get Nat.card G ∣ p.factorial after rewriting Nat.card_perm. Compare Nat.factorization values: Nat.factorization_factorial shows that p has multiplicity one in p!, while Prime.dvd_iff_one_le_factorization supplies the lower bound from p ∣ Nat.card G. Sylow.card_eq_multiplicity then forces Nat.card P = p.

fde626863155762e4c9f36ee8bdf1c1de6b895ca.hook: simpa on a subgroup-membership or kernel-membership goal simplifies to True or makes no progress, suggesting a lost hypothesis.
fde626863155762e4c9f36ee8bdf1c1de6b895ca.name: kernel-membership-close-by-defeq-exact
fde626863155762e4c9f36ee8bdf1c1de6b895ca.body: A subtype coercion's property is definitionally the kernel/membership condition: for z in the kernel-as-subtype, (z : G) in ker f is defeq to z.2, so exact z.2 works directly. Attempts to spell the definitional unfolding out with simpa [MonoidHom.mem_ker, ...] over-simplify (goal becomes True while the hypothesis is genuinely there) and fail. Stop simplifying; offer the definitional term with exact. Instance of the defeq-endpoints-no-rewrite pattern in the subgroup-kernel setting.

9ac68ff01afa25b07781c7fd08aec076cafd9a2c.hook: a goal mixes a bundled morphism coe (MulEquiv, MonoidHom) with an algebra operation the morphism law governs, and simp reports 'made no progress'.
9ac68ff01afa25b07781c7fd08aec076cafd9a2c.name: mulequiv-membership-by-explicit-map-lemma-not-simp
9ac68ff01afa25b07781c7fd08aec076cafd9a2c.body: simp does not unfold a MulEquiv coe into the map_* lemma family. For a membership goal e x ^ k = 1 with e : M =~* N, rewrite explicitly in the direction that consumes the hypothesis: rw [<- map_pow e x k, hx, map_one]. Dually, when simpa on a subgroup-kernel membership simplifies the goal to True, the membership is already definitional (subtype property is defeq to the kernel condition); plain exact z.2 closes where simpa [MonoidHom.mem_ker, powMonoidHom] over-simplifies and fails. Both halves witnessed by compile in the attempt's appended lemmas (profile invariance under MulEquiv and the subtype-to-ker equivalence).

848c2d725c5a612656067f99a31341f25fce91b8.hook: A standalone Lean file proving facts about the imaginary unit or Complex structures fails weirdly: norm_num and rw make no progress on expressions involving I, errors point at I.re or I being an unknown local. Happens in any scratch file about ℂ automorphisms or complex roots.
848c2d725c5a612656067f99a31341f25fce91b8.name: bare-i-auto-bound-fresh-local-complex
848c2d725c5a612656067f99a31341f25fce91b8.body: Without `open Complex`, bare `I` in a standalone Lean file is silently auto-bound as a fresh local variable of type ℂ (the context line `I z : ℂ` gives it away), making `I.re` irreducible to norm_num and rw. Diagnose by reading the local-context line before debugging tactics; fix by opening Complex or writing `Complex.I` explicitly. Auto-bound identifiers masquerade as tactic failures — check the context, not the tactic.

273a2dd22601b4cc7978578615b06e43b9687ef3.hook: Two divisibility-ordered cyclic-product presentations of the same finite commutative group must be proved equal, but total cardinality does not determine the factors.
273a2dd22601b4cc7978578615b06e43b9687ef3.name: recover-normalized-cyclic-factors-from-power-kernel-profiles
273a2dd22601b4cc7978578615b06e43b9687ef3.body: Parent pattern: math-formalization/recover-invariant-factors-from-power-kernel-cardinalities. Compare, for every natural k, the cardinality of the kernel of `powMonoidHom k`. Multiplicative equivalences preserve this kernel cardinality; on `Multiplicative (ZMod n)` use `IsCyclic.card_powMonoidHom_ker` and `Nat.card_zmod` to obtain `n.gcd k`, while `Nat.card_pi` turns a finite product into the product of these gcds. For positive divisibility chains, evaluate the profile at each last factor: saturation says every entry divides that factor, so equality of profiles gives mutual divisibility of the two last factors. Cancel their positive gcd contribution, recurse on `List.dropLast`, and reconstruct with `List.dropLast_append_getLast`. Mined from a residual where uniqueness of normalized invariant factors remained after group cardinality had already been identified with the product of the factors.

3b7631b0302c6170afdc03aff48b7066e8a1c775.hook: A finite Galois fixed field must be shown abelian, but its automorphism group is available only through a quotient equivalence.
3b7631b0302c6170afdc03aff48b7066e8a1c775.name: commutator-fixed-field-abelianness-via-the-normal-automorphism-quotient
3b7631b0302c6170afdc03aff48b7066e8a1c775.body: For the commutator subgroup H of the ambient automorphism group, install H.Normal and IsGalois on fixedField H. IsGalois.normalAutEquivQuotient H identifies the fixed field's automorphisms with the quotient. Prove the quotient commutative using Subgroup.Normal.quotient_commutative_iff_commutator_le.mpr le_rfl, then use Function.Surjective.mul_comm on the equivalence's toMulHom; reverse the resulting equality if the equivalence orientation produces the opposite order. Mined from the residual of proving that a commutator fixed field supplies an abelian Galois object despite the absence of a single packaged fixed-field theorem.

65beeab25afa18533b35a2329c129ab1916f6515.hook: Differentiating a term written with a natural-exponent encoding (c / y ^ i) using Mathlib's zpow-based derivative API.
65beeab25afa18533b35a2329c129ab1916f6515.name: zpow-derivative-api-cast-normalization-gap
65beeab25afa18533b35a2329c129ab1916f6515.body: hasDerivAt_zpow takes (m : ℤ) (x) (h : x ≠ 0 ∨ 0 ≤ m) positionally; passing the nonneg disjunct first fails with 'unsolved goals ℤ'. Its derivative value is spelled ((m : R) * x ^ (m - 1)) with an Int.cast, so hand-written values like -(i : R) * … or (-i : ℤ) * … fail unification; restate the value with the cast visible and normalize with Int.cast_neg / mul_assoc. Critically, ← zpow_natCast does NOT rewrite a nat-exponent HPow occurrence in the goal into zpow form (the pow-with-nat and zpow-with-Int instances do not match the rewrite pattern); converting between the natural a n / x ^ n encoding and the zpow shape requires an explicit congr/convert chain. Budget this normalization as its own subtask.

109af4f8983decfd366fdf0845e002e37d36780f.hook: Sylow congruence and divisibility leave two possible counts for each of two distinct prime orders, and the branch where both counts are large must be ruled out in a finite group.
109af4f8983decfd366fdf0845e002e37d36780f.name: exclude-simultaneous-nonunique-sylow-families-by-disjoint-counting
109af4f8983decfd366fdf0845e002e37d36780f.body: Represent every nonidentity element of every Sylow subgroup as a dependent pair `Σ P : Sylow p G, {x : P // x ≠ 1}` and map it to the ambient group. Prove injectivity within one prime by putting a shared nonidentity element in the intersection: the intersection, viewed as a subgroup of a prime-cardinality Sylow subgroup, is bottom or top, and bottom contradicts nonidentity while top forces the Sylow subgroups equal. Across distinct primes, `Subgroup.inf_eq_bot_of_coprime` rules out a shared nonidentity element. `Nat.card_sigma` computes each family as the Sylow count times `p - 1`; injectivity into the ambient group then makes incompatible large-count branches an arithmetic contradiction.

c0d60233b5629a8835aa3a8cb765ec6013203df8.hook: You rewrite with if_neg/if_pos (or an Exists/forall elimination variant) and then try to swap into the side condition, and get 'goal index out of bounds'.
c0d60233b5629a8835aa3a8cb765ec6013203df8.name: conditional-rewrite-side-conditions-are-arguments-not-goals
c0d60233b5629a8835aa3a8cb765ec6013203df8.body: Conditional rewrite lemmas take their side condition as an explicit argument; the rewrite itself does not generate a swappable side goal. Restructure: state the side condition as a separate have (e.g. have hno : not (exists ...)) up front, prove it, then pass it to the rewrite as an argument. This converts a failed tactic dance into one sequenced proof step.

1c7865d708d05e6ee9b2a7c0ac01256cedd2122c.hook: A kernel has a first-order singularity at a point, but the numerator is replaced by the test function minus its value at that point.
1c7865d708d05e6ee9b2a7c0ac01256cedd2122c.name: regularize-a-first-order-singularity-with-dslope
1c7865d708d05e6ee9b2a7c0ac01256cedd2122c.body: Rewrite the regularized numerator through Mathlib's dslope: away from the base point, (f x - f a) / (x - a) is dslope f a x, while dslope supplies the derivative value at the base point. For the real kernel 1 / |x-a|, the remaining multiplier (|x-a|⁻¹ * (x-a)) has absolute value at most one. Thus continuity of dslope gives local integrability, and the mean-value bound convex_univ.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_deriv_le controls its absolute value by the global derivative supremum. This turns the singular integral into a bounded-multiplier integral with an order-one seminorm estimate.

7f409f7728751462730ea64bc9c6da765f114446.hook: when differentiating a parameter integral to all orders under the integral sign
7f409f7728751462730ea64bc9c6da765f114446.name: iterate-one-derivative-dominated-differentiation-for-parameter-integrals
7f409f7728751462730ea64bc9c6da765f114446.body: Mathlib's dominated-derivative API (of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le family) delivers exactly one derivative at a time; there is no packaged lemma lifting a local first-derivative formula to an n-times-differentiable statement. The move: state the explicit n-th derivative formula — for f(y)/(x+y), the n-th parameter derivative is (-1)^n n! times the integral of f(y)/(x+y)^(n+1) — and run an induction where each step supplies its own local domination bound and its own AEStronglyMeasurable side condition for the new integrand. Do not build a generic iteration framework; instantiate each order concretely.

45f6bde2ad128ef97df225907d1a9338c34aa6d5.hook: A holomorphic or differentiable function vanishes at a point, and the next argument needs an explicit estimate proportional to distance from that point.
45f6bde2ad128ef97df225907d1a9338c34aa6d5.name: Turn differentiability at a zero into a local linear norm bound
45f6bde2ad128ef97df225907d1a9338c34aa6d5.body: For `DifferentiableAt ℂ F 0` with `F 0 = 0`, use `hFd.isBigO_sub.bound` to obtain an eventual norm inequality. Rewrite both subtractions by the zero value, enlarge the coefficient to its absolute value with `le_abs_self`, convert the eventual neighborhood using `Metric.mem_nhds_iff`, and read off `‖F z‖ ≤ |c| * ‖z‖` on a ball. If `F z` is a power such as `g z ^ 2`, `norm_pow` converts this directly into a power-norm estimate.

e37a74e635b4fc50ace2fcffb14a9d5350cd2991.hook: Retrieve when a family of submodules is known to be independent and to span the whole module, but the goal needs one ambient basis whose vectors retain membership in their source summands.
e37a74e635b4fc50ace2fcffb14a9d5350cd2991.name: Construct an ambient basis from iSupIndep and a top supremum
e37a74e635b4fc50ace2fcffb14a9d5350cd2991.body: Choose `bp i := Module.Free.chooseBasis K (p i)`, form the external-direct-sum basis `DFinsupp.basis bp`, and map it through `h_indep.linearEquiv h_top`.
