The resulting basis is indexed by the sigma type of summand indices and local basis indices; when a prescribed finite index type is required, compare `Module.Basis.mk_eq_rank''` with the prescribed basis, turn the cardinal equality into an equivalence, and use `Module.Basis.reindex`. To recover the source-summand membership of a transported basis vector, identify the corresponding DFinsupp basis vector with `DFinsupp.single` via the basis representation, then simplify the linear equivalence. This was mined from a residual where simultaneous eigenspaces already had `iSupIndep` and supremum `top`, while the missing step was a common eigenbasis rather than another spectral theorem.

5aaad71714b0cc9f8fd2188cc2fa70b301d612f2.hook: deriv of a sliced uncurried function vs fderiv component: no lemma found — compose with a constant-identity curve
5aaad71714b0cc9f8fd2188cc2fa70b301d612f2.name: slice-fderiv-by-constant-identity-curve-composition
5aaad71714b0cc9f8fd2188cc2fa70b301d612f2.body: PATTERN (domain: formalized multivariate calculus — bridging one-dimensional deriv of a sliced function to components of fderiv): when a goal mixes deriv (fun p ↦ f (c, p)) (partial application of an uncurried f : E × F → G at a fixed first coordinate) with fderiv ℝ f (c, d) applied to a basis vector, do not search for a 'partial derivative' lemma — Mathlib has none converting deriv of a sliced uncurried C² function into an fderiv component. The move is pure composition: build the affine slice as a curve and let the chain rule do the slicing; no custom ContinuousLinearMap.proj lemma is needed. LEAF: from hf : HasFDerivAt f L (c, d), compose with the constant-identity curve γ p := (c, p), whose HasDerivAt is (hasDerivAt_const c).prodMk hasDerivAt_id giving derivative (0, 1) (HasDerivAt.prodMk, Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/Prod.lean; hasDerivAt_const / hasDerivAt_id, Deriv/Basic.lean). Then hf.comp_hasDerivAt (Analysis/Calculus/Deriv/Comp.lean) yields HasDerivAt (fun p ↦ f (c, p)) (L (0, 1)) c; for f : ℝ × ℝ → ℝ this IS the identification deriv (fun p ↦ f (c, p)) d = fderiv ℝ f (c, d) (0, 1). Dually deriv (fun q ↦ f (q, d)) c = fderiv ℝ f (c, d) (1, 0) via hasDerivAt_id.prodMk (hasDerivAt_const d). Usage discipline for HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt: the explicit point argument x comes FIRST in the signature, and when the goal displays an unapplied composition against a lambda, name the intermediate function with a named argument (l := fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ L p.1 p.2) rather than leaving a metavariable in ?l ∘ _ position. Downstream assembly of a difference/product of sliced derivatives goes through HasDerivAt.sub, HasDerivAt.mul, and HasFDerivAt.hasDerivAt.

2f7aee30eae1dfc85dcf04d7bf1000968cef22e2.hook: differentiate under the integral sign in intervalIntegral: no such lemma surfaced — it lives in ParametricIntervalIntegral
2f7aee30eae1dfc85dcf04d7bf1000968cef22e2.name: differentiate-under-interval-integral-via-parametricintervalintegral
2f7aee30eae1dfc85dcf04d7bf1000968cef22e2.body: PATTERN (domain: formalized calculus of variations / parametric integrals): when differentiating a one-parameter family of integrals ∫ t in a..b, F x t ∂μ (x the parameter, e.g. a variation y + x • η) — the 'differentiate under the integral sign' lemma DOES exist in Mathlib's intervalIntegral namespace; do not rebuild it from scratch or hunt for it only in the Bochner/MeasureTheory API. The obstacle presents as 'no such lemma surfaced in intervalIntegral', but the file is Analysis/Calculus/ParametricIntervalIntegral.lean, not the IntervalIntegral directory under MeasureTheory, so name-based search in the obvious namespace misses it. LEAF: intervalIntegral.hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le (re-exported from hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_lip and the fderiv versions in Analysis/Calculus/ParametricIntegral.lean). Given hs : s ∈ 𝓝 x₀, ae-measurability of F x near x₀, interval integrability of F x₀, ae-measurability of F' x₀ on Ι a b, a bound ∀ᵐ t ∈ Ι a b, ∀ x ∈ s, ‖F' x t‖ ≤ bound t with bound interval-integrable, and differentiability ∀ᵐ t ∈ Ι a b, ∀ x ∈ s, HasDerivAt (F · t) (F' x t) x — it returns IntervalIntegrable (F' x₀) ∧ HasDerivAt (fun x ↦ ∫ t in a..b, F x t ∂μ) (∫ t in a..b, F' x₀ t ∂μ) x₀. For a first-variation computation take x₀ = 0, s a small interval around 0, F' x t by the chain rule in the integrand's second argument; the bound comes from continuity of ∂₂F on a compact parameter window. Variant intervalIntegral.hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_lip when a Lipschitz-on-s bound is easier. Continuation note: the next step, the fundamental lemma of calculus of variations (du Bois-Reymond: ∫ f·η = 0 for all admissible η ⇒ f = 0 a.e.), is genuinely absent from Mathlib and must be built per problem, e.g. from intervalIntegral.integral_eq_zero_iff_of_le_of_nonneg_ae with η a sign/truncation witness.

84a0acde761d889a8084e5604b6a7130528650c2.hook: Needing fderiv of an uncurried R x R -> R function on a pair expressed via its partial derivatives; no Mathlib lemma evaluates fderiv on a pair via partials, and destructuring DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt with obtain fails.
84a0acde761d889a8084e5604b6a7130528650c2.name: two-variable-chain-rule-by-sections
84a0acde761d889a8084e5604b6a7130528650c2.body: DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt gives HasFDerivAt directly, not an Exists, so rcases/obtain destructuring fails. Recover l (v, w) = v * l (1, 0) + w * l (0, 1) by differentiating the two sections with hasFDerivAt_prodMk_left/right composed via comp_hasDerivAt, then map_smul/map_add linearity. This bridges deriv of sliced functions to components of fderiv on the product, which Mathlib lacks a lemma for.

89dbde9eb86c2f8733bbef0e3d1ffec68812d1d9.hook: Proving smoothness or positivity of cosh (or other hyperbolic functions) on the reals: bare contDiff_cosh fails as unknown identifier, Real.cosh_nonneg does not exist, simp [Real.cosh] loops.
89dbde9eb86c2f8733bbef0e3d1ffec68812d1d9.name: real-cosh-namespace-and-positivity
89dbde9eb86c2f8733bbef0e3d1ffec68812d1d9.body: The real versions of hyperbolic lemmas live under the Real namespace (Real.contDiff_cosh, Real.one_le_cosh); the unnamespaced contDiff_cosh is Complex-only. Real.cosh_nonneg is absent from current Mathlib; derive nonnegativity as zero_le_one.trans (Real.one_le_cosh x). simp [Real.cosh] on such goals loops on Real.cosh.eq_1 - do not unfold the definition. Two independent student attempts hit this wall from scratch before a third closed it, so it recurs across fresh sessions.

fa78da700431ced5c9f9354e582c35e368e787ef.hook: Using HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt (or similar composition lemmas) where the goal shows a curried lambda and elaboration reports metavariable application type mismatch.
fa78da700431ced5c9f9354e582c35e368e787ef.name: named-arguments-fix-comp-unification
fa78da700431ced5c9f9354e582c35e368e787ef.body: The explicit point argument comes first in the signature; supply the base point as a named argument (x := u) and pin the composed function explicitly, e.g. (l := fun p : R x R => L p.1 p.2), otherwise higher-order unification leaves ?l against the goal. Algebraic derivative lemmas such as HasDerivAt.mul produce their function in Pi.mul form, which exact rejects against the lambda form; finish with funext t; simp [Pi.mul_apply] instead of re-typing the term.
